Reviewed by Priya Nair (pnair, application_team) who confirmed the pattern. Gateway node IP 10.42.18.55 was the source for all failing requests.

Restarted affected Integration Gateway pods (igw-worker-7c4d9, igw-worker-8a2f3) so all running instances loaded the new token from the updated Kubernetes secret and cleared stale authentication state.

Validated successful authentication handshakes between the Integration Gateway (client IP 10.42.17.88) and API Service on apisvc-prod-east.corplabs.internal, and confirmed sync requests on POST /v1/sync were returning HTTP 200 responses instead of 504 errors. Verification performed by Daniel Okoye and Liang Chen.

Reviewed and updated token rotation controls for svc-reporting-sync to enforce automated renewal 72 hours before expiration via the Vault secrets engine, and added PagerDuty alerting for upcoming token expiry conditions targeting the on-call rotation for Platform Engineering (current on-call: Marcus Reeves, m.reeves@corplabs.com).

Adjusted gateway retry and exponential backoff behavior on the Integration Gateway (max retries reduced from 10 to 3, initial backoff set to 500ms with 2x multiplier, max backoff capped at 4s) to reduce cascading timeout impact during downstream latency spikes and authentication failures. Configuration change reviewed by Priya Nambiar and deployed via Helm chart update.

correspondence.message: Hi Maria — please confirm whether the API client token associated with service account svc-integ-sync was recently rotated or expired, and provide any gateway request IDs tied to the 504 errors along with the latest latency graphs from the Monitoring System dashboard. Also, can you verify whether the issue is isolated to your workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC or if other team members in the Arlington office are also affected? Please loop in Derek Owens (dowens@corplabs.com) if he has additional context from the Operations side.

We do not have confirmation of a recent token rotation for svc-integ-sync. I checked with Priya Nair (pnair, EMP-50184) on our team and she is seeing the same failures from her machine (IP 10.42.17.92). We attached the latency graphs from the Monitoring System and can see spikes during the same periods as the failed sync jobs — particularly between 18:45 and 19:10 UTC. Restarting the gateway did not stop the 504s. Derek confirmed no scheduled maintenance was in progress on the downstream API.

Review indicates the failures align more closely with downstream latency exceeding the gateway timeout than with an authentication error on svc-integ-sync. The temporary increase from 30s to 60s on gw-integ-prod-east.corplabs.internal reduced failures significantly, so timeout and retry settings were adjusted and the backlog was reprocessed. I've coordinated with Raj Patel (rpatel, infrastructure team in Arlington) to monitor the downstream service going forward. Maria and Priya should confirm sync jobs are completing normally.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics covered token validity for service account svc-integ-sync, latency correlation on gw-integ-prod-east.corplabs.internal, and possible rate-limit or retry exhaustion conditions. The strongest evidence linked failures to downstream latency exceeding the gateway's 30-second timeout, because restarts did not help and extending the timeout to 60 seconds reduced failure frequency. Authentication for svc-integ-sync remained unverified, but the incident behavior did not primarily match an auth outage. Diagnostics performed by Derek Owens (EMP-40291) and Raj Patel from the application and infrastructure teams.

root_cause: Primary cause was downstream API latency periodically exceeding the Integration Gateway request timeout window, which produced intermittent 504 errors and delayed sync processing. Token expiration could not be confirmed from the original intake, but available evidence favored timeout sensitivity to elevated downstream response times rather than an authentication failure.

steps: Validated the integration path against gateway monitoring on gw-integ-prod-east.corplabs.internal and confirmed that request latency spikes were breaching the original 30 second timeout window during affected sync periods (18:45–19:10 UTC on 2025-12-03), as reported by Maria Chen and Priya Nair.

Increased the Integration Gateway request timeout from the prior 30 second setting to 60 seconds on gw-integ-prod-east.corplabs.internal so transient downstream latency no longer caused immediate 504 failures for normal sync traffic. Change applied by Raj Patel (rpatel).

Updated retry behavior for service account svc-integ-sync to use controlled exponential backoff (initial 2s, max 32s, jitter enabled) so repeated calls during latency spikes would not rapidly exhaust retries or compound queue congestion on the us-east-1 integration path.

Cleared and reprocessed the pending retry backlog (approximately 47 queued jobs) after the timeout and retry configuration changes were applied to restore delayed synchronization jobs. Confirmed completion with Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com).

Continued post-change monitoring of gateway latency and 504 volume on gw-integ-prod-east.corplabs.internal via the Monitoring System and confirmed reduced failure frequency over the following 4-hour observation window, with guidance to escalate to downstream service owners if sustained latency again exceeds the adjusted 60-second timeout threshold. Derek Owens (EMP-40291) assigned as point of contact for any recurrence.

correspondence.message: Hi Priya — please confirm whether the downstream responses you're seeing show HTTP 429 or other 5xx status codes. Also, can you share the last successful job timing from the Data Ingestion Pipeline so we can determine whether this is a latency degradation or a rate-limit issue? You can pull the trace IDs from the Integration Gateway logs on INTGW-AKS-PROD-01 or forward them to me at r.chen@corplabs.com. — Raymond Chen

Hi Raymond, recent gateway logs from INTGW-AKS-PROD-01 show repeated 504s and the Monitoring System indicates a sharp response-time increase starting at 09:10 UTC. The affected jobs — both the nightly ingestion (job ID RPT-INGEST-0412) and the real-time sync — began failing around 09:12 UTC after previously completing normally at 06:00 UTC. I pulled traces from my session on 10.42.18.93 and they all terminate with gateway timeouts. — Priya Nair (pnair)

Gateway distributed traces from INTGW-AKS-PROD-01 confirm repeated downstream HTTP 429 responses originating from the external analytics API with sustained p99 latency exceeding 28 seconds. The Integration Gateway retry queue depth climbed from ~5 to over 140 pending requests between 09:10 and 09:25 UTC, and retries continued queueing until each request exceeded the 30-second gateway timeout threshold. This explains the failed integration jobs and delayed syncs reported by Priya and the broader Austin Data Integration team. Escalating to the downstream API owner for quota review. — Raymond Chen

Priya Nair (pnair) confirmed data sync restored on her workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN.

Updated the Integration Gateway retry and backoff policy for the reporting integration path on INTGW-AKS-PROD-01 and added Monitoring System alerting thresholds for 429 spike detection (>20 per 5-min window) and downstream latency growth (p95 >5s) to detect recurrence earlier. Alert recipients set to mdelgado@corplabs.com and rchen@corplabs.com.

correspondence.message: We are seeing both 504 timeout spikes at the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east-01) and some 401 responses in client traces originating from 10.42.18.77. Can you confirm whether failures started after the 4.7.2-rc3 deploy at 03:45 UTC and whether all batches are affected or only a subset of integrations? We'd also like to know if the service account svc-batch-integ credentials were refreshed as part of the deployment. — Priya Nair, Application Support

The failures started shortly after the deploy, around 04:00 UTC. Not every batch is failing, but enough are timing out that downstream deliveries are delayed — specifically the order sync and inventory reconciliation jobs. A few client retries from my workstation WORKSTATION-BATCH-ME also reported unauthorized errors. I checked with Darren Cho (dcho, emp ID E-40291) on the platform team and he confirmed no infrastructure changes were made on their side during that window. — Marcus Ellison

Review of gateway logs on igw-prod-east-01 and Monitoring System dashboards shows the main failure pattern is 504 timeouts aligned with downstream Order Fulfillment API latency increases (p99 response time spiking from ~200ms to >12s). Token-related 401s are present but intermittent — affecting roughly 15% of requests from svc-batch-integ. We rotated the token credential for svc-batch-integ and adjusted retry/backoff configuration on the gateway while escalating the latency issue to the downstream service team. Darren Cho confirmed the Kubernetes pod igw-worker-7b4c was also accumulating a request backlog. — Priya Nair

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics covered token validity for service account svc-batch-integ, downstream Order Fulfillment API latency correlation, and possible rate limiting on igw-prod-east-01. The strongest signal was a downstream latency spike (p99 jumping from ~200ms to >12s) that matched the 504 timeout pattern and failure window after the 4.7.2-rc3 deploy at 03:45 UTC. Intermittent 401 responses on approximately 15% of calls confirmed a secondary token issue for svc-batch-integ, which was remediated by rotating the credential, but the incident impact was primarily driven by latency. Rate limiting (429 responses) was reviewed and remained a non-primary or inconclusive factor, with only sporadic occurrences logged.

steps.evidence: No clear dominant rate-limit pattern was established from the reviewed gateway logs. The 429 responses appeared sporadically and did not cluster around the peak failure window, suggesting they were incidental rather than causal.

root_cause: Primary cause was elevated downstream service latency causing the Integration Gateway to exceed its timeout window and return intermittent 504 responses after the deploy. A secondary expired or stale API token condition was also present on some client calls, producing intermittent 401 errors, but this was not the dominant driver of the batch failure spike.

steps: Validated the failure window (04:00–07:00 UTC) against Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east-01) and downstream Order Fulfillment API latency metrics in the Monitoring System to confirm the timeout pattern was primarily latency-driven (p99 >12s vs. 5s gateway timeout) rather than a full authentication outage.

Rotated the integration API token for service account svc-batch-integ to remove the intermittent expired or stale credential condition seen in client traces from 10.42.18.77 (WORKSTATION-BATCH-ME), and updated the credential in the gateway's secret store.

Increased Integration Gateway retry count from 2 to 4 and adjusted exponential backoff settings (initial delay from 500ms to 1500ms, max delay from 3s to 10s) on igw-prod-east-01 so transient downstream latency spikes would not immediately fail scheduled batch requests.

Cleared the gateway request queue (approximately 180 backed-up requests) and restarted the affected gateway pod igw-worker-7b4c to remove backed-up requests created during the latency spike. Darren Cho from the platform team confirmed pod health post-restart.

Escalated the downstream latency condition to the Downstream Service Team (contact: Raj Patel, rpatel@corplabs.com) with aligned gateway logs from igw-prod-east-01 and Monitoring System performance evidence for service-side remediation, while keeping monitoring alerts in place to verify timeout reduction after the gateway changes. Follow-up review scheduled for 2025-12-05.

correspondence.message: Review of integration logs on ig-prod-worker-07 by Rachel Nguyen (rng0042) shows repeated 401 token_expired entries for service account svc-ig-sync starting at 23:50 UTC, followed by cascading 504 Gateway Timeout responses from the downstream API Service endpoint https://api.corplabs.internal/v2/ingest during the nightly sync window. The pattern suggests the gateway credential bound to svc-ig-sync expired at or before the scheduled job kickoff, and subsequent retries backed up in the integration queue. Monitoring System alert ALERT-IG-4781 was triggered at 23:53 UTC and routed to the on-call engineer at ext. 4-7823.

Restarted the Integration Gateway pod ig-prod-worker-07 from host WORKSTATION-RNGN and temporarily increased the request timeout from 30s to 60s on the /v2/ingest route to rule out a transient connectivity issue. Authentication refresh attempts against the token endpoint continued to fail with 401 token_expired for svc-ig-sync. Confirmed with Marcus Delgado that no upstream credential rotation had been performed recently. The pod restart did not resolve the issue; all outbound calls still returned 401 prior to any downstream processing.

Confirmed the configured API token for svc-ig-sync on the Integration Gateway had expired as of 2025-12-03T00:00:00Z — 24 hours before the incident window. Rachel Nguyen rotated the credential via the API Service admin console, redeployed the secret to the ig-prod-worker-07 pod, and validated that token refresh succeeded. Downstream calls to https://api.corplabs.internal/v2/ingest began completing normally within 3 minutes of the rotation. Marcus Delgado (emp ID E-50821) confirmed data freshness was restored for the finance consumers by 00:32 UTC.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics linked the delayed nightly syncs to authentication failure on the Integration Gateway pod ig-prod-worker-07 in us-east-1. The primary failure was an expired API token for service account svc-ig-sync that prevented successful token refresh against the API Service, producing 401 token_expired responses beginning at 23:50 UTC. During the same window, requests to https://api.corplabs.internal/v2/ingest also experienced elevated latency and 504 timeouts, which compounded queue growth and caused 14 integration jobs to fail. A rate-limit condition was checked against gateway and Monitoring System logs and was not supported by the available evidence. Investigation performed by Rachel Nguyen (rng0042) with confirmation from Marcus Delgado.

root_cause: Expired API credential on the Integration Gateway caused token refresh failures, leading to 401 token_expired responses and subsequent downstream call timeouts during the nightly sync window.

steps: Rotated the expired API token for service account svc-ig-sync configured on the Integration Gateway pod ig-prod-worker-07 and confirmed the gateway could successfully authenticate to the downstream API Service at https://api.corplabs.internal/v2/ingest. Rotation performed by Rachel Nguyen (rng0042) at approximately 00:18 UTC.

Validated that token refresh operations for svc-ig-sync completed successfully after the credential update by reviewing gateway logs on ig-prod-worker-07 and confirming that new API requests no longer returned 401 token_expired errors.

Cleared and reprocessed 14 affected integration queue items so delayed nightly sync jobs could resume with valid authentication; Marcus Delgado (E-50821) confirmed data freshness was restored for downstream finance and analytics consumers by 00:32 UTC.

Updated the token_refresh_policy for svc-ig-sync to enforce automated renewal checks 7 days before credential expiry and configured a Monitoring System alert to notify the Dallas application support team (appsupp-dallas@corplabs.com) before credential expiration to prevent recurrence.

Adjusted the integration retry and backoff configuration on ig-prod-worker-07 from a fixed 5s interval to exponential backoff (initial 2s, max 120s, jitter enabled) to better tolerate transient downstream latency without exhausting jobs during the nightly sync window.

Monitored logs and Monitoring System metrics for 24 hours after remediation to confirm normal API latency on the /v2/ingest endpoint, successful sync completion for all scheduled jobs, and no further 401 or 504 spikes. Rachel Nguyen signed off on the 24-hour observation at 2025-12-05T13:00:00Z.

Specifically, the integration service account svc-orderproc was failing token refresh calls against the API Service endpoint every 30 seconds, generating persistent 401 Unauthorized responses. I correlated these with the 504 spikes visible in the Monitoring System dashboard. The gateway pods on node ip-10-0-3-214 were cycling through retry loops, exhausting connection pools and producing the cascading timeouts reported by mdelgado and pnair.

Rotated the integration API token for service account svc-orderproc and restarted gateway pods to load the updated secret; authenticated requests are succeeding again and error rates are returning to baseline. Confirmed with Marcus Delgado and Priya Nair that their scheduled sync jobs are now completing successfully. Monitoring System alerts for the us-east-1 Integration Gateway have cleared as of 04:47 UTC.

correspondence.message: API calls to the Integration Gateway (gw-prod-east.corpsync.internal) began timing out with recurring 504 errors during the nightly customer sync window starting at 03:00 UTC. Multiple integration jobs failed — specifically job IDs SYNC-20251210-0301 through SYNC-20251210-0318 — while gateway response time increased from a baseline of ~220ms to over 4,200ms. I'm Marcus Delgado from the Application Support team in Arlington; the alert was forwarded to me by our on-call engineer Priya Nair (pnair). Monitoring System traces from host WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD show the failures correlating with downstream Order Fulfillment API latency spikes. Client IP 10.42.17.88 was among the affected callers.

We rotated the API token for service account svc-custsync (emp_id E-40291, token last issued 2025-10-03), verified client credentials against the Integration Gateway auth provider, and cleared the gateway cache on gw-prod-east.corpsync.internal. Authentication errors dropped from ~38/min to near zero after the rotation. However, intermittent 504 timeouts continued at a rate of approximately 12–15/min, indicating a separate underlying issue. I coordinated with Priya Nair and escalation lead Tom Hargrove (thargrove) to begin downstream latency analysis. Retry logs from host WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD confirmed the gateway was still failing on calls routed to api-orders.corpsync.internal.

Correlation of gateway failures on gw-prod-east.corpsync.internal with elevated downstream API latency on api-orders.corpsync.internal indicates the remaining issue is service-side performance during the sync window. Distributed traces show request durations exceeding 6.8s against a 2s gateway timeout threshold. Logs, traces, and timing correlation have been packaged and provided to the downstream Order Fulfillment service team (contact: Raj Mehta, rmehta@corplabs.com, ext. 4782) for investigation. Tom Hargrove (thargrove, E-50134) is tracking the escalation from the Denver operations center.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics covered token validity for service account svc-custsync, gateway-to-downstream latency correlation on gw-prod-east.corpsync.internal → api-orders.corpsync.internal, and possible rate-limit behavior. The token problem was partially validated because rotation reduced authentication errors from ~38/min to near zero, but the dominant failure pattern remained 504 timeouts tied to downstream API latency (p95 > 4.2s, peak 6.8s) during the nightly sync window (03:00–04:30 UTC). This supports downstream performance degradation as the root cause, with the expired token on svc-custsync as a secondary contributing factor. Diagnostics were performed by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) and escalation lead Tom Hargrove (thargrove).

correspondence.message: Reviewed gateway logs on igw-east-node04 and Monitoring System dashboards; repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses and a clear downstream latency spike are present from roughly 03:10 to 03:30 UTC, matching the failed jobs and retry exhaustion. Jobs sync-batch-1211-A through sync-batch-1211-F are all showing timeout or partial-failure status.

We rotated the API token (client_id: igw-sync-prod-01) and restarted the gateway pods in the igw-prod namespace on EKS. Authentication retry noise decreased — auth error rate dropped from ~12% to <1% within 5 minutes of rotation — but intermittent 504 timeouts continued at roughly the same frequency (~35 per minute), so the issue does not appear to be primarily credential-related. Engineer Priya Nair (pnair, emp ID E-30587) performed the rotation and pod restart from host WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN at 10.42.22.134. We also confirmed the new token is valid via a manual curl test against the downstream /v2/healthz endpoint, which returned 200 but with a 4.8s response time.

Evidence was escalated to the downstream API Service owners — team lead Raj Venkatesh (rvenkatesh@corplabs.com) in the Dallas office — for sustained latency investigation, including review of recent deployments (deploy api-svc-v3.14.2 rolled out 2025-12-11T10:30Z), scaling behavior on the api-svc-prod node group, and service health during the impacted sync window from 11:15–13:25 UTC. Escalation filed by Carlos Medina (cmedina, emp ID E-22814) with full Monitoring System trace exports and gateway request logs attached.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics ruled out expired or invalid credentials as the main cause because token rotation (performed by Priya Nair at 13:05 UTC) lowered auth retry noise without removing the incident. Correlation of failed sync jobs (sync-batch-1211-A through -F) with repeated HTTP 504 responses and downstream response times averaging 6.2s — well above the gateway's 5s timeout window — pointed to API Service latency as the primary root cause. Rate limiting was not confirmed in gateway logs or Monitoring System dashboards, so the issue was resolved as a downstream service latency incident with mitigation applied on the gateway side and ownership handed to the downstream team led by Raj Venkatesh in Dallas.

Subsequent monitoring from INTGW-PROD-04 showed recovery of request latency (p99 dropped from ~48s to ~1.2s) and sync success rate returned to 100%. Marcus Delgado confirmed billing data freshness restored in the Charlotte operations dashboard.

Endpoint and load balancer checks show the certificate presented for internal.web.internal expired on 2025-12-13, and the renewed certificate chain is not installed on the load balancer. Specifically, openssl s_client connections to LB-PROD-F5-01 (10.200.1.15) returned a leaf certificate with notAfter of Dec 13 00:00:00 2025 GMT, serial 4A:7C:3E:91. The renewed certificate (serial 8B:12:D4:F7) was located in the internal CA vault but had never been deployed. Network engineer Raj Patel (rpatel, EMP-55034) confirmed the chain bundle on the load balancer still referenced the old intermediate CA cert issued 2023-12-13.

Renewed certificate and full intermediate chain were deployed to the production load balancer, the TLS listener was reloaded, and follow-up validation shows successful handshakes from internal clients. Deployment was performed by Raj Patel (rpatel) at 11:42 UTC. Post-deployment verification from client IPs 10.42.17.88 (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC) and 10.42.22.61 confirmed the new leaf certificate (serial 8B:12:D4:F7, valid until 2026-12-13) and complete intermediate chain are now being served. correspondence.message: Hi Maria — we are checking whether the certificate issue is on the service itself or on the internal load balancer path (lb-web-east.corplabs.internal). Could you confirm whether users are seeing browser certificate warnings when navigating to https://appportal.corplabs.internal, and whether the failure occurs only when accessing through the load balancer? Also, please let us know if direct access to the backend on port 8443 shows the same warning. I've looped in Raj Patel from the network team for the load balancer side. — Kevin Marsh, Infrastructure Support

Hi Kevin — yes, users across the Austin and Raleigh offices report certificate warnings in the browser (NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) and the TLS failure is happening through the internal load balancer endpoint lb-web-east.corplabs.internal. I tested from my workstation WORKSTATION-MC-4417 at 10.22.45.88 and confirmed the same error. Restarting the service did not clear the warning. Direct backend access on port 8443 also shows an expired cert, so the renewed cert doesn't seem to have propagated anywhere. — Maria Chen (emp ID: E-50921)

Confirmed via openssl s_client that lb-web-east.corplabs.internal is still presenting an expired certificate (serial 4A:7C:03:EE, expired 2025-12-13T23:59:59Z) and the updated chain was not applied there. Raj Patel verified the renewed certificate bundle was generated by the internal CA on 2025-12-10 but never deployed. We also found no active near-expiration alert for this certificate in the monitoring platform, which explains why renewal deployment was missed before the outage. Assigning remediation to myself and Raj. — Kevin Marsh

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the outage was caused by an expired certificate (CN=appportal.corplabs.internal, serial 4A:7C:03:EE, expired 2025-12-13) being presented through the internal load balancer lb-web-east.corplabs.internal, with an outdated or unapplied certificate chain on the load balancer path. Initial restarts and certificate-store reload attempts by Kevin Marsh did not resolve the issue because the presented certificate chain remained unchanged on both the backend and the load balancer. Review also found missing near-expiration alerting in the certificate monitoring system, which allowed the certificate to lapse without preventive action. Affected users spanned the Austin and Raleigh offices.

correspondence.message: Can you confirm whether users are seeing browser certificate warnings (e.g., ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) versus a generic application error, and whether API clients are failing during TLS handshake or after connection establishment? Also, could you verify whether the issue is isolated to a specific zone or affects all zones behind lb-prod-central-01.infra.example.corp? Please share any screenshots or client-side error output if available. — Marcus Delgado, Infrastructure Operations

Users report certificate date warnings in the browser, and API consumers are failing during TLS negotiation rather than after login or page load. The problem is affecting multiple zones for internal.example.corp. I checked from my machine (WORKSTATION-DESK-RK, IP 10.42.17.88) in the Denver office and got the same ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID. Our colleague Tomás Reyes on the API integrations team (treyes@example.corp) also confirmed that their automated service client on 10.42.22.105 is getting TLS handshake failures when calling the /api/v2/health endpoint. This is blocking several downstream pipelines.

Confirmed the certificate for internal.example.corp (serial 4A:7C:91:D3:00:EF:28:B1) expired on 2025-12-14T08:00:00Z and the load balancer lb-prod-central-01.infra.example.corp is still serving the old chain including the expired leaf cert. openssl s_client output from 10.42.17.88 shows 'verify error:num=10:certificate has expired'. This matches the ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID and TLS handshake failures seen in monitoring dashboards. Engaging the Certificate Authority team and network_team lead Jenna Whitfield (jwhitfield) to begin remediation.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed a certificate-expiration outage rather than an application or generic load balancer fault. The endpoint certificate for internal.example.corp (serial 4A:7C:91:D3:00:EF:28:B1) had expired at 08:00 UTC on 2025-12-14, the load balancer lb-prod-central-01.infra.example.corp was still serving an outdated chain, and renewal monitoring in the Certificate Management platform was not active for this SAN entry. These combined conditions caused browser certificate warnings and TLS handshake failures across all three us-central-1 availability zones until the renewed certificate and full chain were deployed. Investigation led by Marcus Delgado (E-40821) with support from network_team lead Jenna Whitfield.

root_cause: The TLS certificate for internal.example.corp expired, and the load balancer continued serving a stale certificate chain. Certificate renewal alerting was not active, so the expiration was not detected and remediated before client TLS validation began failing.

steps: Issued a new TLS certificate for internal.example.corp (new serial 7B:22:AF:01:CC:D4:90:E3, valid until 2026-12-14) through the Certificate Authority, requested by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, E-40821), before restoring production traffic handling.

Restored certificate renewal alerting in the Certificate Management platform for internal.example.corp with a 30-day and 7-day pre-expiry notification threshold, subscribed to mdelgado@example.corp and infra-ops@example.corp, and added recurring certificate health checks so future expirations are detected before the renewal window closes.

correspondence.message: We confirmed the certificate for CN=internal-web.corplabs.com was renewed at the CA by rgarcia (emp ID E-40291) yesterday at 14:22 UTC. Please verify whether the full certificate chain — including the updated DigiCert intermediate — was also uploaded to the HAProxy load balancer (LB-FRONT-01) and whether all frontend endpoints were reloaded. I can see from the ticket history that the initial deployment was done from workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RG at 10.28.44.73.

The cert renewal was completed yesterday by Ricardo, but it looks like only the renewed leaf cert was deployed to HAProxy — the intermediate bundle wasn't included. I checked from my machine (WORKSTATION-PC-MC, IP 10.28.51.19) and some endpoints still show warnings. Health checks from the Kubernetes pods are also failing TLS. I've looped in James Whitfield (jwhitfield) from the network team to assist with the LB config.

Chain validation on LB-FRONT-01 confirms the intermediate bundle (DigiCert SHA2 Extended Validation Server CA) was missing from the HAProxy frontend bind directive for internal-web.corplabs.com. The leaf cert was valid (expires 2026-12-14) but clients couldn't build the full trust path. Deploying the complete chain bundle and issuing a graceful reload of HAProxy worker processes should clear the certificate warnings and handshake failures. James Whitfield is preparing the corrected PEM bundle now.

Endpoint validation from client IP 10.28.51.19 showed TLS errors and certificate warnings on https://internal-web.corplabs.com, chain inspection on LB-FRONT-01 identified the missing updated intermediate CA bundle in the HAProxy frontend configuration, and monitoring review found a gap in the Nagios certificate check where renewal completion was tracked but chain deployment validation on the load balancer was not covered.

steps.evidence: Root cause notes from the application team indicate Nagios certificate monitoring (check_ssl_cert plugin) only validated leaf certificate expiry and did not detect missing chain deployment after renewal. Alert rule cert_renewal_complete lacked a chain-validation post-condition.

root_cause: The TLS certificate was renewed at the Certificate Authority, but the full certificate chain was not deployed to the HAProxy load balancer serving the Internal Web Service. As a result, some clients continued to receive an expired or incomplete chain, and existing renewal monitoring did not detect the missing chain deployment step, allowing the outage to recur after the first remediation attempt.

steps: Renew the Internal Web Service TLS certificate (CN=internal-web.corplabs.com) with the internal Certificate Authority and retrieve the complete server certificate and intermediate certificate chain (DigiCert SHA2 Extended Validation Server CA). Validate the presented certificate, expiration (2026-12-14), SAN coverage (internal-web.corplabs.com, api.internal.corplabs.com), and full trust chain from internal client perspectives (tested from 10.28.51.19 by mchen and 10.28.44.73 by rgarcia) to confirm successful TLS handshakes with no warnings.

correspondence.message: Users and automated monitors are receiving TLS/SSL warnings for internal-service.example.corp, and the load balancer (LB-PROD-EAST-02) health checks are failing TLS handshakes. I'm Maria Gonzalez (EMP-40821) from the Chicago office — I first noticed the issue around 08:47 UTC when my browser on WORKSTATION-PC-MG (IP 10.22.14.87) threw ERR_SSL_CERT_EXPIRED. Network engineer Priya Nair (pnair) verified the chain mismatch via openssl s_client output from 10.22.14.87 and the load balancer management console. The deployment automation job (cert-deploy-east-prod) last ran successfully on 2024-12-14 but did not execute for this renewal cycle.

Endpoint checks from client IP 10.22.14.87 showed the certificate for internal-service.example.corp expired on 2025-12-15, chain validation confirmed the renewed certificate (issued 2025-12-14 by CA-INT-EAST-01) had not been deployed, and monitoring review by rchen showed the renewal alert did not fire prior to expiration. correspondence.message: Users accessing service.example.internal are getting certificate expired warnings, and the internal health checks against the HTTPS endpoint are failing with TLS errors. I'm Rachel Nguyen from the application support team (rnguyen@corplabs.com). At least five users in Denver have reported the issue this morning, including Marco Pellegrini who was unable to complete his workflow. My workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN at 10.42.17.88 also reproduces the error consistently. The health-check service running on internal-health-check is returning TLS_ERROR for every probe cycle since approximately 09:12 UTC.

Reviewed the certificate presented by load balancer LB-PROD-INT-02 and confirmed it expired on 2025-12-21 (Not After: 2025-12-21T00:00:00Z). The endpoint is still serving the old chain with serial 4A:7C:3E:91:BB:02, which explains the TLS handshake failures. Ran openssl s_client against service.example.internal:443 from diagnostics host 10.42.1.15 and verified the leaf certificate CN and SAN entries match the service name but the validity period has lapsed. Assigning to Derek Castillo (dcastillo, Infrastructure Support) for certificate renewal and chain redeployment.

CA renewal history on the CorpLabs Internal CA shows no recent successful renewal run for CN=service.example.internal — the last recorded issuance was 2024-12-21. Certificate monitoring in the alerting platform had the renewal threshold check disabled since a configuration change on 2025-11-03, so no pre-expiry warning was generated. Infrastructure Support (Derek Castillo, ext. 4455, dcastillo@corplabs.com) was engaged to renew the certificate via the internal CA portal and update the load balancer LB-PROD-INT-02 configuration with the new certificate and chain files.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed a certificate-expiration outage at load balancer LB-PROD-INT-02 serving service.example.internal in the Denver data center. The endpoint leaf certificate (serial 4A:7C:3E:91:BB:02) had expired at 2025-12-21T00:00:00Z, the deployed intermediate chain on the load balancer was not updated, and certificate renewal monitoring had been inadvertently disabled since 2025-11-03, failing to warn before expiration. Service was restored after Derek Castillo renewed the certificate via the CorpLabs Internal CA, deployed the full chain to LB-PROD-INT-02, and reloaded the listener configuration.

correspondence.message: Initial validation by on-call engineer Marcus Ellison shows the Internal Web Service endpoint (internalweb.corplabs.internal) is presenting an expired TLS certificate — the leaf cert serial 4A:9C:03:FF expired at 2025-12-22T00:00:00Z. This matches the ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID health check failures observed from monitoring host MON-CENTRAL-01. Curl tests from workstation WORKSTATION-DELL-ME also reproduce the handshake failure. Escalating to the certificate management team for immediate renewal.

The service certificate was renewed via the internal Certificate Authority by Priya Nagarajan (emp ID: E-40821) and redeployed to the Internal Web Service endpoint at 04:22 UTC. However, follow-up validation from client IP 10.42.17.85 and monitoring probes still shows certificate warnings on some client paths routed through LB-CENTRAL-02.corplabs.internal, indicating the full chain is not yet correct on the load balancer. Engaging the network team for load balancer certificate chain update.

Further testing by network engineer David Kowalski identified that Load Balancer LB-CENTRAL-02.corplabs.internal was still serving an outdated intermediate certificate chain (issued by CorpLabs Intermediate CA G2, which itself expired 2025-12-21). David updated the LB chain configuration with the current intermediates and reloaded the TLS listener at 05:18 UTC. Priya Nagarajan also restored the certificate expiry alerting rule in the monitoring platform (threshold set to 30/14/7 days before expiry). End-to-end TLS validation from WORKSTATION-THINKPAD-DK and automated probes now confirms all certificate warnings and handshake failures are cleared.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the Internal Web Service endpoint (internalweb.corplabs.internal) was serving an expired TLS certificate (serial 4A:9C:03:FF, expired 2025-12-22T00:00:00Z), causing ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID and TLS handshake failures for all clients. A subsequent check by the network team showed the initial renewal deployed by Priya Nagarajan did not fully resolve the issue because Load Balancer LB-CENTRAL-02.corplabs.internal certificate chain was still presenting the expired CorpLabs Intermediate CA G2 certificate. Review of monitoring by the application team found certificate renewal alerting was not effectively in place before expiry — the scheduled alert job had been inadvertently disabled during a monitoring platform migration in November, allowing the outage to occur without advance warning.

correspondence.message: Agent Raj Patel (rpatel, EMP-40821) confirmed that LB-01 is presenting an expired certificate for internal-websvc.example.corp. Raj Patel also confirmed via F5 iControl REST API that the SSL profile 'clientssl-internal-websvc' still references the old certificate object (cert_internal-websvc_2024.crt). Escalating to certificate operations.

However, the updated full certificate chain was not deployed to LB-01. Investigation by Diana Torres (dtorres, EMP-55193) found that the renewal alerting rule in internal-monitoring had been inadvertently disabled during a maintenance window on 2025-12-10, so no 30-day or 7-day expiration warnings were sent to the cert-ops-alerts@example.corp distribution list.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the outage was caused by an expired TLS certificate actively presented by LB-01 (management IP 10.200.5.11) for internal-websvc.example.corp. This aligned with user browser warnings (NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) and monitoring TLS handshake failures observed from the Arlington office and remote VPN clients.

correspondence.message: Automated monitoring detected that the certificate presented by internal-web.internal.example.com expired, and the internal load balancer (lb-internal-01.infra.example.com) began returning TLS handshake failures with 502/523 responses. Initial alert was correlated with failed health probes from client IP 10.42.16.88 (WORKSTATION-DEVOPS-MC) belonging to user mchen. Monitoring node cert-watch-central flagged the expiry at 03:12 UTC.

Validation against the load balancer confirmed the endpoint was serving an expired certificate and outdated chain, matching the certificate warnings reported by clients. Network engineer Raj Patel (rpatel, EMP-55193) from the Austin office inspected the lb-internal-01 configuration and confirmed the certificate bundle referenced serial 4A:3F:9C:01 which had a notAfter of 2025-12-22T23:59:59Z. OpenSSL s_client verification from 10.50.3.22 returned verify error:num=10:certificate has expired.

Renewed the certificate with the internal CA (ca-root-01.infra.example.com), deployed the replacement certificate and full chain to lb-internal-01, reloaded affected services, and confirmed successful TLS health checks. Deployment was performed by Raj Patel (rpatel) and verified by Maria Chen from WORKSTATION-DEVOPS-MC. Post-deployment curl tests from 10.42.16.88 and 10.50.3.22 returned HTTP 200 with valid certificate chain.

correspondence.message: Users report that https://internal-api.local shows certificate warnings and our CI tests now fail TLS handshakes, so the internal API is unreachable over HTTPS. Maria Chen (emp ID E-40821) first flagged the issue at 08:52 UTC from her workstation at 10.24.16.88. Additional reports came in from Raj Patel on the QA team confirming the same NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID error when accessing the endpoint from the Ashburn office.

Initial check by agent dmorris shows the certificate presented by internal-api.local expired on 2025-12-23T00:00:00Z. Running openssl s_client -connect internal-api.local:443 confirmed the leaf certificate serial 3A:F2:9C:01 has a notAfter of Dec 23 00:00:00 2025 GMT. Investigating whether LB-EAST-01.corplabs.internal is still serving an old certificate or incomplete chain. The Certificate Authority portal shows a renewal request was never submitted, consistent with missing monitoring alerts.

A renewed certificate (serial 7B:D4:11:A8) has been obtained from the internal Certificate Authority by dmorris, and the next corrective action is to update the load balancer SSL profile on LB-EAST-01.corplabs.internal with the new full chain because the current endpoint is still presenting the old expired chain. Raj Patel has confirmed from the QA environment at 10.24.17.42 that the old certificate is still being served as of 09:14 UTC.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed a certificate expiration incident rather than a general service outage. The service endpoint certificate for internal-api.local (CN=internal-api.local, issued by CorpLabs Internal CA) was expired as of 2025-12-23T00:00:00Z. LB-EAST-01.corplabs.internal was still presenting the old certificate chain including the expired leaf, and certificate renewal monitoring in the cert-manager dashboard had not been configured for this endpoint, which prevented proactive remediation. These findings explain the browser warnings reported by mchen, CI TLS handshake failures from the build agents, and integration impact across the Ashburn environment.

correspondence.message: Users are getting certificate warnings (ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) when opening internal-web-service at https://appportal.corp.internal, and some API clients cannot complete the TLS handshake through the Load Balancer LB-EAST-01.corp.internal. I first noticed the issue from my workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC when trying to access the portal around 14:30 UTC. My IP is 10.22.47.88. Other team members including Raj Patel (rpatel, emp ID E-20487) in the Austin office have confirmed the same behavior.

Checks against the service endpoint https://appportal.corp.internal show the Load Balancer LB-EAST-01.corp.internal is presenting an expired certificate with Subject CN=appportal.corp.internal, serial 4A:3F:9C:01:BB:72, notAfter 2025-12-23T00:00:00Z. The intermediate certificate (issued by CorpLabs Internal CA G2) is not included in the served chain. Verified by running openssl s_client -connect appportal.corp.internal:443 -servername appportal.corp.internal from diagnostics host. Assigning to Kevin Oduya (koduya) on the infrastructure team for certificate renewal and chain remediation.

Escalated to the Certificate Authority and Load Balancer owners — specifically to the cert-ops group lead Sandra Liu (sliu, ext. 4127, sliu@corp.internal) — to renew the certificate for CN=appportal.corp.internal, deploy the full chain on LB-EAST-01.corp.internal, and restore expiration monitoring in the certificate dashboard with high priority. Target resolution within the Gold SLA window.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the outage was caused at the Load Balancer (LB-EAST-01.corp.internal) TLS termination layer rather than the application itself. The presented end-entity certificate (CN=appportal.corp.internal, serial 4A:3F:9C:01:BB:72) had expired at 2025-12-23T00:00:00Z, and the intermediate certificate (CorpLabs Internal CA G2) was not being served, producing ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID in browsers and TLS handshake failures for automated clients connecting from the Denver and Austin offices. Monitoring and renewal controls also require correction because the expiration was not prevented before service impact. Investigation performed by koduya (Infrastructure) and the security_team.

correspondence.message: Users are getting browser certificate warnings on the internal API and several integrations are failing with ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID; curl also shows TLS handshake failure. Maria Chen (mchen) first reported the issue from her workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC at 10.42.18.97, and we've since received similar reports from James Whitfield and others in the Portland and Denver offices.

The endpoint certificate for api.internal.corplabs.com expired at 2025-12-24 04:00 UTC, and the load balancer is still presenting the previous certificate chain, which explains the TLS validation failures. I verified by running openssl s_client against the VIP at 10.200.5.12 and confirmed the leaf certificate CN=api.internal.corplabs.com had a notAfter of Dec 24 04:00:00 2025 GMT. The certificate was originally issued by our internal CA (ca-root-01.corplabs.internal) and the intermediate chain had not been rotated either.

A TLS reload alone did not resolve the issue, so a renewed certificate is being deployed with the corrected chain and the certificate monitoring alert is being restored. Network engineer Raj Patel (rpatel) is handling the certificate replacement on lb-prod-01 and updating the chain bundle. I'm also coordinating with Lisa Novak (lnovak) from the monitoring team to restore the Nagios certificate expiry check that was inadvertently disabled during last month's maintenance window.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the service outage was caused by an expired endpoint certificate (serial 4A:3F:C8:91:DE) and a stale certificate chain still being served by the HAProxy load balancer lb-internal-01 in us-east-1. Review of the certificate lifecycle controls in the Certificate Management Service also identified missing renewal alerting for the internal.service.example.com endpoint, which allowed the certificate to expire without remediation. Users mdelgado and lkowalski independently confirmed the client-side TLS failures.

correspondence.message: Users across several internal networks including Arlington and Raleigh are getting certificate warnings and cannot open the internal web service over HTTPS; the load balancer is also showing elevated 525/SSL failures. Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) reported the issue first from her workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC at IP 10.42.17.88, and several other developers in the internal-devs group have confirmed the same behavior.

Checked the certificate presented on the service endpoint (internal-web.corplabs.com) and confirmed it expired on 2025-12-25. The symptoms match the browser ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID errors and failed TLS handshakes. I ran openssl s_client against the endpoint from host WORKSTATION-DESK-DO (IP 10.42.18.52) and verified the leaf certificate serial 4A:3F:9C:01 shows notAfter=Dec 25 00:00:00 2025 GMT. The intermediate certificate in the chain was also outdated. Assigning to Derek Owens (dowens) for remediation.

Renewed the certificate with the internal CA (ca-root.corplabs.internal) for CN=internal-web.corplabs.com, updated the full certificate chain on the load balancer LB-EAST-PROD-01, restarted the SSL profile, and verified successful TLS handshakes to the internal web service. Confirmation received from Maria Chen and two other users in the Charlotte office that HTTPS access is restored. Post-fix monitoring alert was re-enabled by Priya Nair (pnair).

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the HTTPS endpoint (internal-web.corplabs.com) was presenting an expired TLS certificate, which matched user-visible certificate warnings and load balancer SSL 525 errors on LB-EAST-PROD-01. Additional validation showed the renewed certificate chain was not fully updated on the load balancer until remediation was completed. Review of monitoring indicated renewal alerting did not prevent the certificate from expiring, so monitoring was restored and strengthened after recovery. Diagnostics performed by Derek Owens (dowens, E-40291) and validated by Priya Nair (pnair).

Renew or reissue the TLS certificate through the internal Certificate Authority for CN=internal-web-svc.corplabs.internal and obtain the correct full certificate chain including required intermediate certificates (CorpLabs Internal Intermediate CA G2). New certificate serial: 7D:01:AF:E8:22:C5, valid through 2026-12-25.

Replace the expired certificate and update the full chain in the load balancer configuration on LB-CENTRAL-02 for the internal-web-svc endpoint. Performed by Ryan Jensen (rjensen) on the network team.

Perform a rolling restart or reload of load balancer LB-CENTRAL-02 across all us-central-1 nodes so the new certificate bundle is actively served on all nodes. Restart completed at 2025-12-25T08:06:00Z.

Validate successful TLS handshakes from internal clients (WORKSTATION-MC-7241, WORKSTATION-RJ-3390) and browsers, confirm certificate date warnings are cleared, and verify certificate-monitoring alerts and renewal checks are active. correspondence.message: Hi Rachel — we can see your device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (Intune Object ID 7a3e91bf-c4d2-4f08-b6a1-2d5e8f3c09ab) is marked Noncompliant in Intune. The compliance record shows the encryption signal as the failing requirement. Could you please confirm whether Company Portal on your end also surfaces an encryption-related compliance issue, and whether the device has been online and connected to the corporate network recently? I've also looped in our endpoint team lead, Derek Holloway (dholloway@corplabs.com), in case we need a policy-side review.

Yes, Company Portal shows the device as Noncompliant with a message about encryption not being detected, and I cannot access Exchange Online — I get a 'Your device is not compliant' block page when I try to sign in at https://outlook.office365.com. The laptop was on earlier today connected to Wi-Fi at the Arlington office, but I had not opened Company Portal before contacting support. My username is rnguyen and I'm logged in with rnguyen@corplabs.com.

Thanks for confirming, Rachel. Review of the Intune record for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN showed the device last checked in on 2025-12-23T23:47:00Z — roughly 36 hours ago — and was not reporting its BitLocker/encryption state during that stale evaluation window. We forced a sync from the Intune console targeting your device and re-applied the encryption configuration profile (policy ID CP-ENC-0042) so compliance could be re-evaluated against current endpoint signals. The device has now checked in successfully and the encryption status is reporting as expected.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics showed that Rachel Nguyen's device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (IP 10.42.17.83) was correctly targeted by the encryption compliance policy (CP-ENC-0042) but had not checked in to Intune since 2025-12-23T23:47:00Z — roughly 36 hours before the reported issue. The stale check-in left the required BitLocker encryption signal missing from the device's compliance payload, so Intune evaluated the device as Noncompliant and Conditional Access denied Exchange Online access for rnguyen@corplabs.com. After forcing policy application and a new check-in via the Intune console, the encryption state reported successfully (BitLocker volume C: encrypted, 256-bit AES-XTS) and compliance returned to healthy.

correspondence.message: Hi Karim — thanks for reaching out. Could you please open Company Portal on your Samsung device (MOBILE-GALAXY-KB) and confirm whether the device still shows Not Compliant? After signing in with your account kbelhadj@corplabs.com, try running a manual sync from Settings > Sync within Company Portal and let me know if anything changes. I can see the device record on our side but want to confirm what you're seeing locally before we push anything remotely.

After the sync, Company Portal still showed Not Compliant and encryption was listed as "Not reported." Outlook Mobile seemed to briefly connect and pull a few messages, but then got blocked again. OneDrive Mobile was still completely blocked — I get the "Your device is not compliant" screen every time. I'm currently at the Lyon office and need these apps for a client presentation tomorrow, so any help is appreciated.

Thanks for confirming, Karim. I checked the Intune portal under Devices > Android > MOBILE-GALAXY-KB and confirmed the device (enrolled under user kbelhadj, EMP-40291) had not checked in for 14 days — last check-in was 2025-12-11T08:42Z. The compliance failure was tied exclusively to the missing encryption signal; OS version and all other policy conditions were passing. I forced another sync from the Intune console, re-sent the "EMEA Sales - Mobile Compliance" policy targeting the device, and after approximately 8 minutes the device completed a fresh check-in from IP 10.47.83.112. The encryption signal then reported as compliant and the overall device state flipped back to Compliant. Conditional Access blocks should now be cleared for both Outlook and OneDrive.

correspondence.message: Several managed laptops started showing NonCompliant in Intune after last night's compliance policy update (CP-WIN-ENCRYPT-v3), and users are being blocked from GlobalProtect VPN and SharePoint Online by Conditional Access. I'm Rachel Simmons in the Richmond sales office—my device WORKSTATION-RSIMMONS (IP 10.42.18.77) was the first one flagged. Derek Huang and Priya Nair on my team are also affected. We can't access any gated corporate resources and it's impacting our end-of-quarter pipeline work.

Initial review in the Intune admin center shows multiple affected devices have stale check-in timestamps predating the 2025-12-25 policy push. For example, rsimmons's device WORKSTATION-RSIMMONS last checked in on 2025-12-24 at 09:11 UTC, and dhuang's laptop WORKSTATION-DHUANG hasn't synced since 2025-12-23. Most appear to be failing on outdated compliance state rather than a sign-in or Conditional Access policy misconfiguration. I've also confirmed that pnair's device (WORKSTATION-PNAIR) is in the same stale state. Escalating to force sync across the affected device group. — Kevin Marsh, Endpoint Support (EMP-30294)

Forced device sync and compliance re-evaluation were run from the Intune admin console for all 12 affected endpoints. Nine devices—including WORKSTATION-RSIMMONS (rsimmons) and WORKSTATION-PNAIR (pnair)—returned to Compliant status within minutes of the forced sync. The remaining three devices (WORKSTATION-DHUANG for dhuang, plus laptops belonging to Marco Reyes and Lisa Choi) still show a missing encryption signal; BitLocker is either not enabled or has not reported status back to Intune. Those users have been contacted at dhuang@corplabs.com, mreyes@corplabs.com, and lchoi@corplabs.com with remediation instructions. — Kevin Marsh

We can also see the last check-in from your device was around 2025-12-24, which is well outside the expected 8-hour sync window.

I could not access email or SharePoint at all — every attempt redirected me to a Conditional Access block page. I do not think the Mac had synced recently, and FileVault was not fully enabled yet. I opened Company Portal and followed the prompt to turn encryption on. My colleague Niamh Brennan (nbrennan) mentioned she had a similar issue last month so she walked me through the steps.

Thanks Liam. Intune showed MACBOOK-PRO-LG (serial: C02FW3ABML7H) had not checked in for approximately 48 hours and the encryption signal was missing from the compliance report for user lgallagher. After a manual sync and FileVault enablement, the compliance state refreshed to compliant at 18:25 UTC and Conditional Access stopped blocking access to Exchange and SharePoint for your account.

correspondence.message: Several remote users reported sign-in failures this morning — Elena Brandt (ebrandt, EMP-40821) was the first to open a case, followed by reports from Tomasz Krol and at least five others in the Frankfurt and London offices. About 18 devices are showing noncompliant in the Intune admin center after last night's policy update pushed by mkovacs. The compliance policy appears to still reference ComplianceBaseline_v1, which I believe was retired as part of the December baseline refresh. Users are getting Conditional Access blocks when accessing Exchange and SharePoint from their corporate laptops.

Review shows the affected devices are in the correct Intune policy scope under the EMEA-RemoteWorkers device group, but the compliance policy is still pointing to deprecated ComplianceBaseline_v1 instead of the current ComplianceBaseline_v2. Multiple devices also have stale check-in timestamps — for example, Elena Brandt's workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-EB (IP 10.47.83.112) last checked in on 2025-12-26T14:22Z, well before the policy change at 22:00 UTC. Tomasz Krol's device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-TK (IP 10.47.84.56) shows a similar pattern. Compliance has not re-evaluated since the change on any of the ~18 affected endpoints, so Conditional Access is correctly denying access based on the stale noncompliant state.

I updated the policy reference from ComplianceBaseline_v1 to ComplianceBaseline_v2 in the Intune admin center and forced a device check-in across all 18 affected endpoints. Most devices — including those belonging to Elena Brandt, Tomasz Krol, and Priya Nair — have now returned to compliant status and can access Exchange and SharePoint again. The remaining four devices (users: Lars Henriksen EMP-40955, Sofia Ruiz, Amir Youssef, and Chen Wei) still need BitLocker enablement or have pending Windows cumulative updates before Conditional Access will allow sign-in. I've escalated remediation guidance to those users directly via email.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed this was primarily a policy configuration issue — the compliance policy still referenced deprecated ComplianceBaseline_v1 after admin mkovacs pushed the December baseline refresh — amplified by stale device check-ins across the EMEA-RemoteWorkers group. The affected 18 devices were in the intended compliance scope, but the stale baseline reference meant compliance signals were evaluated against outdated criteria. After correcting the baseline to ComplianceBaseline_v2 and forcing check-in, most endpoints (14 of 18) immediately re-evaluated as compliant. The remaining four devices (belonging to Lars Henriksen, Sofia Ruiz, Amir Youssef, and Chen Wei) required endpoint-level remediation for BitLocker encryption enablement or pending Windows 10 21H2 cumulative updates.

root_cause: The Intune device compliance policy was left pointing to the deprecated ComplianceBaseline_v1 assignment after the recent policy update. Devices that had not checked in after the change were re-evaluated against a stale baseline reference, so encryption and related compliance signals were not refreshed correctly and Conditional Access denied access based on noncompliant state.

steps: Updated the Intune compliance policy to replace the deprecated ComplianceBaseline_v1 reference with ComplianceBaseline_v2 in the Intune admin center, verified by admin mkovacs and the service desk.

Triggered a forced device check-in via the Intune admin console for all 18 impacted endpoints in the EMEA-RemoteWorkers group so the corrected policy and current compliance signals were evaluated immediately against ComplianceBaseline_v2.

Reviewed the remaining four noncompliant devices (Lars Henriksen WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-LH, Amir Youssef WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-AY, Sofia Ruiz, Chen Wei) to identify the specific failing signals, which were pending BitLocker enablement on two devices and required Windows cumulative update KB5048652 on the other two.

Sent targeted remediation guidance via email to the four affected users (lhenriksen@corplabs.com, sruiz@corplabs.com, ayoussef@corplabs.com, cwei@corplabs.com) instructing them to enable BitLocker via Control Panel > System and Security, install pending Windows updates including KB5048652, and reboot their devices to complete remediation.

Verified that all 18 devices re-reported compliant status in the Intune admin console after policy refresh and user remediation, restoring Conditional Access eligibility for Exchange Online and SharePoint Online. Final confirmation received from Elena Brandt and Priya Nair that access was restored.

correspondence.message: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether BitLocker still shows as enabled locally on the laptop (WORKSTATION-DELL-MR, IP 10.42.17.88) and whether any hardware maintenance or component replacement (e.g., motherboard, TPM module) was performed recently. Also, can you verify the last time you successfully synced through Company Portal? I can see the device is enrolled under your account m.reeves@corplabs.com in the Sales_Laptops group.

BitLocker shows as on in Control Panel — the C: drive is listed as fully encrypted. The laptop had a motherboard replacement done last Thursday at the Charlotte office by our on-site tech, and this morning around 02:15 I started getting blocked from Microsoft 365 because the device was reported noncompliant. I tried syncing from Company Portal but it just spun and didn't seem to complete. My username is mreeves and the hostname is WORKSTATION-DELL-MR.

Thanks Marcus. Intune shows the device WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (enrolled to mreeves, EMP-40821) has not checked in for 36 hours and is failing the encryption compliance signal even though BitLocker is enabled locally. The TPM attestation data appears to have been invalidated by the motherboard replacement, which means the Device Compliance Service never received an updated encryption status from the new hardware. This points to stale encryption telemetry after the hardware change rather than encryption being actually disabled. I'll proceed with remediation steps now.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the compliance failure was not caused by policy scoping or group assignment drift. The device WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (enrolled to user mreeves / EMP-40821, IP 10.42.17.88) had a stale 36-hour Intune check-in and an inconsistent encryption signal: BitLocker was enabled locally on the OS drive, but Intune still evaluated the endpoint as not encrypted due to missing TPM attestation data following the motherboard replacement at the Charlotte facility. This mismatch is consistent with a telemetry/reporting issue after the recent hardware swap, which caused Conditional Access to deny Microsoft 365 access for m.reeves@corplabs.com until the device re-synced and compliance was re-evaluated.

Verified locally that BitLocker protection was enabled on the OS drive (C:, AES-256) and re-applied the recovery key information via manage-bde so Windows management reporting and TPM-backed encryption status were correctly exposed to the new motherboard's TPM 2.0 chip.

Re-ran compliance evaluation in Intune for WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and monitored the device record until the encryption state updated from Not Encrypted to Compliant (encrypted) at 03:18 UTC and the overall device status returned to Compliant, restoring Conditional Access pass-through for m.reeves@corplabs.com.

I've pulled the Intune records for Maria Chen's device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (IP 10.47.83.112) and Derek Holloway's device WORKSTATION-PC-DH (IP 10.47.84.56) as initial samples. Can you also verify with the affected users whether they have been connected to VPN or had network access during the past two weeks?

Users reported they were blocked from corporate resources and several Company Portal entries showed old sync status. Maria Chen confirmed BitLocker is enabled locally on her machine but Company Portal last synced on 2025-12-16. Derek Holloway and Priya Nair reported similar issues — their devices appear encrypted locally, but Intune still shows them as noncompliant. Priya mentioned she hasn't been able to access Outlook since Monday. I also heard from Tom Beckett (tbeckett, phone 503-555-0147) who has the same problem on WORKSTATION-SURFACE-TB.

Review confirmed affected devices — including those belonging to mchen, dholloway, pnair, and tbeckett — had not checked in for more than 14 days and were missing the encryption compliance signal. After triggering a remote sync from the Intune admin console and initiating compliance reassessment, Maria Chen's device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC and Derek Holloway's device WORKSTATION-PC-DH returned to compliant status and regained access within 20 minutes. Priya Nair's and Tom Beckett's devices followed shortly after. All four users confirmed restored access to corporate resources.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed that the primary failure was stale endpoint management check-in across multiple RemoteWorkers devices in the Portland region, which prevented current encryption compliance telemetry from being evaluated. The assigned compliance policy (CP-WIN-ENCRYPT-01) scope was correct for the RemoteWorkers group, and the failing condition was the missing BitLocker signal combined with outdated compliance state on devices such as WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (mchen) and WORKSTATION-PC-DH (dholloway), leading Conditional Access to block access. Agent Raj Patel (EMP-10584) coordinated the investigation.

root_cause: Stale Intune device check-in older than 14 days prevented current compliance telemetry from reaching the Device Compliance Service, leaving the BitLocker encryption signal missing and causing Conditional Access to classify affected devices as noncompliant.

steps: Triggered immediate remote sync for impacted devices in Intune — including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (mchen), WORKSTATION-PC-DH (dholloway), and WORKSTATION-SURFACE-TB (tbeckett) — to refresh endpoint management check-in and force updated compliance telemetry submission. Agent Raj Patel (rpatel@corplabs.com) initiated the bulk sync action from the Intune admin console.

Initiated compliance reassessment for the affected device population (four devices across the Portland RemoteWorkers group) so Conditional Access could reevaluate device state after the new sync cycle completed. Reassessment was triggered via the Device Compliance Service at 2025-12-31T09:15:00Z.

Guided users — Maria Chen (503-555-0193), Derek Holloway, Priya Nair, and Tom Beckett — to confirm BitLocker was enabled on their Windows devices and to open Company Portal so the encryption state could be re-registered and reported back to Intune. All four users confirmed BitLocker active and Company Portal sync initiated.

Validated that device check-in timestamps advanced to 2025-12-31 and that the encryption compliance signal populated correctly (EncryptionStatus: Compliant) for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC, WORKSTATION-PC-DH, and WORKSTATION-SURFACE-TB before confirming access restoration for all affected users.

Adjusted reassessment timing to a 7-day compliance evaluation interval and placed short-term monitoring on devices that had previously stale check-ins so non-reporting endpoints can be escalated promptly if compliance telemetry stops updating again. Monitoring alerts configured by Raj Patel and assigned to the Portland endpoint management queue.

correspondence.message: Comparing affected corp.local lookups between the corporate resolver (dns-resolver-01.corp.local / 10.20.1.10) and authoritative DNS servers (ns1-auth.corp.local, ns2-auth.corp.local) now. Running nslookup and dig queries for internal-portal.corp.local, service-discovery.corp.local, and inventory-api.corp.local from Marcus Ellison's workstation WORKSTATION-DELL-ME at 10.20.44.87 and from the Network Monitoring probe in Denver. Need to confirm whether failures are stale answers at the resolver or missing records in the internal zone. — Raj Mehta, Network Engineering

Authoritative internal DNS servers (ns1-auth.corp.local and ns2-auth.corp.local) have the current records — internal-portal.corp.local correctly resolves to 10.20.30.15, service-discovery.corp.local to 10.20.30.22, and inventory-api.corp.local to 10.20.30.40 on the authoritative side. However, the corporate resolver at 10.20.1.10 is intermittently returning NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, and an older A record (10.10.10.5) for several of these hosts. Tested from both mellison's workstation and pnagarajan's machine WORKSTATION-HP-PN at 10.20.44.93 — same stale results. This points to stale cached resolver data rather than a zone content issue. Escalating cache flush to dns-resolver-01 immediately.

Flushed the primary resolver cache on dns-resolver-01.corp.local (10.20.1.10) using rndc flush and retested from representative clients including Marcus Ellison's workstation (WORKSTATION-DELL-ME / 10.20.44.87) and Priya Nagarajan's machine (WORKSTATION-HP-PN / 10.20.44.93). Lookups now return the current addresses from the authoritative zone — internal-portal.corp.local → 10.20.30.15, service-discovery.corp.local → 10.20.30.22, inventory-api.corp.local → 10.20.30.40. Affected internal services are resolving normally again. Notified mellison@corpnet.com and pnagarajan@corpnet.com of the resolution. — Raj Mehta

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the issue was isolated to the corporate resolver path (dns-resolver-01.corp.local / 10.20.1.10) rather than the authoritative internal DNS zone (ns1-auth.corp.local, ns2-auth.corp.local). Comparative lookups from affected clients in the Denver office showed the resolver was serving stale cached answers and intermittent failures (NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, old A record 10.10.10.5), while authoritative servers held the correct updated records. Flushing the resolver cache via rndc flush on dns-resolver-01 and tightening TTL settings from 86400s to 3600s on impacted zone entries restored consistent internal name resolution for all reported users.

steps.evidence: Resolver and authoritative responses did not match for several affected internal hosts. dig queries from WORKSTATION-DELL-ME (10.20.44.87, user mellison) against dns-resolver-01 returned 10.10.10.5 for internal-portal.corp.local while the authoritative server returned 10.20.30.15. Similar mismatches observed for service-discovery.corp.local and inventory-api.corp.local.

steps.action: Inspected the internal DNS zone records, TTL values, and current authoritative data for the impacted hostnames.
steps.expected_result: Zone contains the current record with expected TTL.
steps.observed_result: Authoritative zone data on ns1-auth.corp.local and ns2-auth.corp.local was current (internal-portal.corp.local → 10.20.30.15, service-discovery.corp.local → 10.20.30.22, inventory-api.corp.local → 10.20.30.40), but TTL settings on affected records were set to 86400 seconds (24 hours), allowing stale resolver data to persist much longer than desired after the zone update performed on 2026-01-04.
steps.evidence: Authoritative servers showed updated records for impacted names. Zone file inspection confirmed SOA serial incremented on 2026-01-04T22:15:00Z, but high TTL (86400s) meant the resolver would not re-query until the cache expired, well past the time users began reporting failures.

steps.action: Reviewed resolver handling for the internal zone and flushed the resolver cache to clear stale entries before retesting lookups.
steps.expected_result: Forwarder routes the zone correctly and cache returns fresh data.
steps.observed_result: After cache flush via rndc flush on dns-resolver-01.corp.local, the corporate resolver returned fresh answers matching the authoritative servers (internal-portal.corp.local → 10.20.30.15, service-discovery.corp.local → 10.20.30.22, inventory-api.corp.local → 10.20.30.40) and client tests from WORKSTATION-DELL-ME and WORKSTATION-HP-PN succeeded immediately.
steps.evidence: Cache flush on dns-resolver-01.corp.local restored correct responses for test clients (mellison at 10.20.44.87, pnagarajan at 10.20.44.93) and Network Monitoring probes. All three affected hostnames resolved to their updated A records within seconds of the flush.

root_cause: Corporate DNS resolver cache contained stale internal A records and continued serving outdated answers after authoritative corp.local zone records had been updated.

steps: Flushed the stale cache entries on the primary corporate DNS resolver (dns-resolver-01.corp.local / 10.20.1.10) using rndc flush to remove outdated A records (e.g., 10.10.10.5) being returned for affected corp.local hosts including internal-portal.corp.local, service-discovery.corp.local, and inventory-api.corp.local.

Verified the authoritative internal DNS zone contents on ns1-auth.corp.local and ns2-auth.corp.local for impacted records and confirmed the current addresses (10.20.30.15, 10.20.30.22, 10.20.30.40) were correct on the authoritative servers. SOA serial and zone transfer status validated between both authoritative nodes.

Adjusted TTL values for the affected zone records from 86400 seconds (24 hours) to 3600 seconds (1 hour) to reduce the likelihood and duration of long-lived stale cache entries after future record changes. Change approved by Raj Mehta and applied to the corp.local zone on ns1-auth.corp.local.

Validated name resolution from representative clients — Marcus Ellison's workstation WORKSTATION-DELL-ME (10.20.44.87) and Priya Nagarajan's workstation WORKSTATION-HP-PN (10.20.44.93) — and Network Monitoring paths to confirm the resolver now returned the same current addresses as the authoritative servers. All three affected service endpoints confirmed reachable by FQDN.

Clients on 10.20.30.0/24 are using resolver 10.20.30.2 (dns-res-east-02.corplabs.internal), which is a different internal resolver path than the one used by other subnets. dig @10.20.30.2 app-db.internal returns NXDOMAIN every time. The same lookup succeeds immediately when I point dig at 10.50.1.10 (dns-res-core-01.corplabs.internal). My colleague Raj Patel on the dev subnet (10.40.10.0/24) confirmed resolution works fine from his side. — Maria Gonzalez

Escalation team (network_team, handled by Kevin Osei) reviewed the affected resolver path on dns-res-east-02.corplabs.internal (10.20.30.2). The conditional forwarder for the .internal zone was pointing to an outdated upstream target that had been decommissioned during last quarter's infrastructure refresh. We corrected the forwarding target to point to the current authoritative internal DNS servers (dns-auth-01.corplabs.internal / dns-auth-02.corplabs.internal) and flushed all cached DNS entries on dns-res-east-02. Validation from Maria's workstation (10.20.30.47) and from Raj's subnet now both return the expected A record 10.60.5.22 for app-db.internal, matching known-good resolver results.

The conditional forwarder on dns-res-east-02 was targeting a decommissioned upstream server. Updating the resolver's forwarding target and clearing stale cached NXDOMAIN data restored consistent internal name resolution for all affected users including Maria Gonzalez.

correspondence.message: Initial DNS checks for app.example.internal showed mixed results from internal resolvers. Running `dig @dns-primary-01.dc1.internal app.example.internal A` from Priya's workstation WORKSTATION-L490-PN (10.30.14.88) returned the stale IP 10.20.5.47, while queries from resolver dns-secondary-02.dc1.internal intermittently returned NXDOMAIN. Agent Marcus Reilly confirmed the inconsistency by querying from the Portland resolver path as well, suggesting stale zone data or cached resolver responses were the root of the problem.

Reviewed the internal zone file /etc/named/zones/db.example.internal on dns-primary-01.dc1.internal and found the A record for app.example.internal still pointed to 10.20.5.47 — a decommissioned backend that was retired on 2025-12-18. Updated the zone entry to point to the active backend IP 10.20.8.112, incremented the zone serial from 2025121801 to 2026010501, reloaded named via `rndc reload example.internal`, and cleared resolver caches on both dns-primary-01 and dns-secondary-02 using `rndc flush`. Change performed by mreilly under change task CHG-88412.

Post-change validation from affected client paths and monitoring confirmed app.example.internal now resolves consistently to 10.20.8.112. Priya Nambiar verified from WORKSTATION-L490-PN that the hostname resolved correctly and the internal-app-service dashboard loaded without errors. Network Monitoring dashboard checks from both Austin and Portland resolver paths returned the correct address. The hostname access issue is cleared.

steps: Corrected the A record for app.example.internal in the internal DNS zone file /etc/named/zones/db.example.internal so it pointed to the active backend IP 10.20.8.112 instead of the decommissioned address 10.20.5.47.
