Recommended adjusting the internal DNS TTL policy from 86400s to 3600s for application-tier hostnames to reduce the duration and impact of stale cached records in future changes. Flagged for review by the network team lead Deepak Rao.

correspondence.message: Internal service owners report that svc-db.internal intermittently returns NXDOMAIN and several application pods cannot reach the DB by name. Marcus Delgado (EMP-40821) initially flagged the issue after internal-order-service health checks began failing from host WORKSTATION-LINUX-MD at 10.42.17.88. Traces show failures concentrated to queries served by dns-resolver-01.corp.internal, with secondary impact observed by Priya Nair (pnair) on the payment-processor team. Affected pods are running on app-node-03 and app-node-07 in the Phoenix datacenter.

Testing confirmed NXDOMAIN responses from dns-resolver-01.corp.internal when querying svc-db.internal. Running `dig svc-db.internal @dns-resolver-01.corp.internal` from 10.42.17.88 returned status NXDOMAIN consistently, while dns-resolver-02.corp.internal returned the expected 10.20.9.42. The internal DNS zone entry for svc-db.internal contains an outdated A record pointing to 10.20.5.14 (last modified 2025-06-12) with stale metadata, plus a deprecated internal-dns-policy-v1 reference in the zone management config. Findings reviewed with network engineer Tomás Reyes (treyes) before proceeding with remediation.

Performed a targeted cache flush on dns-resolver-01.corp.internal using `rndc flush` to validate stale resolver state, then prepared the corrective zone record update (svc-db.internal A → 10.20.9.42, TTL 300) and policy reference replacement (internal-dns-policy-v1 → internal-dns-policy-v2) before broader cache propagation to dns-resolver-02 and dns-resolver-03. Change approved by Tomás Reyes (treyes@corplabs.com) under CHG-88214. Post-flush, resolution from WORKSTATION-LINUX-MD at 10.42.17.88 returned the correct address immediately.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics tied the outage to the DNS layer rather than the database service itself. Resolver-specific testing from affected host WORKSTATION-LINUX-MD (10.42.17.88) showed intermittent NXDOMAIN responses from dns-resolver-01.corp.internal, while dns-resolver-02.corp.internal resolved correctly to 10.20.9.42. Zone inspection found a stale A record for svc-db.internal pointing to decommissioned IP 10.20.5.14 (last updated 2025-06-12), and configuration review identified a deprecated internal-dns-policy-v1 reference in zone management that allowed the outdated record to persist. After correcting the A record to 10.20.9.42, updating the policy reference to internal-dns-policy-v2, and flushing resolver caches on dns-resolver-01 through dns-resolver-03, hostname resolution was restored and validated from affected application hosts by network engineer Tomás Reyes.

steps.evidence: Zone review via Internal DNS Zone management console matched the stale record condition described in the incident — A record target 10.20.5.14 vs. expected 10.20.9.42 — and identified the deprecated internal-dns-policy-v1 reference preventing zone synchronization on dns-resolver-01.corp.internal.

correspondence.message: service.internal.corp is intermittently failing from the Austin and Raleigh sites through resolver 10.1.1.10. We see NXDOMAIN and occasional timeouts — tested from my workstation WORKSTATION-MBP-MD (IP 10.22.4.117) and from colleague Priya Nair's machine WORKSTATION-LNX-PN. Direct nslookup checks against the authoritative DNS server dns-auth-01.internal.corp return the expected A record 10.40.16.55 every time. This is blocking our CI/CD pipeline and developer portal access. — Marcus Delgado (mdelgado)

Confirmed the authoritative zone on dns-auth-01.internal.corp is healthy and contains the expected A record (service.internal.corp → 10.40.16.55, TTL 300). The mismatch is on resolver 10.1.1.10, which is intermittently serving NXDOMAIN or delayed responses for the same name. Ran parallel dig queries from network monitoring host in Raleigh — approximately 30% of queries to 10.1.1.10 returned NXDOMAIN while the remainder resolved correctly. Assigning to network_team lead Raj Venkatesh (rvenkatesh) for resolver-side investigation.

Cache flush alone on resolver 10.1.1.10 did not fully resolve the issue — NXDOMAIN responses persisted for roughly 1 in 5 queries after the flush. Upon inspection, the internal zone conditional forwarder on 10.1.1.10 had a stale secondary target (10.1.1.22, decommissioned) alongside the valid authoritative server dns-auth-01.internal.corp (10.1.1.30). When the resolver round-robined to the dead forwarder target, it cached negative responses. Removed the stale forwarder entry, corrected the forwarder path, and cleared all negative cache entries. Repeated lookups from Marcus Delgado's workstation (WORKSTATION-MBP-MD) and Priya Nair's machine (WORKSTATION-LNX-PN) now return 10.40.16.55 consistently. Verified from both Austin and Raleigh. — Raj Venkatesh

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics established that the internal zone record for service.internal.corp (A → 10.40.16.55) existed and authoritative DNS on dns-auth-01.internal.corp was healthy. The failure pattern was isolated to resolver 10.1.1.10, which intermittently returned NXDOMAIN or timed out for a hostname that authoritative servers resolved correctly. Approximately 30% of recursive queries failed. Cache flush by itself did not fully remediate the issue, supporting a resolver forwarding/configuration problem — specifically a stale secondary forwarder target (10.1.1.22, decommissioned) combined with stale negative cache behavior. After correcting the resolver conditional forwarder path for the internal zone and clearing cached data, lookups from affected clients (including WORKSTATION-MBP-MD at 10.22.4.117 and WORKSTATION-LNX-PN) became consistent across both Austin and Raleigh sites.

After removing the stale forwarder entry, correcting resolver forwarding behavior, and clearing stale negative cache, lookups stabilized across all tested clients.

Forwarder config on 10.1.1.10 listed two targets: 10.1.1.30 (valid, dns-auth-01.internal.corp) and 10.1.1.22 (decommissioned). Queries routed to 10.1.1.22 timed out and generated negative cache entries, confirmed by Raj Venkatesh (rvenkatesh) via resolver debug logs.

root_cause: Resolver 10.1.1.10 had an internal DNS forwarding/cache issue for the internal zone: the authoritative server held the correct A record for service.internal.corp, but the resolver intermittently served NXDOMAIN or timed-out responses until conditional forwarder behavior and cached zone data were corrected.

steps: Validated that the authoritative DNS server dns-auth-01.internal.corp (10.1.1.30) for the internal zone returned the expected A record for service.internal.corp (10.40.16.55, TTL 300) and confirmed the issue was isolated to recursive resolver 10.1.1.10 behavior rather than a missing zone record. Verification performed by Raj Venkatesh from the Raleigh network monitoring host.

Reviewed and corrected the conditional forwarder path for the internal zone on resolver 10.1.1.10 — removed stale secondary forwarder target 10.1.1.22 (decommissioned) so queries for service.internal.corp consistently routed only to the valid authoritative DNS server dns-auth-01.internal.corp (10.1.1.30).

Cleared stale cached entries and negative cache data (rndc flush) on the affected internal resolver 10.1.1.10 after the forwarder configuration was corrected, ensuring no residual NXDOMAIN responses persisted from the decommissioned target.

Retested repeated lookups for service.internal.corp from the affected resolver and from multiple client locations — including Marcus Delgado's workstation WORKSTATION-MBP-MD (10.22.4.117, Austin) and Priya Nair's machine WORKSTATION-LNX-PN (Raleigh) — to confirm the resolver now returned 10.40.16.55 consistently without NXDOMAIN or timeout responses. 100/100 queries succeeded.

Monitored resolver and DNS query behavior via Network Monitoring dashboards for 2 hours after the change to verify timeout spikes stopped and internal applications (internal-service-api, developer-portal) could consistently resolve the service endpoint. Confirmed with Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) that CI/CD pipeline and portal access were fully restored.

The hostname is internal-app.company.local, and failures were seen between 09:12 and 09:40 EST with repeated NXDOMAIN responses on multiple client machines. We corrected the A record, incremented the zone serial from 2025120901 to 2026010701, reloaded the zone via `rndc reload company.local`, flushed resolver cache state on both cache-east-01 and cache-east-02 with `rndc flush`, restarted named on the primary resolver, and verified successful lookups from affected subnets including Marcus's workstation WORKSTATION-MD-4821 and monitoring probes. — Priya Nair

The A record for internal-service.corp.local was pointing to the decommissioned address 10.40.12.40 in cache instead of the current 10.40.12.55. Confirmed with dig queries from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN and from host WORKSTATION-DESK-MO used by Marcus Okonkwo. correspondence.message: Hi Priya — please confirm whether app.payments.corp fails only through the standard internal resolver (DNS-CACHE-01.corplabs.internal, 10.20.1.53) or also when tested against another known-good internal DNS path such as DNS-AUTH-02.corplabs.internal, and whether the issue started immediately after last night's DNS maintenance. Also, can you let us know which client hostnames or IPs you tested from?

We tested from different clients and regions. From my workstation WORKSTATION-PN-7241 at IP 10.44.12.87 in the Chicago office and from host WORKSTATION-DLEE-3390 (Derek Lee, dlee) in the Austin office, the normal internal resolver intermittently returns NXDOMAIN or times out, and the behavior started after the DNS maintenance window last night. Our monitoring dashboard also flagged the same pattern from several other endpoints.

Network team (Marcus Reeves, mreeves, EMP-55034) reviewed the zone and resolver path on DNS-CACHE-01.corplabs.internal and DNS-CACHE-03.corplabs.internal, then flushed resolver caches and corrected DNS routing/forwarder handling for the internal namespace. Follow-up lookups for app.payments.corp are now consistent from all tested locations including Chicago and Austin.

After resolver-side correction and cache clearing, app.payments.corp resolved consistently again to 10.30.5.120.

root_cause: DNS maintenance left inconsistent internal resolver state for the app.payments.corp zone path, with stale or incorrect cached data and/or forwarder handling causing intermittent negative responses and timeouts despite the zone record needing to resolve internally. The incident behavior across multiple hosts and regions points to resolver-side cache/forwarder inconsistency rather than a single client issue.

steps: Reviewed the internal zone record and recent maintenance changes for app.payments.corp to confirm the expected target value (10.30.5.120) and TTL (300s) after the DNS work performed during change CHG-90412 by mreeves on 2026-01-07.

Assigning remediation to Priya Nair (pnair) from the network infrastructure team. — Reviewed by Kevin Cho, Network Tier 2

correspondence.message: Monitoring and users are seeing app.example.corp intermittently resolve to 10.0.1.23, while other lookups return 10.0.2.45 or NXDOMAIN, so the application endpoint is not consistently reachable by name. I first noticed the issue around 13:20 UTC when my build pipeline failed to pull from the endpoint. My workstation (WORKSTATION-MACBOOK-MD, IP 10.12.4.87) gets the old IP about half the time. Colleagues Priya Nair (pnair) and Jason Whitfield (jwhitfield) in the Portland office confirmed the same behavior from their machines. Network Monitoring dashboard for us-west-2 shows elevated DNS lookup failures starting shortly after the record change window. — Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com), EMP-40291

Additionally, dns-rec-west-03 intermittently returned NXDOMAIN, suggesting its cache state was partially corrupted. Ran dig @dns-rec-west-02.corplabs.internal app.example.corp and confirmed the stale answer. The authoritative SOA serial has already incremented. Escalating to flush and restart the affected resolver instances. — Reviewed by Tanya Reeves (treeves), Network Engineering

Flushed affected resolver caches on dns-rec-west-02.corplabs.internal and dns-rec-west-03.corplabs.internal using rndc flush, then restarted the resolver service (named) on dns-rec-west-03 which was not honoring TTL refresh behavior correctly. Follow-up queries from Marcus's workstation (10.12.4.87), Priya's machine (WORKSTATION-DELL-PN, 10.12.4.92), and Jason's host now consistently return 10.0.2.45. Network Monitoring probes across the Portland and Seattle segments confirm uniform resolution. Will continue monitoring for 24 hours for any residual stale responses. — Tanya Reeves (treeves)

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the authoritative DNS zone on ns-auth.corplabs.internal was correct, but recursive resolvers ns-rec-01 and ns-rec-02 were serving stale and negative cached data for internal-service.corp. Cross-checking resolver responses against the authoritative record isolated cache divergence as the failure point. Investigation led by Priya Nair (pnair) confirmed that the stale entry (192.0.2.50) had been cached prior to a record update performed on 2026-01-07. Cache flushes and temporary TTL reduction from 3600s to 300s restored consistent resolution to 192.0.2.75 across all resolver nodes in the Arlington data center.
observed_errors: stale DNS record present in resolver cache

steps.action: Query internal-service.corp from affected resolvers and compare the answer with a known-good authoritative response.
steps.expected_result: Both resolvers return the same current address.
steps.observed_result: Affected resolvers ns-rec-01.corplabs.internal and ns-rec-02.corplabs.internal returned intermittent NXDOMAIN or stale address 192.0.2.50, while the authoritative source ns-auth.corplabs.internal showed 192.0.2.75. Queries from client 10.22.9.34 (WORKSTATION-PC-MD) consistently received NXDOMAIN.
steps.evidence: Resolver logs on ns-rec-01 showed repeated NXDOMAIN responses for internal-service.corp between 09:40–09:55 UTC; ns-rec-02 logs showed stale cached A record value 192.0.2.50 served to 14 unique client IPs including 10.22.9.34 and 10.22.14.88.

steps.action: Inspect the internal DNS zone record, TTL, and current authoritative value for internal-service.corp.
steps.expected_result: Zone contains the current record with expected TTL.
steps.observed_result: Authoritative Internal DNS Zone on ns-auth.corplabs.internal was correct and showed A record 192.0.2.75 with original TTL 3600s; TTL was then reduced temporarily to 300s by Priya Nair to speed propagation across recursive resolvers.
steps.evidence: Zone validation via dig @ns-auth.corplabs.internal internal-service.corp A matched the intended current service address 192.0.2.75. SOA serial 2026010802 confirmed the record had been updated on 2026-01-07 at 22:15 UTC.

steps.action: Check recursive resolver cache behavior and flush stale entries so the zone returns fresh data consistently.
steps.expected_result: Forwarder routes the zone correctly and cache returns fresh data.
steps.observed_result: Recursive cache on ns-rec-01 and ns-rec-02 contained stale A record (192.0.2.50) and negative cache entries (NXDOMAIN, TTL remaining ~1800s); after cache flush executed by Ramon Estrada (restrada), resolvers returned the fresh authoritative answer 192.0.2.75.
steps.evidence: Post-flush validation via nslookup and dig from WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.22.9.34), WORKSTATION-LT-KC (10.22.14.88), and Network Monitoring probe at 10.22.0.5 confirmed consistent resolution of internal-service.corp to 192.0.2.75 across all affected nodes.

root_cause: Stale and inconsistent DNS cache entries on recursive resolvers caused internal-service.corp to return NXDOMAIN or an outdated A record (192.0.2.50) instead of the authoritative value (192.0.2.75).

steps: Validated that the authoritative Internal DNS Zone on ns-auth.corplabs.internal for internal-service.corp was correct and publishing A record 192.0.2.75 (SOA serial 2026010802, updated 2026-01-07 22:15 UTC).

Compared responses from affected recursive resolvers ns-rec-01.corplabs.internal and ns-rec-02.corplabs.internal against the authoritative zone and confirmed cache divergence, including stale A record 192.0.2.50 and intermittent NXDOMAIN responses affecting clients such as 10.22.9.34 (mdelgado) and 10.22.14.88 (kcho).

Flushed DNS cache on the primary resolver ns-rec-01.corplabs.internal and affected recursive nodes ns-rec-02 and ns-rec-03 to remove stale and negative cached entries for internal-service.corp. Flush performed by Ramon Estrada (restrada, EMP-55190).

Cleared client-side DNS cache on impacted application nodes including WORKSTATION-PC-MD (Marcus Delgado, 10.22.9.34) and WORKSTATION-LT-KC (Kevin Cho, 10.22.14.88) and re-ran lookups to confirm consistent resolution to 192.0.2.75.

Temporarily reduced the record TTL from 3600s to 300s to accelerate propagation of the corrected answer and monitored resolver responses via Network Monitoring for 30 minutes to confirm stability after cache refresh. TTL will be restored to 3600s after 24-hour observation window.

correspondence.message: Hi Marcus — please provide any affected internal hostnames (e.g., hrportal.corp.eastnet.local, payroll-api.corp.eastnet.local), approximate failure times, and whether the NXDOMAIN or timeout behavior changes by site or application server so we can compare resolver paths. Also, can you confirm which client machines or app servers you've tested from? If you have nslookup or dig output from WORKSTATION-PC-MD or any of the app nodes, please attach those as well. — Priya Nair, Network Engineering

We do not have a complete hostname list, but HR Portal (hrportal.corp.eastnet.local), Payroll API (payroll-api.corp.eastnet.local), and Inventory calls (inventory.corp.eastnet.local) are intermittently failing. Different servers seem to get different answers — for example, APPNODE-EAST-04 gets NXDOMAIN while APPNODE-EAST-07 resolves fine. I ran nslookup from my workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.40.12.88) and got the stale 10.40.2.17 address for hrportal.corp.eastnet.local. Some retries work later without any application change. Colleagues Janelle Torres (jtorres) and Raj Mehta (rmehta) in the Newark office have reported the same behavior from their machines.

Comparison lookups from DNS-RES-EAST-01 and DNS-RES-EAST-02 showed inconsistent DNS answers across internal resolvers, including NXDOMAIN and stale IP responses (10.40.2.17 vs. the current 10.40.5.33) for hrportal.corp.eastnet.local and payroll-api.corp.eastnet.local. The conditional forwarder on DNS-RES-EAST-02 for the corp.eastnet.local zone was missing the updated delegation to the authoritative server DNS-AUTH-EAST-01. We are correcting conditional forwarding and clearing resolver cache on both DNS-RES-EAST-01 and DNS-RES-EAST-02, then validating repeated lookups from multiple locations including Marcus's workstation and the affected app nodes. — Priya Nair

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics showed inconsistent answers for the same internal hostname (hrportal.corp.eastnet.local, payroll-api.corp.eastnet.local, inventory.corp.eastnet.local) across resolver paths DNS-RES-EAST-01 and DNS-RES-EAST-02, including NXDOMAIN, timeout, and stale IP responses (10.40.2.17 instead of 10.40.5.33). The authoritative zone on DNS-AUTH-EAST-01 appeared present with the correct records, but resolver behavior indicated stale cache and inconsistent forwarding/delegation to authoritative DNS. DNS-RES-EAST-02 was missing the conditional forwarder entry for the corp.eastnet.local zone. After correcting forwarder behavior and clearing resolver cache on both resolvers, repeated cross-location queries from client 10.40.12.88 (WORKSTATION-PC-MD) and app nodes returned consistent current records.
observed_errors: stale address observed in resolver cache

steps.action: Queried the same internal hostname from an affected resolver path and from a comparison resolver to check for answer consistency.
steps.expected_result: Both resolvers return the same current address.
steps.observed_result: Lookup results were inconsistent: queries from DNS-RES-EAST-02 for hrportal.corp.eastnet.local returned NXDOMAIN or timed out, while DNS-RES-EAST-01 returned 10.40.2.17 (stale address). Direct query against DNS-AUTH-EAST-01 returned the current address 10.40.5.33. At least one probe from client 10.40.12.88 (WORKSTATION-PC-MD, user mdelgado) showed the older IP for the same name.
steps.evidence: Cross-location lookups did not agree on answer or response behavior. nslookup hrportal.corp.eastnet.local from DNS-RES-EAST-01 returned 10.40.2.17; from DNS-RES-EAST-02 returned NXDOMAIN; direct authoritative query returned 10.40.5.33. Client WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.40.12.88) received the stale cached answer.

steps.action: Inspected the internal DNS zone record state, TTL, and recent record validity for reported internal service names.
steps.expected_result: Zone contains the current record with expected TTL.
steps.observed_result: Authoritative zone review on DNS-AUTH-EAST-01 supported that the intended A records for hrportal.corp.eastnet.local (10.40.5.33), payroll-api.corp.eastnet.local (10.40.5.41), and inventory.corp.eastnet.local (10.40.5.52) existed with TTL 300s, but resolver responses from DNS-RES-EAST-01 and DNS-RES-EAST-02 did not consistently reflect the same current values, indicating propagation or cache inconsistency rather than a uniformly missing record.
steps.evidence: Zone data on DNS-AUTH-EAST-01 and live resolver answers from DNS-RES-EAST-01 / DNS-RES-EAST-02 did not fully align across all probes. dig @DNS-AUTH-EAST-01 hrportal.corp.eastnet.local A returned 10.40.5.33 (TTL 300), but dig @DNS-RES-EAST-02 returned SERVFAIL for the same query.

steps.action: Checked conditional forwarder behavior for the internal namespace and flushed stale resolver cache before retesting repeated queries.
steps.expected_result: Forwarder routes the zone correctly and cache returns fresh data.
steps.observed_result: Forwarder configuration on DNS-RES-EAST-02 required correction — the conditional forwarder for corp.eastnet.local was missing the delegation to DNS-AUTH-EAST-01. Cached stale responses on DNS-RES-EAST-01 (10.40.2.17 for hrportal) were cleared; after cache flush on both resolvers and forwarder validation, repeated lookups from WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.40.12.88) and app nodes returned the current addresses (10.40.5.33, 10.40.5.41, 10.40.5.52) consistently.
steps.evidence: Post-change testing from client 10.40.12.88 (mdelgado), APPNODE-EAST-04, and APPNODE-EAST-07 no longer reproduced NXDOMAIN or stale-address responses. All queries for hrportal.corp.eastnet.local, payroll-api.corp.eastnet.local, and inventory.corp.eastnet.local returned the correct current A records via both DNS-RES-EAST-01 and DNS-RES-EAST-02.

root_cause: Intermittent resolution was most consistent with inconsistent internal DNS pathing: one or more resolvers had stale cached records while conditional forwarding or zone delegation for the affected internal zone was not consistently returning authoritative answers. This caused different resolvers to return NXDOMAIN, timeouts, or outdated addresses for the same hostname until cache and forwarder configuration were corrected.

steps: Reviewed the affected internal DNS zone records on DNS-AUTH-EAST-01 for the corp.eastnet.local zone, validated current A records (hrportal → 10.40.5.33, payroll-api → 10.40.5.41, inventory → 10.40.5.52) and TTL values (300s), and corrected stale record data where resolver responses did not match the authoritative zone.

Verified conditional forwarder and zone routing configuration between internal resolvers DNS-RES-EAST-01 / DNS-RES-EAST-02 and the authoritative DNS server DNS-AUTH-EAST-01, then added the missing forwarder path on DNS-RES-EAST-02 for the corp.eastnet.local namespace.
Flushed DNS cache on impacted internal resolvers DNS-RES-EAST-01 and DNS-RES-EAST-02 (dnscmd /clearcache) and repeated lookups to remove stale answers (10.40.2.17) previously being served from cache.

Retested name resolution from multiple resolver paths and client locations — including WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.40.12.88, mdelgado), APPNODE-EAST-04, and APPNODE-EAST-07 — using repeated nslookup/dig queries to confirm the same current address was returned consistently for all three affected service hostnames.

Enabled follow-up monitoring via Network Monitoring for internal name resolution on the corp.eastnet.local zone so future NXDOMAIN, timeout, or stale-answer patterns can be correlated with affected hostnames and timing if the issue recurs. Notified Marcus Delgado (mdelgado), Janelle Torres (jtorres), and Raj Mehta (rmehta) of the resolution.

correspondence.message: Primary resolver DNS-PRI-EAST.corp.internal is returning intermittent NXDOMAIN for svc-inventory.corp. Agent mellison confirmed that direct IP connectivity to 10.42.16.55 still works from workstation WORKSTATION-DELL-ME, which points to a DNS resolution problem rather than the Inventory Service being down. Ticket escalated by Priya Nair (pnair) on the network operations team.

Review of the internal zone corp.internal and resolver cache on DNS-PRI-EAST.corp.internal found an A record tied to decommissioned host 10.42.16.12 with a TTL of 86400 seconds, allowing stale DNS data to persist on the primary resolver. Zone last modified by dcohen on 2025-11-03 during the infrastructure migration. Cross-checked with Network Monitoring dashboard; NXDOMAIN spike correlates with the record staleness window.

Corrected the zone record for svc-inventory.corp to point to 10.42.16.55, lowered the TTL to 300 seconds, and flushed caches on DNS-PRI-EAST.corp.internal and DNS-SEC-EAST.corp.internal. Validation from subnets 10.42.16.0/24 and 10.42.20.0/24 now returns the expected address for svc-inventory.corp. Confirmed with mellison and application owner Rachel Torres (rtorres) that the Inventory Service and Internal Web App are reachable by hostname again.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed this was an internal DNS data freshness issue rather than an application or network reachability outage. Lookup checks from WORKSTATION-DELL-ME (10.42.20.107) showed NXDOMAIN behavior from the primary resolver DNS-PRI-EAST.corp.internal, zone inspection identified a stale A record pointing to decommissioned host 10.42.16.12 with an excessively long TTL of 86400s, and cache validation confirmed the bad record persisted until resolver caches were flushed on both primary and secondary resolvers.

steps.action: Query svc-inventory.corp from the affected primary resolver and compare the result with resolution behavior seen by clients on multiple subnets.
steps.expected_result: Both resolvers return the same current address.
steps.observed_result: Affected lookups from client 10.42.20.107 (WORKSTATION-DELL-ME, user mellison) returned NXDOMAIN intermittently from the primary resolver DNS-PRI-EAST.corp.internal while users reported direct IP access to 10.42.16.55 still worked, indicating a DNS-specific issue rather than service unavailability.
steps.evidence: Network Monitoring showed elevated NXDOMAIN responses on DNS-PRI-EAST.corp.internal beginning 2026-01-08T22:15:00Z, and app teams including rtorres reported hostname failures from subnets 10.42.16.0/24 and 10.42.20.0/24 in Charlotte.

steps.action: Inspect the internal DNS zone record, TTL, and recent record state for svc-inventory.corp.
steps.expected_result: Zone contains the current record with expected TTL.
steps.observed_result: The zone corp.internal and related record state showed an A record for svc-inventory.corp tied to decommissioned host IP 10.42.16.12 and a TTL of 86400 seconds that allowed stale data to persist. The record was last updated by dcohen on 2025-11-03.
steps.evidence: Zone review on DNS-PRI-EAST.corp.internal matched the stale address condition (10.42.16.12 vs. current 10.42.16.55) described in resolver behavior. Change log attributed last modification to dcohen.

steps.action: Check resolver cache behavior for the affected name and clear stale cached data on primary and secondary resolvers.
steps.expected_result: Forwarder routes the zone correctly and cache returns fresh data.
steps.observed_result: Resolver cache on DNS-PRI-EAST.corp.internal contained the stale entry pointing to 10.42.16.12; after cache flush on both DNS-PRI-EAST and DNS-SEC-EAST, lookups returned the corrected address 10.42.16.55 from multiple subnets.
steps.evidence: Post-flush validation confirmed successful resolution of svc-inventory.corp to 10.42.16.55 on primary and secondary resolver paths. Verified by pnair from 10.42.20.0/24 and 10.42.16.0/24 subnets.

root_cause: A stale A record for svc-inventory.corp remained cached on the primary resolver and was associated with a decommissioned host, and the long TTL allowed the incorrect data to persist and be served during internal DNS lookups.

steps: Reviewed the internal DNS zone corp.internal for svc-inventory.corp and corrected the A record so it pointed to the current service IP 10.42.16.55 instead of the decommissioned host reference 10.42.16.12.
Reduced the TTL on the affected DNS record from 86400 seconds to 300 seconds to shorten persistence of incorrect cached data during propagation of the corrected entry.
Flushed DNS cache entries on the primary resolver DNS-PRI-EAST.corp.internal and secondary resolver DNS-SEC-EAST.corp.internal to remove the stale record immediately.

Validated name resolution for svc-inventory.corp from multiple client subnets (10.42.16.0/24 and 10.42.20.0/24) and confirmed the hostname consistently returned the expected address 10.42.16.55. Reporter mellison and application owner rtorres both confirmed service restoration.

Updated DNS monitoring logic in Network Monitoring and operational guidance for the Charlotte network team to better detect stale-record and elevated NXDOMAIN patterns for internal service names, including automated alerting thresholds for NXDOMAIN spikes.

correspondence.message: We are comparing answers from bind-resolver-01 (10.20.5.12) against the authoritative corp.local zone on ns-auth-01.corp.local to confirm whether the issue is with the source record or stale resolver data for service1.corp.local. Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) reported that his workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD at 10.20.41.77 was receiving NXDOMAIN responses when querying the hostname. Network engineer Priya Nair is leading the investigation.

The authoritative zone on ns-auth-01.corp.local returns the current IP 10.50.12.88 for service1.corp.local, but bind-resolver-01 (10.20.5.12) intermittently returns NXDOMAIN or the prior A record pointing to 10.50.12.60, which indicates stale resolver cache rather than a missing DNS record. We also confirmed the same stale behavior from a second affected host belonging to Tomás Rivera (trivera) at 10.20.41.93 in the Charlotte office, ruling out a client-side issue.

Updated the outdated resolver policy reference in /etc/bind/named.conf.options on bind-resolver-01, flushed cache via rndc flush, and restarted the named service; follow-up lookups from both mdelgado's workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD and trivera's host now return the current authoritative address 10.50.12.88 consistently. Priya Nair has confirmed monitoring dashboards are green.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the authoritative corp.local zone on ns-auth-01.corp.local was healthy and serving the correct A record (10.50.12.88) for service1.corp.local, while bind-resolver-01 (10.20.5.12) intermittently answered with NXDOMAIN or the outdated address 10.50.12.60 from stale cache. Resolver-side configuration review by Priya Nair identified an outdated update policy reference in named.conf.options contributing to stale response behavior. After correcting the resolver configuration and clearing cache, lookups from the resolver and affected hosts (including WORKSTATION-PC-MD at 10.20.41.77) aligned with authoritative data and monitoring recovered.
observed_errors: cached old A record returned by resolver

steps.action: Query the affected hostname from bind-resolver-01 and compare the result with the authoritative response for the same record.
steps.expected_result: Both resolvers return the same current address.
steps.observed_result: The authoritative zone on ns-auth-01.corp.local returned the updated IP 10.50.12.88, while bind-resolver-01 (10.20.5.12) intermittently returned NXDOMAIN or the previous A record 10.50.12.60 for service1.corp.local.
steps.evidence: dig @10.20.5.12 service1.corp.local A returned 10.50.12.60 (stale) or NXDOMAIN on successive queries, whereas dig @ns-auth-01.corp.local service1.corp.local A consistently returned 10.50.12.88. Mismatch confirmed from mdelgado's workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.20.41.77).

steps.action: Inspect the internal corp.local zone record, TTL, and recent update state for the affected hostname.
steps.expected_result: Zone contains the current record with expected TTL.
steps.observed_result: The zone on ns-auth-01.corp.local contained the correct current A record (service1.corp.local → 10.50.12.88, TTL 300) for the affected host, indicating the issue was not with the authoritative record at time of validation.
steps.evidence: rndc zonestatus corp.local on ns-auth-01.corp.local showed serial 2026010903 with last update at 2026-01-09T10:15:00Z. Authoritative zone check confirmed the expected record value 10.50.12.88 with a 300-second TTL.

steps.action: Review resolver forwarding or update policy behavior and flush stale cache entries on bind-resolver-01.
steps.expected_result: Forwarder routes the zone correctly and cache returns fresh data.
steps.observed_result: Resolver cache on bind-resolver-01 contained stale data mapping service1.corp.local to 10.50.12.60; after policy correction in named.conf.options and cache flush via rndc flush, fresh responses matched the authoritative zone (10.50.12.88) and NXDOMAIN behavior stopped.
steps.evidence: rndc dumpdb -cache on bind-resolver-01 showed a cached entry for service1.corp.local pointing to 10.50.12.60 with an artificially extended TTL. Post-flush validation via dig from 10.20.41.77 (WORKSTATION-PC-MD) and 10.20.41.93 (trivera's host) confirmed stale resolver state was the active fault.

root_cause: bind-resolver-01 was serving stale cached DNS data for corp.local due to an outdated DNS update policy reference and cache entries that were not invalidated after the authoritative record changed, causing intermittent NXDOMAIN and old A record responses despite the authoritative zone being correct.

steps: Verified the authoritative corp.local zone on ns-auth-01.corp.local contained the correct A record (10.50.12.88) for service1.corp.local and corrected the record where needed so the source of truth matched the intended service IP.

Reviewed the resolver configuration on bind-resolver-01 (10.20.5.12) and updated the outdated DNS update policy reference in /etc/bind/named.conf.options contributing to stale response behavior, as identified by Priya Nair.
Flushed the DNS cache on bind-resolver-01 via rndc flush and restarted the named service to remove stale NXDOMAIN and old A record entries (10.50.12.60) for service1.corp.local.

Queried service1.corp.local from the resolver and from affected internal hosts — including WORKSTATION-PC-MD (mdelgado, 10.20.41.77) and trivera's workstation (10.20.41.93) — to confirm the resolver now returned the same current address 10.50.12.88 as the authoritative zone.

Confirmed dependent service checks and Network Monitoring alerts cleared after cache refresh and configuration correction, with hostname resolution for service1.corp.local remaining stable across all queried clients in the Charlotte office.

correspondence.message: Multiple users are seeing internal-app.example.corp fail intermittently; repeated nslookup from workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (10.22.14.87) returns either NXDOMAIN or the old IP 10.0.2.5 after the recent DNS change. Rachel Nguyen and Kevin Park both confirmed the issue from their machines in the Charlotte office. Kevin's workstation WORKSTATION-DESKTOP-KP at 10.22.14.92 shows the same behavior.

The internal zone now has the corrected A record and dns-resolver-01 was flushed, but monitoring still shows several downstream resolvers serving 10.0.2.5, indicating stale cache outside the primary resolver. I checked from dns-resolver-02 in the Raleigh data center and confirmed stale responses there as well. David Kowalski (dkowalski) confirmed the zone change was committed at 17:45 UTC but propagation did not complete uniformly.

TTL was temporarily reduced and targeted cache purge requests were sent to known forwarders and edge resolvers; we are validating that all resolver paths now return the updated record consistently. Marcus Hale from the network operations team is coordinating the flush across the Raleigh and Charlotte resolver tiers. Users rnguyen and kpark have been asked to verify resolution from their endpoints after the purge.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the authoritative internal DNS zone contained the corrected record, but downstream forwarders and resolver caches were not uniformly refreshed after the recent change by dkowalski. This caused intermittent NXDOMAIN and stale-IP responses depending on which resolver handled the request. Workstations in the Charlotte office, including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (10.22.14.87) and WORKSTATION-DESKTOP-KP (10.22.14.92), exhibited the failure pattern. Cache flushes and propagation checks resolved the inconsistency.

steps.observed_result: Repeated lookups from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (10.22.14.87) returned mixed results, including intermittent NXDOMAIN and the old IP 10.0.2.5, while the updated record was present on the primary path via dns-resolver-01.
steps.evidence: User reports from rnguyen and kpark, along with Network Monitoring dashboards, showed inconsistent answers across resolvers. nslookup traces from 10.22.14.87 alternated between NXDOMAIN and 10.0.2.5 over a 10-minute window.

steps.action: Inspect the internal DNS zone record, TTL, and recent change history for internal-app.example.corp.
steps.expected_result: Zone contains the current record with expected TTL.
steps.observed_result: The internal zone had the corrected A record (pointing to 10.0.3.20) after the recent change committed by dkowalski at 17:45 UTC; SOA serial was incremented to 2026010902 and TTL was reduced to accelerate propagation.
steps.evidence: Agent Marcus Hale confirmed the zone update on the authoritative side by querying the SOA and A records directly against the primary internal DNS zone server.

steps.action: Check forwarder and downstream resolver cache behavior and flush stale entries where outdated responses persist.
steps.expected_result: Forwarder routes the zone correctly and cache returns fresh data.
steps.observed_result: Several forwarders and edge resolvers, particularly those serving the Raleigh and Charlotte sites, continued serving cached 10.0.2.5 until purge requests were performed; responses normalized afterward.
steps.evidence: Network Monitoring identified resolvers outside dns-resolver-01 still returning stale answers. dns-resolver-02 and dns-resolver-04 in Raleigh were confirmed stale via dig queries run by mhale.

root_cause: After the A record change for internal-app.example.corp, some DNS resolvers and forwarders continued serving cached stale data, and some queries returned NXDOMAIN during inconsistent propagation because not all downstream caches had refreshed from the updated internal zone.

steps: Verified the current A record for internal-app.example.corp in the internal DNS zone, confirmed the intended target address 10.0.3.20, and incremented the zone SOA serial to 2026010902 so downstream resolvers could detect the update. Change was originally committed by David Kowalski (EMP-40291).
Temporarily lowered the record TTL to 60 seconds to reduce cache persistence and speed propagation of the corrected DNS response across all resolver tiers including Charlotte and Raleigh.

Flushed cache on the primary resolver dns-resolver-01 and requested targeted cache purges on known forwarding and edge resolvers (dns-resolver-02, dns-resolver-04) that were still observed returning 10.0.2.5. Marcus Hale coordinated the flush operations.

Validated resolution from multiple resolver paths until queries consistently returned the updated address 10.0.3.20 and no longer returned NXDOMAIN or the stale IP. Confirmation obtained from rnguyen (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN) and kpark (WORKSTATION-DESKTOP-KP).

Continued monitoring after cache purge activity and closed the incident once observed resolvers were serving the same current record consistently. Final validation performed by Marcus Hale at 19:45 UTC with no further anomalies detected.

correspondence.message: Hi Marcus — can you confirm whether the Internal Portal service IP changed recently (we show a migration was scheduled for internal-portal.company.local last weekend) and whether users in both the Chicago and Atlanta offices are seeing NXDOMAIN or an old address (10.22.4.17)? Also, could you or someone from your team run 'nslookup internal-portal.company.local dns-res-east-01.corp.local' and share the output so we can compare resolver behavior? Please reach out to me at n.okafor@corplabs.com or ext 4-7823 if it's easier to discuss live.

Yes, the issue is affecting both the Chicago and Atlanta offices — I confirmed with Priya Nair (priya.nair, EMP-51087) in Atlanta that her lookups from WORKSTATION-LT-PN at 10.40.12.55 return the old IP 10.22.4.17, while my queries here in Chicago return NXDOMAIN. Monitoring Dashboard started showing elevated DNS errors around 08:15 this morning. The portal migration to 10.22.8.40 was completed Saturday night per the change ticket, so the old IP should no longer be in use.

Thanks Marcus. Authoritative zone review on zone master dns-auth-01.corp.local shows the internal-portal.company.local A record was never updated after the migration — it still pointed to 10.22.4.17 with a TTL of 86400 seconds. That explains the mixed stale-IP and NXDOMAIN behavior across recursive resolvers: Chicago's resolver had the negative cache entry from a brief zone reload gap, while Atlanta's resolver was still serving the cached stale record. I'm correcting the A record to 10.22.8.40 now and will coordinate cache flushes with the network team. — Nkem Okafor, Network Engineering

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed this was not an application outage but a DNS data consistency issue following the weekend portal IP migration from 10.22.4.17 to 10.22.8.40. Cross-resolver testing from Chicago (dns-res-east-01.corp.local) and Atlanta (dns-res-east-02.corp.local) showed intermittent NXDOMAIN and stale-IP responses for internal-portal.company.local, while zone inspection on dns-auth-01.corp.local identified an outdated authoritative A record with a TTL of 86400s that was never updated post-migration. Clearing resolver caches after correcting the zone record restored consistent name resolution across both sites.

correspondence.message: Hi Maria — we are checking the internal DNS path for internal-service.local from the corp-dc-east resolver infrastructure. Can you confirm whether the intermittent failures are only being reported by users in the Denver office, and whether the issue started after the application migration on 2026-01-09? Also, could you let us know if you're seeing the same behavior from other machines on the 10.20.0.0/16 subnet? — Kevin Briggs, Network Operations

Yes, reports are from Denver office users. The failures started right after the migration on the 9th, and some lookups return the old address 10.10.5.3 while others fail to resolve the name entirely with NXDOMAIN. I checked with my colleague Raj Patel (rpatel@corplabs.com) on the same floor and he's seeing the same thing from his machine WORKSTATION-RP3087. My workstation IP is 10.20.14.55 if that helps with tracing.

Thanks for confirming, Maria. Testing from dc-resolver1.corplabs.internal shows the primary resolver and caching forwarders fw-resolver1 and fw-resolver2 are intermittently serving stale data for internal-service.local, including the old A record (10.10.5.3) and occasional NXDOMAIN. The correct post-migration address should be 10.10.7.18. We are proceeding with cache flushes on all affected resolvers and validation of the updated zone record. I'll update you once resolution is confirmed. — Kevin Briggs

Comparison testing showed inconsistent answers from the affected resolver path versus the intended current record. Queries from Maria Castillo's workstation (10.20.14.55) and Raj Patel's workstation alternated between the stale A record, NXDOMAIN, and timeouts. Cache-clearing tests confirmed stale resolver and forwarder cache state as the source of the issue.

steps: Validated the internal DNS zone entry for internal-service.local on the Internal DNS Zone and updated the A record to the correct post-migration IP address 10.10.7.18 (previously 10.10.5.3), ensuring the SOA serial was incremented.

Flushed DNS cache on the primary resolver dc-resolver1 and on caching forwarders fw-resolver1 and fw-resolver2 to remove stale responses for internal-service.local. Executed by Kevin Briggs (kbriggs, Network Operations).

Adjusted internal zone refresh interval from 3600 to 900 seconds and reduced default TTL policy to 300 seconds to reduce the likelihood and duration of stale-cache behavior after future service IP changes.

Verified successful name resolution from multiple client subnets (10.20.0.0/16, 10.21.0.0/16), including workstations WORKSTATION-MC2041 (Maria Castillo) and WORKSTATION-RP3087 (Raj Patel), confirming consistent responses to the current address 10.10.7.18 with no further NXDOMAIN results.

The conditional forwarder on dns-resolver-east-04 appears to be routing the example.com zone through an outdated upstream path.

Flushed caches on primary internal resolvers dns-resolver-east-01 and dns-resolver-east-02 and reloaded DNS service via rndc flush. Some lookups now return 10.2.3.50, but mixed responses remain from downstream resolvers dns-resolver-east-04 and dns-resolver-south-01. User Priya Nair (pnair) confirmed she can now resolve correctly from her workstation WORKSTATION-LT-PNAIR (10.50.17.63), but Marcus Reeves in Charlotte still sees the old address intermittently. Additional cache clears and forwarder review are in progress—contacted network engineer David Cho (dcho@corplabs.com) to assist with the downstream resolver configuration.

After downstream cache clears on dns-resolver-east-04 and dns-resolver-south-01, and conditional forwarder review completed by David Cho (dcho), validation from multiple locations—Charlotte, Raleigh, and the us-east-1 monitoring endpoints—returned 10.2.3.50 consistently. Temporary TTL reduction from 3600s to 300s was applied to the internal-service.example.com A record to limit recurrence during future record changes. Marcus Reeves (mreeves) and Priya Nair (pnair) both confirmed resolution is now stable from their respective offices.

correspondence.message: Hi Priya — please run `dig @10.12.4.10 api.internal.corp A` from both APPNODE-PRD-01 (10.20.31.44) and APPNODE-PRD-02 (10.20.31.45), attach /etc/resolv.conf from both affected hosts, and confirm whether the NXDOMAIN response is coming only from the internal resolver path. Also, can you verify whether your teammate Raj Menon on the AppTeam cluster sees the same behavior from his workstation WORKSTATION-RM-PC? Please send results to dns-ops@corplabs.com so we can correlate. — Kevin Albrecht, Network Operations

Kevin — both app servers (APPNODE-PRD-01 and APPNODE-PRD-02) are using the corporate resolver 10.12.4.10 per resolv.conf. Repeated `dig` tests from my workstation WORKSTATION-PNAIR still show intermittent NXDOMAIN from that resolver, while the alternate resolver 8.8.8.8 returns A records (10.20.50.12) for api.internal.corp. Raj confirmed the same intermittent failure from his side. Attaching dig output and resolv.conf from both hosts. — Priya Nair (pnair)

Resolver-side DNS handling was corrected for the internal.corp zone on the corporate resolver (10.12.4.10). The conditional forwarder entry for internal.corp was updated to point to the authoritative nameserver ns1.internal.corp (10.12.4.20), and stale negative cache entries were flushed. Follow-up queries from APPNODE-PRD-01, APPNODE-PRD-02, and Priya's workstation WORKSTATION-PNAIR now return the expected A record (10.20.50.12) consistently with no further NXDOMAIN observed. — Kevin Albrecht

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics established that the failure was isolated to the corporate DNS resolution path (resolver 10.12.4.10) rather than the application endpoint itself. Cross-resolver testing from hosts APPNODE-PRD-01 (10.20.31.44) and APPNODE-PRD-02 (10.20.31.45) showed the affected hosts received intermittent NXDOMAIN from the internal resolver while the public resolver 8.8.8.8 returned valid A records (10.20.50.12). With no confirmed recent zone deletion and a pattern matching resolver-side inconsistency, the issue was attributed to a missing conditional forwarder for the internal.corp zone and stale negative cache entries on the corporate DNS infrastructure. After resolver configuration correction and cache clearing, repeat lookups from affected hosts and user workstation WORKSTATION-PNAIR returned consistent records.

steps.action: Review conditional forwarder configuration for the internal zone on the corporate resolver and flush stale cache entries if negative caching is suspected.
steps.expected_result: Forwarder routes the zone correctly and cache returns fresh data.
steps.observed_result: Symptom pattern aligned with a missing conditional forwarder for the internal.corp zone on the corporate resolver 10.12.4.10; the resolver was attempting recursive resolution externally rather than forwarding to ns1.internal.corp (10.12.4.20). Additionally, stale negative cache entries from prior failed lookups were being served. Cache flush and forwarding configuration correction restored consistent answers.
steps.evidence: Intermittent internal NXDOMAIN combined with successful alternate resolution is consistent with resolver forwarding or cache-state fault. Forwarder configuration dump on 10.12.4.10 showed no conditional forwarder entry for the internal.corp zone, causing fallback to root-hint recursion which returned NXDOMAIN for the private namespace.

root_cause: Internal DNS resolution for api.internal.corp was impacted by stale or incorrect resolver-side handling of the zone, most likely a missing or incorrect conditional forwarder and/or cached negative response on the corporate resolver path. The symptom pattern of intermittent NXDOMAIN from the internal resolver while another resolver returned A records is consistent with resolver configuration or cache state rather than an application issue.

steps: Reviewed the internal DNS zone on authoritative nameserver ns1.internal.corp (10.12.4.20) and confirmed the expected A record for api.internal.corp (10.20.50.12) and its TTL of 300 seconds were present and current.

Corrected the resolver path for the internal.corp zone by adding the missing conditional forwarder configuration on the corporate DNS resolver 10.12.4.10, pointing internal.corp queries to the authoritative nameserver ns1.internal.corp (10.12.4.20) to handle affected app-server queries.

Cleared stale DNS cache entries, including any negative cached NXDOMAIN responses for api.internal.corp, on the affected internal resolver 10.12.4.10 using `rndc flush` and instructed cache flush (`systemd-resolve --flush-caches`) on the impacted application hosts APPNODE-PRD-01 and APPNODE-PRD-02.

Change performed by Priya Nair (pnair) and verified via zone transfer to ns2.corp.local.

Reloaded the authoritative nameserver ns1.corp.local using rndc reload corp.local and verified the authoritative response returned the expected current A record 10.10.8.33 and updated zone serial 2026011201 from multiple query sources.

Flushed cached entries on the primary internal resolvers dns-resolver-west.corp.local and dns-resolver-west-02.corp.local using rndc flush and restarted named resolver services where cache state did not clear cleanly. Performed by Rachel Dominguez (rdominguez) with confirmation from Network Monitoring dashboards.

Cleared local stub resolver caches on affected application hosts (FINAPI-PROD-01, build runner at 10.22.4.102) and test client workstations WORKSTATION-DEV-MJ and WORKSTATION-QA-TR using systemd-resolve --flush-caches to remove stale hostname data held outside the central DNS resolvers.

Validated resolution from affected paths with repeat lookups (50 iterations) against both resolver and authoritative sources from hosts in Portland and Seattle, then confirmed finance-api application smoke tests passed with HTTP 200 responses. Monitored DNS query alerts in Network Monitoring for 24 hours with no recurrence. Final sign-off by Marcus Jennings (mjennings) and Tomás Reyes (treyes).

correspondence.message: Hi Marcus — please compare nslookup or dig results for api.internal.company.local using the corporate DNS resolver (dns-corp-01.infra.company.local) and a known-good public resolver such as 8.8.8.8, and confirm whether the failure is NXDOMAIN, timeout, or no answer at each affected site. If possible, run the test from your workstation (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD) and ask Priya Nair (pnair) in the Chicago office to do the same so we can compare results across locations. Please include the full nslookup output and your client IP.

From multiple office locations, corporate DNS returns NXDOMAIN and sometimes times out for api.internal.company.local, while a public resolver returns 10.200.5.34. I ran nslookup from my machine (10.42.17.88, Austin office) and got NXDOMAIN. Priya Nair confirmed the same behavior from her workstation WORKSTATION-PC-PN at 10.38.22.115 in Chicago. Kevin Ortiz (kortiz) in Portland also reported intermittent timeouts from 10.55.9.201. We do not have resolver cache dumps or additional zone history attached yet.

Network/DNS review by the Infrastructure DNS team (lead: Raj Subramanian, rsubramanian) indicates inconsistent internal resolver handling for the company.local namespace across corporate resolvers dns-corp-01.infra.company.local and dns-corp-02.infra.company.local. We validated the internal record path for api.internal.company.local (expected A record: 10.200.5.34, TTL 300), corrected the conditional forwarder configuration on dns-corp-02 which was missing the company.local zone delegation, and cleared resolver cache on both servers to remove stale NXDOMAIN responses. Resolution confirmed from Austin, Chicago, and Portland client subnets.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics showed a resolver-path discrepancy: affected corporate DNS servers (dns-corp-01.infra.company.local and dns-corp-02.infra.company.local) intermittently returned NXDOMAIN or timeouts for api.internal.company.local while public DNS (8.8.8.8) still resolved the name to 10.200.5.34. Testing was performed from client IPs in the Austin (10.42.17.88), Chicago (10.38.22.115), and Portland (10.55.9.201) offices. Available intake evidence did not prove a recent zone edit issue, so the strongest fit was inconsistent internal DNS handling caused by stale cache on dns-corp-01 and a missing conditional forwarder on dns-corp-02 for the company.local namespace. Remediation focused on validating the internal A record, correcting resolver forwarding behavior on dns-corp-02, and clearing stale resolver cache on both servers.

root_cause: Corporate DNS resolution for api.internal.company.local was intermittently failing because the internal zone/conditional forwarding path was not consistently returning the authoritative record across corporate resolvers, leading some resolvers to answer NXDOMAIN from stale or incorrect cache/forwarding state while public lookup still returned an address.

steps: Validated the authoritative A record for api.internal.company.local in the intended internal DNS zone (company.local) and corrected the record TTL to the current expected value of 300 seconds, confirming the record pointed to 10.200.5.34.

Reviewed corporate DNS resolver handling for company.local on dns-corp-01.infra.company.local and dns-corp-02.infra.company.local, and corrected the conditional forwarder/zone routing on dns-corp-02 (which was missing the company.local delegation) so queries for the internal namespace were sent to the proper authoritative path.

Flushed cache on impacted corporate DNS resolvers (dns-corp-01 and dns-corp-02) to remove stale NXDOMAIN or outdated entries being intermittently served to the Austin, Chicago, and Portland office locations.

Retested name resolution from affected corporate resolver paths — mdelgado (10.42.17.88, Austin), pnair (10.38.22.115, Chicago), and kortiz (10.55.9.201, Portland) — and confirmed api.internal.company.local returned the expected address 10.200.5.34 instead of NXDOMAIN.

Documented the need to capture resolver cache output and comparative nslookup/dig results from multiple sites (including client IPs and resolver targets) if symptoms recur, to distinguish cache poisoning/staleness from future forwarding drift. Added monitoring alert in Network Monitoring for NXDOMAIN spike detection on api.internal.company.local.

correspondence.message: Several engineers — myself (Raj Patel, rpatel), Lina Chen (lchen), and Marco DeSilva (mdesilva) — are seeing intermittent failures resolving service.internal.company.com since 08:30 UTC this morning. We're all in the Newark office on the Engineering VLAN. Direct IP access to 10.22.4.87 still works, but nslookup against corp-resolver-01 from my workstation WORKSTATION-THINKPAD-RP (10.10.52.118) is returning the old address 10.22.4.50. Lina confirmed the same behavior from her machine at 10.10.52.134. Our CI/CD jobs are failing because they rely on hostname resolution. Can someone from the network team take a look?

Checked corp-resolver-01 and confirmed it is serving a stale cached A record (10.22.4.50) for service.internal.company.com instead of the current address 10.22.4.87. Ran dig @corp-resolver-01 service.internal.company.com and the response TTL was still high, suggesting the record was cached before the recent address change. This points to resolver or zone freshness rather than an application outage. Assigning to myself, Tomás Rivera (trivera), for remediation. I've also looped in Priya Nair (pnair) from the DNS zone management team to validate the authoritative record.

Flushed the resolver cache on corp-resolver-01 using rndc flush and forced a reload of the Internal DNS Zone via rndc reload internal.company.com, then revalidated the authoritative A record. The zone serial was advanced from 2026011301 to 2026011302 to ensure downstream propagation. Clients now resolve service.internal.company.com to the updated IP 10.22.4.87. Confirmed with Raj Patel (rpatel) and Lina Chen (lchen) that resolution is working correctly from their workstations. Network Monitoring dashboards show no further NXDOMAIN or stale-address responses. Closing the incident.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics isolated the issue to internal DNS resolution rather than service reachability because direct IP access to 10.22.4.87 remained healthy while hostname queries from engineering workstations (e.g., WORKSTATION-THINKPAD-RP at 10.10.52.118, reported by rpatel) intermittently returned NXDOMAIN or the outdated address 10.22.4.50. Investigation of corp-resolver-01 by Tomás Rivera (trivera) identified a stale cached A record with an unexpired TTL, and validation of the Internal DNS Zone by Priya Nair (pnair) confirmed the need to reload and correct zone data — the zone serial had not been incremented after the service IP migration. After cache flush and zone refresh, resolution returned the updated address 10.22.4.87 consistently from Network Monitoring probes and client systems in the Newark datacenter.

correspondence.message: Multiple app teams confirm service1.company.local intermittently returns NXDOMAIN or times out for 30-60 seconds, while the host is still reachable by IP at 10.42.18.61 and monitoring shows resolver latency spikes before the failures. Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) first noticed the issue around 00:15 UTC when his deployment pipeline on WORKSTATION-LNX-MD failed to connect to the service endpoint. Priya Nair from the frontend team also reported identical symptoms from her workstation WORKSTATION-LNX-PN at 10.42.22.95.

Resolver query logs on dns-resolver-east-01 show cached A record data for service1.company.local pointing to the old address 10.42.18.40 rather than the current 10.42.18.61 in the internal zone file, indicating the internal resolver is serving a stale entry after the recent record update. Network engineer Raj Kapoor (rkapoor) confirmed the mismatch by querying the resolver directly and comparing against the authoritative zone. The zone change was committed at 2026-01-13T23:48:00Z but the resolver never picked up the new record due to the long TTL on the cached entry.

Flushed the internal DNS resolver cache on dns-resolver-east-01, verified the zone record for service1.company.local now returns 10.42.18.61 with the corrected TTL of 300s, and retested from the resolver path and application hosts. Raj Kapoor (rkapoor) confirmed resolution now returns the correct address consistently during validation from both Marcus Delgado's host WORKSTATION-LNX-MD and Priya Nair's host WORKSTATION-LNX-PN. Application connectivity checks by the platform team passed without further NXDOMAIN or timeout events.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the outage was resolver-side rather than host-side: the authoritative internal zone had the intended updated A record (10.42.18.61), but the internal resolver on dns-resolver-east-01 intermittently served stale cached data (old address 10.42.18.40) and produced NXDOMAIN/timeouts. Cache flush restored correct answers immediately, and subsequent validation from application hosts including WORKSTATION-LNX-MD (Marcus Delgado) and WORKSTATION-LNX-PN (Priya Nair) and monitoring confirmed stable resolution. Conditional forwarder behavior remains a follow-up review item assigned to Raj Kapoor (rkapoor), but the immediate incident was caused by stale resolver cache after the zone update.

root_cause: The internal DNS resolver served a stale cached A record for service1.company.local after a recent zone update, causing intermittent mismatches between resolver cache contents and the current internal zone data and resulting in NXDOMAIN responses and lookup timeouts until the cache was flushed.

steps: Reviewed the authoritative internal DNS zone for service1.company.local, corrected the A record to match the current endpoint address (10.42.18.61), and confirmed the zone data reflected the intended value. Raj Kapoor (rkapoor) performed the verification against the zone file on the authoritative server.
Flushed the internal DNS resolver cache on dns-resolver-east-01 to remove the stale cached entry (10.42.18.40) that was being returned instead of the updated zone record.

Retested name resolution from the affected resolver path and from application hosts including WORKSTATION-LNX-MD and WORKSTATION-LNX-PN to confirm service1.company.local consistently returned the current address without NXDOMAIN or timeout responses.

Validated recovery through monitoring and application connectivity checks to confirm resolver latency normalized and the service was reachable by name. Marcus Delgado and Priya Nair both confirmed their applications reconnected successfully.
Adjusted the DNS TTL from 86400s to 300s to reduce the likelihood and duration of stale-cache impact after future record changes.

Documented follow-up review of conditional forwarder behavior to ensure the resolver refreshes the internal zone correctly after updates. Follow-up ticket assigned to Raj Kapoor (rkapoor, EMP-30157) for completion by 2026-01-21.

correspondence.message: Can you compare svc-api.internal.corp from a few affected workstations and a known-good resolver? Users like Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) and Raj Patel (rpatel) are seeing either NXDOMAIN or an older IP depending on where they test. Maria's workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC at 10.14.22.87 gets NXDOMAIN, while Raj's machine at 10.14.23.41 returns the stale 10.2.3.4 address. Please check from both dns-res-01.internal.corp and dns-res-02.internal.corp.

Resolver checks show the A record age at 14 days on the primary zone server dns-auth-01.internal.corp, two DC resolvers (DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal and DC-EAST-04.corplabs.internal) are missing the conditional forwarder to corp-ad, and Network Monitoring recorded SERVFAIL spikes at 10:12 and 10:25 UTC. I ran nslookup from the workstations reported by mchen and rpatel — confirmed NXDOMAIN from DC-EAST-04 and stale 10.2.3.4 from dns-res-02. The forwarder gap explains why queries routed through those DCs never reached the authoritative zone. Assigning to network_team lead Tomás Rivera (trivera) for remediation.

Updated the authoritative A record on dns-auth-01.internal.corp to the current service IP 10.2.7.15, flushed resolver caches on dns-res-01 and dns-res-02, and applied the missing forwarder settings on DC-EAST-03 and DC-EAST-04. Follow-up nslookup tests from mchen's workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (10.14.22.87) and rpatel's endpoint (10.14.23.41) now return the correct address. Remaining outliers likely due to endpoint-side DNS cache retention — notified the Newark internal-devs team via Slack to flush local caches.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the incident was not isolated to a single client. Query comparison from workstations belonging to mchen (10.14.22.87) and rpatel (10.14.23.41) showed mixed NXDOMAIN and stale-record responses across resolver paths through dns-res-01.internal.corp and dns-res-02.internal.corp. Internal DNS Zone inspection found the svc-api.internal.corp A record on dns-auth-01.internal.corp had gone stale (last updated 14 days prior), and DNS Resolver review identified missing conditional forwarders on DC-EAST-03 and DC-EAST-04. After correcting the authoritative record to 10.2.7.15, flushing caches, and aligning forwarder configuration, resolution behavior became consistent aside from short-lived client cache persistence on a handful of Newark endpoints.

root_cause: Inconsistent DNS resolver state caused intermittent failures: the authoritative record had been stale, some resolvers continued serving cached old data, and two domain controller resolvers were missing the required conditional forwarder for the corp-ad path, resulting in mixed NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, and stale-address responses depending on which resolver answered the query.

steps: Updated the authoritative A record for svc-api.internal.corp on dns-auth-01.internal.corp from the stale 10.2.3.4 to the correct current IP 10.2.7.15, and verified the Internal DNS Zone data reflected the intended value and a TTL of 300s. Change performed by Tomás Rivera (trivera).

Flushed DNS caches on the primary and secondary internal resolvers (dns-res-01.internal.corp and dns-res-02.internal.corp) using dnscmd /clearcache so they would stop serving the previously cached 10.2.3.4 address.

Added and standardized the missing conditional forwarder configuration on the two domain controller resolvers DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal and DC-EAST-04.corplabs.internal so all resolvers used the same resolution path for the internal.corp zone via corp-ad.

Validated resolution from multiple resolver paths and client perspectives — confirmed correct 10.2.7.15 response from mchen's workstation (10.14.22.87), rpatel's endpoint (10.14.23.41), and three additional Newark developer machines to confirm the hostname no longer returned mixed NXDOMAIN or stale-address results.

Requested affected teams in Newark to clear local DNS caches on impacted endpoints (ipconfig /flushdns) and monitored Network Monitoring dashboards for recurrence until lookup failures and stale responses subsided. Final confirmation received from Maria Chen at 10:15 UTC.

Monitoring alerts for the api.internal.corp endpoint cleared within 3 minutes of the secondary flush.

correspondence.message: Users in several office locations — Portland and Sacramento in particular — and some application hosts are getting intermittent NXDOMAIN for internal-service.internal.corp, and the service times out when they try to reach it by name. I'm Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com), and my workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD at 10.42.16.55 has been failing lookups since about 07:30 UTC this morning. Colleagues Priya Nair and Jason Whitfield on the same floor are seeing the same behavior.

Inspection of the Internal DNS Zone found the A record for internal-service.internal.corp still pointed to the decommissioned host app-legacy-07 (10.42.8.12), which was taken offline on 2026-01-13. The current service endpoint is hosted on app-prod-03 at 10.42.8.45. This would explain the failed lookups and stale responses being served by internal resolvers DNS-RES-W1-01 and DNS-RES-W1-02. Verified by network engineer rchen who queried the zone directly.

Performed a cache flush on the primary resolver DNS-RES-W1-01 as a short-term mitigation and prepared the corrected A record update (10.42.8.12 → 10.42.8.45) plus cluster-wide cache clearing across DNS-RES-W1-01 and DNS-RES-W1-02 to restore consistent resolution. Post-flush, confirmed lookups from Marcus Delgado's workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD and from deployment-service nodes now return the correct address. Monitoring via Network Monitoring dashboard shows no further NXDOMAIN events.

correspondence.message: Users and monitoring across us-east started seeing NXDOMAIN and occasional lookup timeouts for internal-app.service.local around 06:15 UTC. Marcus Delgado (EMP-90234) first flagged the issue from his workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.22.4.87) when the Internal Portal returned connection errors. I confirmed the same behavior from my machine at 10.22.5.12 — nslookup internal-app.service.local against both resolver-01.dns.corp.internal and resolver-02.dns.corp.internal alternates between NXDOMAIN and a stale 10.40.1.15 answer. The application cannot reach the service by hostname.

Inspection of resolver-01.dns.corp.internal and resolver-02.dns.corp.internal found stale cached data for internal-app.service.local, including an outdated A record pointing to the decommissioned IP 10.40.1.15 instead of the current 10.40.2.30. I logged into the authoritative zone master (ns-auth-01.dns.corp.internal) and confirmed the zone file was updated during last week's migration by Priya Nair (pnair), but the TTL on the old record was set to 86400 seconds, which allowed the resolvers to hold onto the stale entry well past the change window. I am validating the authoritative zone and cache behavior now. Network Monitoring shows intermittent failures from probes in the Newark and Ashburn datacenters.

Cleared the affected resolver caches on resolver-01.dns.corp.internal and resolver-02.dns.corp.internal using rndc flush and refreshed the DNS resolver service on resolver-01 where persistent cached data was observed. Then re-queried the hostname from multiple endpoints — Marcus Delgado's workstation (10.22.4.87), the QA jump host at 10.22.6.50, and external monitoring probes — to confirm the updated zone record (10.40.2.30) is being returned consistently. All lookups now resolve correctly. Closing coordination with Priya Nair on the TTL policy update.

steps: Compared responses from the primary resolver dns-resolver-01.internal.corp (10.40.2.10) and the authoritative internal DNS server ns-auth-01.internal.corp to confirm the resolver was returning stale data (10.40.50.18) for payroll-svc.internal.corp instead of the current record (10.40.50.22).

correspondence.message: App team (Marcus Delgado, m.delgado@corplabs.com) is seeing intermittent failures resolving app-service.internal in prod-east. Monitoring shows bursts of NXDOMAIN and some responses still returning old IP 192.0.2.45. Affected clients include WORKSTATION-DEV-KP (10.40.12.87, user kpatel) and several hosts on the 10.40.12.0/24 subnet. Marcus reports the issue started around 17:30 UTC today and is impacting the App Platform group's deployment pipeline.

Checked the internal DNS zone (managed by dns-admin rchen, Ravi Chen) and found a duplicate stale A record for app-service.internal pointing to 192.0.2.45. Resolver cache on dns-resolver-01.corplabs.internal is also serving 192.0.2.45, which matches the intermittent behavior reported by Marcus. Cross-referenced with zone change log — the stale record appears to have been left behind after a migration on 2026-01-10 and was not cleaned up. dns-resolver-02.corplabs.internal cache shows the same stale entry.

Removed the stale zone entry (performed by rchen on the Internal DNS Zone console), lowered TTL from 3600 to 300 seconds, and flushed resolver caches on dns-resolver-01.corplabs.internal and dns-resolver-02.corplabs.internal. Subsequent queries from WORKSTATION-DEV-KP (10.40.12.87) and other client hosts are returning the correct A record (10.40.8.20) consistently. Confirmed with Marcus Delgado that the app-service endpoint is now reachable. Closing ticket per SLA Gold-InternalDNS.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the issue was not an application defect but an internal DNS data and cache inconsistency affecting the Ashburn prod-east environment. The hostname app-service.internal intermittently returned NXDOMAIN or the retired IP 192.0.2.45 due to a duplicate stale A record in the internal zone (left from a migration on 2026-01-10) and cached stale resolver data on dns-resolver-01.corplabs.internal and dns-resolver-02.corplabs.internal. After rchen removed the stale record, lowered TTL to 300s, and flushed resolver caches, resolution normalized across monitoring and client hosts including WORKSTATION-DEV-KP (kpatel, 10.40.12.87).

steps: Reviewed the internal DNS zone for app-service.internal (zone managed by dns-admin rchen) and identified the duplicate stale A record pointing to retired host IP 192.0.2.45, originally associated with decommissioned host WORKSTATION-APPOLD-MD.
Removed the stale DNS entry (performed by rchen via Internal DNS Zone console) and confirmed the authoritative zone retained only the correct A record 10.40.8.20 for app-service.internal.

Flushed DNS cache entries on dns-resolver-01.corplabs.internal and dns-resolver-02.corplabs.internal so cached stale responses (192.0.2.45) would no longer be served to clients such as WORKSTATION-DEV-KP (10.40.12.87).

correspondence.message: svc-inventory.internal.corp intermittently fails to resolve from some subnets since 08:30. The service is reachable by IP, but DNS lookups are timing out and sometimes returning NXDOMAIN. Reported by r.menon (Rajesh Menon, r.menon@corplabs.com, phone 512-884-3091) from the Austin platform engineering group. My workstation WORKSTATION-RMENON-L1 (IP 10.42.16.112) consistently fails lookups while colleagues on other subnets have no issues.

Hi Rajesh — thanks for the detail. Please provide nslookup output from your affected client WORKSTATION-RMENON-L1, including the resolver IP shown, and confirm whether any recent DNS forwarder or internal zone changes were made. I'm assigning this to our network team lead, Patricia Hwang (p.hwang), for further investigation. You can also reach me at d.kowalski@corplabs.com if you have additional logs.

Review by Patricia Hwang (p.hwang, EMP-55190) indicates the A record for svc-inventory.internal.corp exists on the internal zone hosted on DNS-AUTH-02.internal.corp, but the resolver path used by the Austin 10.42.16.0/24 subnet (resolver 10.42.1.12) is not forwarding the internal.corp zone consistently and appears to be serving stale negative cache responses. The conditional forwarder on resolver 10.42.1.12 was last modified on 2025-12-09 and references an outdated authoritative server address.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics showed the hostname issue was limited to DNS resolution and not service reachability, because the service IP 10.42.16.55 was directly reachable from WORKSTATION-RMENON-L1 and other affected hosts. The authoritative record existed on DNS-AUTH-02.internal.corp, while failures varied by subnet and resolver path — specifically the Austin 10.42.16.0/24 subnet using resolver 10.42.1.12 — with timeouts and NXDOMAIN responses. This pattern supports a resolver-side problem involving conditional forwarding and stale cache rather than a missing application record.

Issue affected only the Austin 10.42.16.0/24 subnet and included both timeout and NXDOMAIN responses, matching resolver path/cache inconsistency. After correction by p.hwang, all lookups returned expected results.

root_cause: Intermittent name resolution was caused by an internal DNS resolver path issue affecting some subnets, most consistent with an incorrect or missing conditional forwarder and stale cached responses on one or more internal resolvers for the internal.corp zone.

correspondence.message: Several services and users from the Newark and Richmond offices cannot reach app.internal.corp by name. DNS lookups intermittently return either NXDOMAIN or an old IP address (10.20.30.40). I've confirmed the issue from my workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MCHEN (10.16.4.87) and colleague David Okafor also reports the same behavior from his machine at 10.18.2.33. Affected users include teams in both locations — please advise. Contact me at mchen@corplabs.com or ext 4-7193 if you need more info.

Internal resolver checks from DNS-RES-01 (10.16.0.5) and DNS-RES-02 (10.18.0.5) show inconsistent answers for app.internal.corp compared with the authoritative zone on DNS-AUTH-01. Queries routed through DNS-RES-01 serving the Newark subnet intermittently returned NXDOMAIN, while DNS-RES-02 in Richmond returned the stale A record 10.20.30.40 instead of the current target 10.20.31.15. The zone was last modified on 2026-01-16 at 22:10 UTC by admin user rgarcia, but the resolver caches did not pick up the updated record within the expected TTL window (previously set to 3600s). Network Monitoring alerts corroborate lookup failures from both segments starting at approximately 05:48 UTC.

The DNS A record for app.internal.corp was corrected to 10.20.31.15 on the authoritative zone hosted on DNS-AUTH-01, resolver caches on DNS-RES-01 and DNS-RES-02 were flushed, and the internal.corp zone was reloaded. Follow-up nslookup and dig tests from the affected subnets in Newark (10.16.0.0/16) and Richmond (10.18.0.0/16) now return the current address 10.20.31.15 consistently. Maria Chen and David Okafor both confirmed application connectivity is restored from their workstations. Closing the ticket — please reopen if the issue recurs.

The zone had been updated by rgarcia on 2026-01-16 at 22:10 UTC but the high TTL (3600s) and a cache inconsistency prevented timely propagation. Updating the zone record, flushing resolver caches, and reloading the zone restored consistent resolution to the correct address 10.20.31.15 across all affected segments.
