correspondence.message: Hi, this is Marco Kessler (mkessler@corplabs.com). My laptop LAPTOP-SALES-MK is showing noncompliant for encryption in Intune. BitLocker says 'Protection Off' and 'Encryption: None' on the OS volume. I cannot find any recovery key in the Device Compliance Service portal. I've already restarted the machine and triggered an Intune sync from Company Portal, but nothing changed. My manager Petra Lindgren asked me to raise this urgently since I'm unable to access several Field Sales resources due to the compliance block.

Remote checks on LAPTOP-SALES-MK (IP 10.42.17.83) confirm the Endpoint Disk Encryption policy (profile 'FS-Encryption-Win10') is assigned to mkessler's device object in Intune and the last successful check-in was 2026-01-19T09:12Z. However, running manage-bde -status C: remotely shows 'Conversion Status: Fully Decrypted' with zero protectors configured. Because no TPM-based protector was ever initialized on this device, BitLocker could not begin encryption, and the MDM recovery key escrow request returned a failure—'Recovery key escrow attempt failed (MDM escrow response failure)'. The TPM chip itself reports as ready (tpm.msc shows 'The TPM is ready for use', version 2.0), so protector initialization should succeed without hardware issues.

Initialized the TPM protector on LAPTOP-SALES-MK using 'manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm', which completed successfully. Then started BitLocker encryption with 'manage-bde -on C:'. Encryption began on the OS volume and is currently at 100% with protection status 'On'. Forced an Intune sync from the device (dsregcmd /forcerecovery followed by a Company Portal sync), and within a few minutes the recovery key for mkessler's device appeared in the Device Compliance Service portal. Device compliance state has flipped to 'Compliant' in Intune. Notified Marco Kessler at mkessler@corplabs.com that the issue is resolved.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics on WORKSTATION-LATITUDE-MB (user mbellini, IP 10.42.17.83) confirmed the slowdown occurred during the immediate post-login window and was driven by resource contention rather than a single application fault. CPU and disk I/O were abnormally high during startup, the GPO policy push dated 2026-01-27 introduced heavy post-login processing including additional startup scripts, and an Endpoint Protection scan backlog of 14 queued definition updates compounded the impact. The 256 GB SSD had only 8.2 GB free, and temporary file buildup in C:\Windows\Temp and the user profile AppData\Local\Temp further increased disk pressure. root_cause: A recently applied resource-heavy startup policy triggered excessive post-login processing, and an endpoint protection scan backlog ran concurrently, causing sustained CPU and disk I/O contention that delayed application launches and degraded overall laptop responsiveness.

steps: Reviewed startup-impacting processes on the affected laptop WORKSTATION-LATITUDE-MB (user mbellini) and disabled 4 non-essential startup items (including redundant telemetry agents and a legacy inventory scanner) contributing to the post-login CPU spike.

Cleared the Endpoint Protection scan backlog of 14 queued definition updates by rescheduling full scans to off-hours (02:00 local Milan time) and allowing an immediate lighter quick-scan cycle to complete during support handling on mbellini's device.

Removed 11.1 GB of temporary files from C:\Windows\Temp and C:\Users\mbellini\AppData\Local\Temp and reclaimed disk space (free space restored to 19.3 GB) to reduce paging and startup disk contention during user sign-in on WORKSTATION-LATITUDE-MB.

Validated performance after logoff and logon on mbellini's session, then monitored CPU and disk I/O until they returned to normal startup levels (CPU below 25% within 90 seconds, disk queue length < 2) and Marco Bellini confirmed Outlook, Chrome, and the Sales CRM opened normally within 3-5 seconds. steps: Verified that OWA continued to receive new mail for mreeves@corplabs.com, confirming the mailbox was accessible and narrowing the issue to client synchronization on WORKSTATION-MR-7540 and IPHONE-MR-2026 rather than a full Exchange service outage.

Validated that desktop and mobile mail flow resumed for Marcus Reeves after backend throttling reset and compliance follow-up, completing restoration across both affected clients. Confirmed with user at (704) 553-8192 that email was fully operational.

correspondence.message: My Outlook on iPhone and desktop (WORKSTATION-RNGUYEN) stopped syncing this morning. New emails are not appearing in my mailbox rachel.nguyen@corplabs.com, and the desktop client shows Disconnected in the status bar. Last good sync was around 06:30. I'm in the Charlotte office and need this for client-facing communications today.

Exchange Online is not showing throttling for the mailbox rachel.nguyen@corplabs.com (UPN: rnguyen@corplabs.internal). I confirmed the desktop client on WORKSTATION-RNGUYEN at IP 10.42.18.97 is in a disconnected state and the mobile partnership for her iPhone appears unhealthy in the MDM console, so I am resetting the mobile sync relationship and checking reauthentication. Assigning to desktop support contact Marcus Bell for the profile rebuild portion.

After clearing the mobile sync partnership for rnguyen@corplabs.internal and forcing resync via Exchange Online PowerShell, Outlook reauthenticated and headers began updating on WORKSTATION-RNGUYEN, but full folder sync remained incomplete. I proceeded with a desktop profile rebuild under the rnguyen local Windows profile, re-added the Exchange Online account, and then confirmed mailbox sync recovered on both the desktop and the iPhone. Rachel confirmed she can see all recent emails on both devices.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics showed the Outlook desktop client on WORKSTATION-RNGUYEN (IP 10.42.18.97) was in a disconnected state while Exchange Online itself was not throttling the mailbox for rachel.nguyen@corplabs.com. A reauthentication event allowed only partial header sync, which pointed to a stale or corrupted Outlook profile rather than a service outage. In parallel, the mailbox's mobile sync partnership for rnguyen@corplabs.internal and MDM compliance state on the enrolled iPhone were unhealthy. Full service was restored after clearing the mobile partnership, remediating device compliance, and rebuilding the Outlook profile on WORKSTATION-RNGUYEN.

Rebuilt the Outlook desktop profile on WORKSTATION-RNGUYEN under the rnguyen Windows profile and re-added the Exchange Online account (rachel.nguyen@corplabs.com) to remove the stale local profile and cached sync state.

correspondence.message: Hi Karen — please confirm whether all users printing through PS-PRINT01 are seeing jobs stuck in queue or driver unavailable errors, and whether the printer appears offline from their PCs. Can you also verify if users on the 3rd floor like Marcus Jennings (mjennings) are affected as well?

Yes, multiple users are affected. I'm Karen Ostrowski (kostrowski@corpmail.com) and my jobs stay in the queue. The shared HP LaserJet 4250 printer shows offline, and some PCs report driver unavailable or spooler timeout when trying to print. Marcus Jennings on the 3rd floor confirmed the same issue from his workstation WORKSTATION-HP-MJ at 10.47.22.91. I also checked with Diane Pham (dpham) and she's seeing the same behavior.

Checked PS-PRINT01 and confirmed the queue is stalled, the Print Spooler is hanging during job processing, and the HP driver package on the server appears corrupted. Verified affected users include kostrowski, mjennings, and dpham across the Columbus office. Proceeding with driver removal, reinstall, queue cleanup, and spooler restart. — Tech: Rafael Dominguez (rdominguez)

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the issue was not a simple paused queue or isolated client problem. The shared queue on PS-PRINT01 serving the Columbus office was backing up with jobs from multiple users including kostrowski, mjennings, and dpham. The spooler was hanging during job handling, and the installed HP driver package was identified as corrupt. Reinstalling the approved HP Universal Print Driver and resetting the affected queues restored normal print processing.
observed_errors: EventID 7011: Service timeout while waiting for Print Spooler

steps.action: Checked the shared print queue state on PS-PRINT01 to confirm whether jobs were paused, stuck, or failing.
steps.expected_result: Print queue is online and accepts new jobs.
steps.observed_result: Affected HP LaserJet 4250 queue showed 23 accumulated jobs stuck in spooling state — including submissions from kostrowski and mjennings — and clients saw the printer as offline.
steps.evidence: Jobs did not progress and queue backlog continued to grow on PS-PRINT01. Oldest stuck job was submitted by Karen Ostrowski (kostrowski) at 18:42 UTC from workstation WORKSTATION-DELL-KO (10.47.22.85).

steps.action: Compared the installed print driver package on PS-PRINT01 with the approved HP Universal Print Driver version.
steps.expected_result: Endpoint uses the current approved printer driver.
steps.observed_result: Installed HP driver package (v5.6.0.2341) on the server was found to be corrupt and did not reliably support the shared queue. The approved version is HP Universal Print Driver v5.8.
steps.evidence: Driver corruption aligned with client driver unavailable errors and queue mapping instability. Verified by Rafael Dominguez (rdominguez) using Printer Management Console on PS-PRINT01.

steps.action: Reviewed Print Spooler service status and attempted to process a test job through the affected queue.
steps.expected_result: Spooler processes a test job without retry or access errors.
steps.observed_result: Print Spooler became unresponsive while processing the queue and generated timeout behavior until the driver was replaced and jobs were cleared. Test print submitted by rdominguez from 10.47.20.15 failed to complete.
steps.evidence: Observed spooler hang and EventID 7011 service timeout while waiting for Print Spooler. Spooler process consumed 98% CPU on PS-PRINT01 during the hang condition.

root_cause: Corrupt HP printer driver package on PS-PRINT01 caused Print Spooler instability, queue processing failures, and client driver unavailable errors.

steps: Reviewed the affected shared printer queues on PS-PRINT01 and confirmed 23 jobs were accumulating in a spooling state while the printer showed offline to clients across the Columbus office, including submissions from kostrowski, mjennings, and dpham.
Removed the corrupted HP driver package (v5.6.0.2341) from the Windows Server 2019 print server and reinstalled the approved HP Universal Print Driver v5.8 package per the standard driver catalog.

Cleared all stuck jobs from the impacted print queues and restarted the Print Spooler service after the driver refresh. Notified affected users Karen Ostrowski and Marcus Jennings that their pending jobs would need to be resubmitted.

Remapped the affected printer queues to the refreshed HP Universal Print Driver v5.8 package to ensure the queues were bound to the correct server driver. Confirmed queue binding via Printer Management Console.

Validated successful test prints from multiple client machines including WORKSTATION-DELL-KO (kostrowski) and WORKSTATION-HP-MJ (mjennings), and confirmed the spooler remained responsive with no further queue hang behavior. Diane Pham (dpham) also confirmed printing restored at 20:05 UTC.

correspondence.message: Hi Maria — can you confirm whether all affected printers are mapped through PS-PRINT01? Also, are users seeing the same 'Driver unavailable' message in their queue, or only an offline status on the printer icon? If possible, please share the exact printer queue name (e.g., \\PS-PRINT01\NWK-3F-HP4050) that you were printing to when the issue occurred.

Yes, the affected users are all printing through PS-PRINT01. I was sending to \\PS-PRINT01\NWK-3F-HP4050 and Kevin Ostrowski on the same floor was using \\PS-PRINT01\NWK-3F-HP5200. Most of us report jobs stuck in queue at 0%, and on the server the queues show 'Driver unavailable' while the printers look offline from our PCs. I also checked with Raj Patel (rpatel) on the second floor and he has the same problem with \\PS-PRINT01\NWK-2F-HP4050. My workstation is WORKSTATION-PC-MD if that helps.

Reviewed PS-PRINT01 queue and event logs remotely from my workstation (10.22.4.87). The Print Spooler is logging repeated HP Universal driver load failures — Event ID 372 in the Microsoft-Windows-PrintService/Operational log — and restart attempts of the spooler service do not clear the condition. The driver package version 6.9.0.24297 on PS-PRINT01 does not match the current approved version (6.9.0.24300) in the SCCM driver store, and the local driver files appear corrupted (hash mismatch on hpuni197.dll). This confirms a corrupted print driver package on the server is the root cause.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics covered queue state, driver health, and spooler behavior on PS-PRINT01 serving the Newark office. The queue check confirmed jobs from users mdelgado, kostrowski, and rpatel were stuck with 'Driver unavailable' across queues NWK-3F-HP4050, NWK-3F-HP5200, and NWK-2F-HP4050. Driver review and event logs (Event ID 372) tied the failure to a corrupted HP Universal driver package v6.9.0.24297 with a hash mismatch on hpuni197.dll. Spooler testing showed restart alone was insufficient, confirming the driver package itself was the blocking condition. Reinstalling the approved driver v6.9.0.24300, clearing queues, and restarting the spooler restored normal printing for all affected users.
observed_errors: Print Spooler service errors (driver load failures)

steps.action: Checked shared print queues on PS-PRINT01 for paused, stuck, or failing jobs and reviewed queue state across affected printers.
steps.expected_result: Print queue is online and accepts new jobs.
steps.observed_result: Multiple jobs were stuck in queue at 0% across queues \\PS-PRINT01\NWK-3F-HP4050, \\PS-PRINT01\NWK-3F-HP5200, and \\PS-PRINT01\NWK-2F-HP4050. Printers appeared offline to users including mdelgado (WORKSTATION-PC-MD) and kostrowski, and queue entries showed 'Driver unavailable' instead of processing. A total of 23 stalled jobs were identified across the three queues.
steps.evidence: Default and affected shared queues on PS-PRINT01 contained 23 stalled jobs with no progress; queue \\PS-PRINT01\NWK-3F-HP4050 alone had 11 pending documents submitted between 00:12 and 00:45 UTC on 2026-02-22, all at 0% completion with status 'Driver unavailable'.

steps.action: Compared the installed HP Universal driver on PS-PRINT01 with the approved package and reviewed spooler driver load behavior.
steps.expected_result: Endpoint uses the current approved printer driver.
steps.observed_result: The HP Universal package v6.9.0.24297 installed on PS-PRINT01 failed to load in the spooler and was determined to be corrupted — the file hpuni197.dll had a SHA-256 hash mismatch compared to the SCCM source package. The current approved version v6.9.0.24300 was not present on the server, requiring reinstall of the approved package.
steps.evidence: Event logs on PS-PRINT01 reported Print Spooler driver load failures (Event ID 372, source: Microsoft-Windows-PrintService) for the HP Universal driver package. File integrity check showed hpuni197.dll (v6.9.0.24297) hash did not match the expected value in the SCCM deployment manifest.

steps.action: Reviewed Print Spooler service status, restarted the spooler, and tested whether a print job would clear through the queue.
steps.expected_result: Spooler processes a test job without retry or access errors.
steps.observed_result: Before remediation the spooler on PS-PRINT01 produced repeated service errors (Event ID 372) and did not clear queued jobs even after two manual restarts of the Print Spooler service; after driver reinstall to v6.9.0.24300 and queue cleanup, test jobs from WORKSTATION-PC-MD (mdelgado) and kostrowski's workstation printed successfully within seconds.
steps.evidence: Initial restart attempts at 01:00 and 01:02 UTC did not restore processing — spooler continued logging driver load failures. Validation prints from endpoints belonging to mdelgado and rpatel succeeded only after the approved HP Universal driver v6.9.0.24300 was reinstalled and queues were flushed.

root_cause: Corrupted HP Universal printer driver package on PS-PRINT01 caused the Print Spooler to fail loading the driver, leaving shared print jobs stuck with a 'Driver unavailable' state.

steps: Validated that the affected queues on PS-PRINT01 (\\PS-PRINT01\NWK-3F-HP4050, \\PS-PRINT01\NWK-3F-HP5200, \\PS-PRINT01\NWK-2F-HP4050) were failing with the message 'Driver unavailable' and identified the HP Universal driver package v6.9.0.24297 as the common failing component across all three queues.

Reinstalled the approved HP Universal driver package v6.9.0.24300 on PS-PRINT01 through SCCM to replace the corrupted driver files, verifying the SHA-256 hash of hpuni197.dll matched the deployment manifest after installation.

Cleared all 23 stuck print jobs from the affected queues and restarted the Print Spooler service on PS-PRINT01 to reload the corrected driver package cleanly. Confirmed the spooler started without Event ID 372 errors.
Remapped the affected printer queues (NWK-3F-HP4050, NWK-3F-HP5200, NWK-2F-HP4050) to the approved driver package v6.9.0.24300 so queue-to-driver associations were consistent after reinstall.

Submitted validation print jobs from multiple endpoints — WORKSTATION-PC-MD (mdelgado), kostrowski's workstation, and rpatel's workstation — and confirmed the queues processed normally without new spooler driver load failures. All test pages printed within 5 seconds of submission.

Updated the approved printer driver deployment policy in SCCM to pin HP Universal driver v6.9.0.24300 as the mandatory version and added a file-integrity pre-check to prevent the stale or corrupted package v6.9.0.24297 from being redeployed to the print server. Notified the Newark Workplace Services team lead, Sandra Chen (schen@corplabs.com), of the policy update.

correspondence.message: Hi Maria — please confirm whether new print jobs on PDQ-Print01 stay in spooling state for all affected department printers (Sales-Main, HR-Floor2-Queue) or only specific queues. Also, can you or your team lead Kevin Marsh verify whether any recent driver update was pushed to PDQ-Print01? You can reach me at ext. 4127 or at d.nakamura@corplabs.com if you have additional details.

Sales and HR printers are both affected — I checked with Kevin Marsh and also with Priya Reddy from Sales, and new jobs keep sitting in spooling on both \\PDQ-Print01\Sales-Main and \\PDQ-Print01\HR-Floor2-Queue. Restarting the spooler from my workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MG helped briefly, then the same driver unavailable message returned across the shared queues. No one on our side applied any driver updates recently. My username is mgonzalez if you need to check my print history.

Reviewed Windows event logs (Event ID 372 and 808) and driver metadata on PDQ-Print01; found checksum mismatch on the HP Universal Print Driver package v6.9.0 installed under C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\x64\3. Queue mappings for Sales-Main and HR-Floor2-Queue were still tied to the older driver version (v6.7.2), explaining the repeated driver unavailable errors. The corrupt package appears to have been staged during a failed silent update on 2026-02-21. Diagnostics performed from admin session by dnakamura on PDQ-Print01 (10.22.4.55).

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed this was not a simple spooler stall. Queue inspection on PDQ-Print01 (10.22.4.55) showed jobs from users mgonzalez, kmarsh, and preddy continuously stuck in spooling state across Sales-Main and HR-Floor2-Queue. Driver validation showed checksum mismatch on the HP Universal Print Driver package v6.9.0 installed on 2026-02-21, and queue mappings still referenced the older v6.7.2 driver version. Temporary relief after spooler restart further indicated the underlying cause was driver corruption or mismatch rather than a transient service outage.
observed_errors: Print jobs stuck in queue (status: spooling)
Print spooler restart transiently clears jobs
Driver package checksum mismatch detected in event log

steps.action: Checked the shared PDQ-Print01 queues to verify whether jobs were paused, stuck, or continuously spooling.
steps.expected_result: Print queue is online and accepts new jobs.
steps.observed_result: Multiple jobs were stuck in spooling state on \\PDQ-Print01\Sales-Main and \\PDQ-Print01\HR-Floor2-Queue. New submissions from users mgonzalez and preddy accumulated behind blocked department queues, with 14 jobs total pending at time of inspection.
steps.evidence: Affected users Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez) and Priya Reddy (preddy) reported persistent stuck jobs and queue blockage on PDQ-Print01. Print Management console showed 14 queued jobs across both department queues with status 'Spooling' and no progress.

steps.action: Compared the installed printer driver package and queue mappings against the approved driver version for the affected printers.
steps.expected_result: Endpoint uses the current approved printer driver.
steps.observed_result: Logs showed driver package checksum mismatch for HP Universal Print Driver v6.9.0 (expected SHA256 did not match installed binary) and queue mappings for Sales-Main and HR-Floor2-Queue still pointed to the older v6.7.2 driver version.
steps.evidence: Event logs on PDQ-Print01 (Event ID 372) and driver package metadata under C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\x64\3 indicated checksum validation failure. Queue configuration exported by dnakamura confirmed stale v6.7.2 mapping on both affected queues.

steps.action: Reviewed Print Spooler service behavior and tested whether restarting the service would allow jobs to clear normally.
steps.expected_result: Spooler processes a test job without retry or access errors.
steps.observed_result: Spooler restart temporarily freed 3 of 14 jobs submitted by kmarsh, but the queue quickly reblocked within 90 seconds and driver unavailable errors returned for all subsequent submissions.
steps.evidence: Repeated spooler restarts (3 attempts by service desk agent Daniel Nakamura) did not provide a lasting recovery; each restart cleared a small batch before the corrupt driver package was re-invoked by the queue.

root_cause: Approved printer driver package on PDQ-Print01 was corrupt or mismatched by checksum, and affected printer queues were still mapped to an older driver version, causing repeated driver unavailable errors and queue blockage.

steps: Remove the corrupt or mismatched HP Universal Print Driver package v6.9.0 from PDQ-Print01 (10.22.4.55) using Print Management and install the approved HP Universal Print Driver package v6.9.0-hotfix that passes checksum validation, sourced from the approved driver repository.

Stop and restart the Print Spooler service on PDQ-Print01 after clearing all 14 stuck jobs from the affected Sales-Main and HR-Floor2-Queue print queues on the server. Verified by dnakamura that spool directory C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS was empty before service restart.

Remap the impacted department printer queues (\\PDQ-Print01\Sales-Main and \\PDQ-Print01\HR-Floor2-Queue) from the stale v6.7.2 driver version to the corrected approved v6.9.0-hotfix driver package, updating queue-to-driver assignments in Print Management.

Submit test print jobs from workstations WORKSTATION-PC-MG (mgonzalez) and WORKSTATION-PC-PR (preddy) through the remapped queues to confirm jobs leave spooling state and complete without driver unavailable errors. Both test pages printed successfully within 5 seconds.

If any queue still referenced the bad v6.9.0 package, roll back to the last known-good approved driver package (v6.7.2) and revalidate queue-to-driver assignments. Notify Kevin Marsh (kmarsh, 555-209-4418) and the Phoenix Workplace Services team of the resolution.

correspondence.message: After the overnight driver update, anything sent to PrinterQueue-Corp on print-server-02 stays in a printing state indefinitely. I'm Maria Gonzalez in Accounting — my workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MG at 10.42.16.88 can't print at all. Other users like Derek Huang and Priya Nair are also affected. We all get a 'driver unavailable' message and jobs just sit in the queue.

Checked the queue and spooler logs on print-server-02. There are 47 jobs stuck in the queue across departments. The HP Universal PCL6 driver is failing to load repeatedly with error 0x80070643 after the recent deployment package (v7.1.0.25054) was pushed last night at 02:15 AM. Reviewed event logs and confirmed the driver DLL fails integrity checks on load. Affected users include mgonzalez (10.42.16.88), dhuang (10.42.16.92), and pnair (10.42.17.14). Escalating to driver remediation. — Kevin Brashear, Workplace Services

Cleared all 47 stuck jobs from PrinterQueue-Corp, restarted the Print Spooler service on print-server-02, removed the corrupted HP Universal PCL6 driver package (v7.1.0.25054) from the server driver store, and reinstalled the approved HP Universal PCL6 driver (v7.0.0.24980) from the internal repository at \\pkg-repo-east\drivers\hp-upcl6. Sent validation test prints from mgonzalez's workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MG and dhuang's machine WORKSTATION-PC-DH — both completed successfully. Notifying affected users. — Kevin Brashear

correspondence.message: Several Finance users in Newark cannot print to the Dept-Color-Queue on PS-PRINT01. I'm one of the affected users — Maria Delgado, username mdelgado. correspondence.message: Hi Maria — can you confirm whether other queues on PS-PRINT01 (e.g., HR-Printer, Legal-Printer) are still processing jobs normally, and whether the approved HP Universal Print Driver package v7.2.1 was deployed to that server before the Finance-Printer failures began? Also, could you check from your workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC whether the queue shows as offline in Devices and Printers? I've asked jgarcia@corplabs.com to gather affected user names as well.

The reports are centered on Finance-Printer only — other queues like HR-Printer on PS-PRINT01 seem fine. The issue started right after today's driver deployment around 04:30 UTC. Users including myself (mchen, employee ID FIN-20481) and Robert Liu (rliu) see jobs stuck with 'Driver unavailable' and the queue looks offline. I'm printing from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC at IP 10.22.14.87 in the Newark office. Jorge Garcia (jgarcia) also confirmed the same behavior from his machine WORKSTATION-DESK-JG at 10.22.14.92.

Jobs from mchen's workstation (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC) advanced only briefly before returning to 'Driver unavailable', which strongly points to a corrupt or incomplete HP Universal Print Driver v7.2.1 package installed on PS-PRINT01. I'm escalating to proceed with a clean driver reinstall. — Kevin Patel (kpatel, Workplace Services)

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics isolated the fault to the Finance-Printer queue on PS-PRINT01 after the HP Universal Print Driver v7.2.1 deployment at ~04:30 UTC. Queue inspection showed 14 stuck jobs from finance users (mchen, rliu, jgarcia) and offline behavior. Spooler restart on PS-PRINT01 did not resolve the condition, and fallback remapping to the Class Driver only worked briefly before reverting. The repeated 'Driver unavailable' state after these checks confirmed a corrupted or incomplete driver installation rather than a simple paused queue or transient spooler issue. All affected users were in the Newark office on the 10.22.14.x subnet.

correspondence.message: Hi Rachel — please confirm whether new print jobs on PRINTER_QUEUE are staying in spooling state for all affected Floor2 Engineering users and whether the error shown is still "driver unavailable" after the spooler restart this morning. Also, can you verify whether the issue is limited to workstations on the 10.40.12.0/24 subnet or if users printing from other segments are also impacted? I can see your machine WORKSTATION-ROKONKWO is one of the affected hosts.

Yes, multiple users are still affected — myself, David Hargreaves, and at least seven others on the floor. New jobs appear in the shared queue on PrintServer01 but remain spooling, and the queue still shows the driver as unavailable even after the restart. I tried from my workstation WORKSTATION-ROKONKWO (10.40.12.47) and David tried from WORKSTATION-DHARGREAVES (10.40.12.53), same result on both. We also had Priya Nair (p.nair) attempt from her machine and she got the identical error.

Validation on PrintServer01 shows the queue is still mapped to an incorrect or corrupt driver package from the earlier reinstall carried out over the weekend. The driver store on the server contains HP Universal Print Driver v2.1 (vendor package) instead of the approved v2.2 package. Residual driver cache under C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\x64 is preventing the spooler from loading the correct driver component, which explains the recurring stuck jobs for r.okonkwo, d.hargreaves, p.nair, and the other affected accounts. I'll proceed with remediation — Marcus Tan (m.tan) from Desktop Support will assist with the driver swap.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the issue was not a simple stuck queue: the queue remained online but jobs stayed in spooling state for all Floor2 Engineering users (verified from WORKSTATION-ROKONKWO at 10.40.12.47 and WORKSTATION-DHARGREAVES at 10.40.12.53), spooler restart alone did not clear processing, and PrintServer01 was still referencing the incorrect HP Universal Print Driver v2.1 (corrupt vendor package) after the previous weekend reinstall. Review of driver version and spooler behavior by Marcus Tan (m.tan, Desktop Support) isolated the recurrence to stale queue mapping plus residual corrupt driver cache on PrintServer01 affecting the Bristol site's Floor2 printer infrastructure.

Investigation on PRN-SRV-01 found multiple stuck queues across three Finance department printers and repeated Event Log entries showing 'Driver unavailable' for HPUniversal_v6. Queue clears and spooler restarts are not persistent; the driver package appears corrupted at the server level. Approved driver reinstall and queue remapping are required. Escalation handled by Kevin Ostrowski (kostrowski, EMP-90274) from the Workplace Services print infrastructure team. Affected users confirmed: rng4521, mwebb03, pdesai. diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed this was not a simple stuck queue condition. The HP-LaserJet queue (\\PS-Print01\HP-LJ-FIN-3F) on PS-Print01 had 23 jobs stalled at 0%, submitted by Finance users including rnguyen, thadley, and mparker. Additionally, please verify from your workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MG whether the printer status shows as offline or online in the Devices panel. We have asked Derek Liu (dliu) from desktop support to review the server-side mapping in parallel.

Yes, new jobs are still getting stuck in Finance-Printer1 after the restart. I tried printing a test PDF from my machine WORKSTATION-PC-MG at around 08:38 and it went straight to stuck status. The spooler log on PRNSRV-EAST-02 continues to show "driver unavailable" for the same shared printer. My colleague Raj Patel (rpatel) on the same floor also confirmed the same behavior from his workstation at 10.47.22.85.

Confirmed the approved driver package (HP Universal Print Driver v7.1.0.25) is present in the central repository, but Finance-Printer1 on PRNSRV-EAST-02 is still mapped to an incorrect queue/driver association — it was pointing to the legacy PCL5 driver entry instead of the approved PCL6 package. This mismatch explains the recurring stuck jobs and spooler service errors after the prior reinstall on 2026-02-25. Derek Liu (dliu) has identified the exact mapping discrepancy and will proceed with the corrective steps.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed this was not just a stale queue condition on PRNSRV-EAST-02. The shared Finance-Printer1 queue had 23 stuck jobs across multiple Finance user accounts, spooler logs repeatedly showed "driver unavailable" (Event ID 372), and the printer remained associated with an incorrect PCL5 queue/driver mapping after the prior reinstall on 2026-02-25. Reinstalling the approved HP Universal Print Driver v7.1.0.25 alone had not resolved the underlying mapping inconsistency because the queue object on PRNSRV-EAST-02 still referenced the legacy driver entry. Service was restored after clearing the queue, restarting the spooler, and correcting the queue-to-driver mapping to point to the approved PCL6 package.

Cleared all 167 stuck print jobs from the Office-Color and Finance-BW queues to remove the backlog created during the driver failure condition. Notified affected users mgonzalez, dpark, and lokafor to resubmit their jobs.

Restarted the Print Spooler service on PrintServer01 and validated that it remained stable for 30+ minutes after the corrected driver package (v3.7.1) was loaded. No further Event ID 372 or 7031 entries appeared.
Reassociated the impacted printer queues (Office-Color and Finance-BW) with the corrected v3.7.1 driver package and confirmed both queues returned to an online state in Print Management.

Submitted validation print jobs through the affected queues from WORKSTATION-MG-12 (mgonzalez) and WORKSTATION-DP-7 (dpark) and monitored PrintServer01 for recurrence for approximately 2 hours with successful job completion on both queues. No further driver errors observed.

correspondence.message: We restarted the printer and the queue again from WORKSTATION-PC-MCHEN, but print jobs are still sitting at 0% and the Floor 2 printer shows offline to users. I also tried printing from my laptop WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RP and got the same result. Multiple people on our team have reported the same — Maria Chen, David Okonkwo, and myself have all had jobs stuck since yesterday afternoon.

Reviewed the print server PRINTSRV-NYC-02 (10.42.8.15) and found the shared queue \\PRINTSRV-NYC-02\Floor2-HPM477 still mapped to an older driver GUID {4A3B21CF-8E7D-4F12-9C6A-1D5E0F3B7A82} instead of the current approved GUID. Event logs on the server also show spooler crash behavior (EventID 7031) and driver load failure 0x8007007e under the SYSTEM context, which explains why the issue returned after the temporary restart performed by Raj Patel (emp ID E-50823). The stale GUID reference was left behind by the 2026-03-03 driver deployment.

Proceeding with removal of the incorrect driver package (HP Universal Print Driver v6.5.0, GUID {4A3B21CF-8E7D-4F12-9C6A-1D5E0F3B7A82}) from PRINTSRV-NYC-02, reinstall of the approved HP Universal Driver v6.8, remap of the Floor2-HPM477 queue to the current driver GUID, and a deployment policy correction in the print management console to prevent regression. Will coordinate with Lisa Nakamura (lnakamura, Workplace Services lead) to validate the fix across affected user workstations.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed this was not a simple offline printer condition on the Floor 2 HP M477 queue served by PRINTSRV-NYC-02. The shared queue at \\PRINTSRV-NYC-02\Floor2-HPM477 was accepting submissions but jobs stalled at 0% for users including mchen and dokonkwo. Event logs on the print server showed Print Spooler crashes (EventID 7031) and driver load failures (0x8007007e), and the queue still referenced an outdated driver GUID {4A3B21CF-8E7D-4F12-9C6A-1D5E0F3B7A82}. The combination of stale queue mapping and an incorrect or corrupt driver package caused the recurring failure until the approved HP Universal Driver v6.8 was reinstalled and the queue mapping was corrected.

correspondence.message: Multiple Marketing users in Portland confirmed their jobs remain stuck on PRNT-SRV-01. Rachel Nguyen (r.nguyen@corplabs.com) and David Kowalski reported that the printers appear offline, and each queue shows 'Driver unavailable' after last night's driver update (CR-2026-0187). Rachel's workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN at IP 10.42.16.88 had 3 stuck jobs in the MKT-CLR-Q2 queue, and David's machine WORKSTATION-PC-DK at 10.42.16.91 had 5 stuck jobs across two queues. The issue appears to affect all Marketing floor printers mapped through PRNT-SRV-01.

Investigation on PRNT-SRV-01 by technician Marcus Bell (m.bell, EMP-30254) found the newly deployed printer driver package (v6.8.1.4020) is corrupted with INF parse and checksum validation failures, which is preventing the spooler from loading the driver. The deployed package checksum (SHA256: 4a7c...e1f3) does not match the approved baseline checksum (SHA256: 9b2d...a804) from the Driver Package repository. Event logs on PRNT-SRV-01 show repeated 'Printer driver load failure (INF parse error)' entries beginning at 02:17 UTC when the scheduled deployment completed. Marcus confirmed the issue is isolated to the v6.8.1.4020 package pushed via the overnight change window.

Cleared the affected print queues (MKT-CLR-Q1, MKT-CLR-Q2, MKT-BW-Q3) and restarted the Print Spooler service on PRNT-SRV-01 to restore limited service. Initiated rollback to the previous approved driver version (v6.7.2.3850) while preparing a verified signed reinstall of v6.8.1.4020-r2. Confirmed with Rachel Nguyen and David Kowalski that test prints from their workstations now process, though queue remapping is still pending. Escalated to Workplace Services lead Priya Deshmukh (p.deshmukh) for sign-off on the corrected driver package deployment.

Driver comparison by Marcus Bell (EMP-30254) identified a corrupted INF/checksum mismatch in the deployed v6.8.1.4020 package versus the approved baseline, and spooler testing showed only temporary improvement until the driver was rolled back to v6.7.2.3850 and reinstalled from a validated signed package.

Maria's workstation WORKSTATION-FIN-MG at 10.42.18.77 shows five pending jobs. David reports the same from his machine at 10.42.18.83.

Service desk agent Tyrone Mitchell cleared the queue on PRN-PS-01 and restarted the Print Spooler service (spoolsv). Some jobs dropped briefly, but the queue returned to the same failed state within approximately four minutes and did not process new print jobs normally. Event log on PRN-PS-01 showed repeated Event ID 7031 spooler crash entries. Tyrone confirmed the issue is server-side and not isolated to a single client.

steps: Confirmed in Endpoint Protection telemetry that the AcmeApp installer (AcmeAppSetup_v4.2.exe) was being denied as Not Approved under the Approved Applications policy (EP-APCTRL-0087) on endpoints WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC, WORKSTATION-DESK-DO, and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN, rather than failing due to package corruption or device inventory issues.

However, Azure AD sign-in logs for the same correlation IDs still show conditional access denials (resultType: 53003, failureReason: 'Access has been blocked by Conditional Access policies'). Cross-referencing Okta group sync, these users are members of 'Okta-Marketing' and 'Okta-Sales' but the Azure AD side-group mapping drifted after last week's directory sync update. diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the issue was not a simple user-factor failure. Reproduction with accounts rnguyen and mparker showed a true MFA loop — Okta MFA succeeded but Azure AD conditional access policy 'CA-SaaS-MFA-Required' denied the federated token. Okta enrollment remediation (factor reset for dholloway, mparker) improved factor state but did not consistently restore access, confirming the block was downstream. Policy comparison identified that the Azure AD Conditional Access group 'SG-SaaS-Marketing-Sales' no longer included the synced Okta group members after a directory sync change on 2026-03-30, causing scope mismatches against current Okta group assignments as the blocking condition.

correspondence.message: Hi, this is Elena Vasquez (username: evasquez). After I approve the Okta MFA push on my phone, GlobalProtect connects for about 30 seconds and then drops. The gateway log entry at 13:44:28 shows 'TLS handshake failed: certificate expired' referencing the device certificate with thumbprint 9A:3F:C2:... issued by the internal Device Certificate Service CA. The same pattern was confirmed on Marcus Hahn's device (username: mhahn, host WORKSTATION-HP-MH, IP 10.42.17.92). correspondence.message: Hi Marcus, thanks for reporting this. Also let us know if you see any 802.1X or certificate prompts during reconnect. Could you run 'netsh wlan show interfaces' and share the output? — Priya Nair, Network Support

Hi Priya, it joins the Corporate Wi-Fi (CorpNet-Secure) briefly — I can see the connected status for maybe 20–30 seconds — then shows no internet/network access and disconnects. On later attempts I can see repeated EAP timeout and 802.1X authentication failure messages in Event Viewer (Event ID 11001, Source: WLAN-AutoConfig). The netsh output shows the profile as 'CorpNet-Secure' with authentication WPA2-Enterprise but the state flips between 'authenticating' and 'disconnected'. My username is mdelgado and I'm in the ENG-East device group.

Thanks Marcus. After reviewing the NAC logs and Wireless Controller session data for your device (MAC ending :A3:7F, username mdelgado), the issue points to an incorrect NAC policy assignment for the ENG-East device group introduced during the 2026-04-24 policy update. The earlier rollback and profile reset only masked the issue temporarily because the corrected policy was not fully propagated. We are correcting the policy targeting on the ClearPass NAC server now and will then re-enroll your wireless profile to restore stable access. I've looped in Raj Patel from the network infrastructure team to validate the controller side. — Priya Nair

correspondence.message: Hi, I'm Rachel Nguyen from the Sales team in Philadelphia. I can join Corporate Wi-Fi (CorpNet-Secure) on my laptop LAPTOP-RNGUYEN-04, but it shows Connected, no internet and then fails EAP authentication after I enter my credentials for rng_sales. I need wireless access for client demos today — can someone look into this urgently?

Review of the wireless controller (WLC-EAST-02) showed the RADIUS server certificate used for EAP on the authentication path had expired as of 2026-04-26T00:00:00Z. This would cause certificate validation and authentication to fail for any client attempting EAP-TLS or PEAP, including Rachel's device LAPTOP-RNGUYEN-04 at IP 10.22.47.118. The issue was confirmed by network engineer David Kowalski after checking the Cisco ISE RADIUS logs for username rng_sales, which showed repeated "EAP Authentication failed" rejections with reason code 'server certificate not trusted'.

The certificate was renewed by David Kowalski and applied to WLC-EAST-02, then the wireless profile on LAPTOP-RNGUYEN-04 was cleared so the laptop could forget and rejoin the CorpNet-Secure SSID. Rachel confirmed she regained connectivity at 08:29 local time. Follow-up monitoring is planned for intermittent drops — I've asked Marcus Pham (marcus.pham@corplabs.com) on the NAC team to keep an eye on the controller association logs for the Philadelphia floor 3 AP group over the next 24 hours.

correspondence.message: Several staff on floor 3 in the Denver office cannot connect to Corporate Wi-Fi since this morning; devices join but then show no network access and keep dropping on laptops and phones. I'm Maria Gonzalez (employee ID EMP-90214) and my laptop WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MG at IP 10.42.3.117 was one of the first to fail. My colleague Raj Patel (rpatel) on the same floor is also affected, along with most of our team.

Wireless controller and RADIUS/NAC logs show repeated 802.1X failures tied to certificate validation, and the server certificate on radius-auth01.corplabs.internal expired at 07:50. Reviewing authentication logs filtered by the reporting user mgonzalez (EMP-90214) and rpatel confirmed EAP-TLS handshake failures beginning immediately after expiry. Network engineer Kevin Liu (kliu) from the network operations team in Denver pulled the RADIUS event timeline and confirmed the scope is building-wide, not limited to floor 3.

Escalated to Wireless Infrastructure lead Diane Choi (dchoi, phone 303-555-0178) to renew the 802.1X certificate and update NAC trust; temporary limited PSK guest access was recommended until authentication service was restored. Diane confirmed the renewal request has been submitted to the internal CA and expects the new certificate to be deployed within the hour. Users like mgonzalez and rpatel should use the guest SSID (CorpNet-Guest) in the interim.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed this was an infrastructure-side wireless authentication outage rather than a client-specific Wi-Fi profile issue. Affected devices could associate to the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID, but RADIUS/NAC logs on radius-auth01.corplabs.internal showed certificate validation failures immediately after the 802.1X server certificate expired at 07:50 on 2026-04-26. Wireless controller behavior was consistent with backend auth rejection, explaining the repeated disconnects and lack of network access across multiple device types. Testing was performed using endpoints belonging to mgonzalez (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MG, IP 10.42.3.117) and rpatel to reproduce the failure on both Windows and macOS platforms.

steps.evidence: Controller review aligned repeated disconnects with unsuccessful 802.1X transactions. Disconnect events for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MG and rpatel's device correlated precisely with RADIUS rejection timestamps logged by kliu's investigation.

root_cause: The 802.1X/RADIUS server certificate used for Corporate Wi-Fi authentication expired, causing EAP-TLS certificate validation failures and NAC denial after association.

steps: Renew and install a valid 802.1X/RADIUS server certificate on the wireless authentication infrastructure (radius-auth01.corplabs.internal) with the correct subject, validity period, and full certificate chain. Diane Choi (dchoi) submitted the CSR to the internal CA and received the renewed certificate with a new expiry of 2028-04-25.

Update the Network Access Control and related trust configuration to recognize the renewed certificate chain and ensure EAP-TLS validation succeeds. The NAC console was updated by kliu to reference the new certificate thumbprint and intermediate CA, and trust was verified against the CorpNet-Secure authentication policy.

Apply the updated certificate configuration on the wireless controller and authentication path, then restart or reload affected authentication services as required to clear the expired certificate state. Diane Choi (dchoi) deployed the renewed certificate to radius-auth01.corplabs.internal and performed a rolling restart of the RADIUS service at 15:32 to activate the new certificate.

Validate successful client authentication by testing managed Windows and macOS devices on the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID and confirming successful EAP-TLS handshakes, policy assignment, and network access. Verification was performed with mgonzalez on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MG (IP 10.42.3.117) and rpatel's MacBook — both authenticated successfully and received full corporate network access within seconds of reconnecting.

Keep the temporary limited PSK guest SSID available only until production authentication is confirmed stable, then remove the workaround and notify users to reconnect if they cached failed sessions. Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez@corplabs.com) and other affected users on floors 2–4 in Denver were notified via email at 16:00 that Corporate Wi-Fi was restored and the guest SSID workaround would be disabled at 18:00.

correspondence.message: Please confirm whether affected devices are failing before getting network access and whether the issue is limited to managed laptops or also impacting BYOD users on the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-Secure). Also, can you verify whether the failures are isolated to specific floors or APs? We need to know if users like mespinoza and dhuang are seeing the same behavior on different device types so we can rule out endpoint-side profile corruption before escalating to the network team.

The failures are happening to both managed and BYOD devices across floors 4 and 7. Users can join the SSID but are denied access or disconnect immediately — this started right after the overnight certificate change around 00:15 UTC. I personally tested with my laptop WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-DH and my iPhone and both fail the same way. Maria Espinoza on floor 7 confirmed the same from her workstation WORKSTATION-PC-ME. We've had at least 15 people call the helpdesk so far this morning.

Wireless controller (WLC-HQ-01.corplabs.internal) and RADIUS review on RADIUS-EAST-01.corplabs.internal shows repeated EAP-TLS authentication failures with 'certificate expired' errors beginning at the 00:15 UTC rollover window. The RADIUS service at 10.22.1.50 is still presenting the old server certificate (CN=radius-auth.corplabs.internal, expired 2026-04-28T00:00:00Z) instead of the renewed one. This confirms the authentication service failed to bind the new certificate during the automated rollover, causing all 802.1X sessions to be rejected. Assigning to network engineer Priya Nair (pnair, EMP-40821) for immediate remediation.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics showed a service-side authentication failure on RADIUS-EAST-01.corplabs.internal (10.22.1.50) rather than an endpoint-specific Wi-Fi profile issue. NAC and RADIUS logs consistently reported EAP-TLS certificate expired failures starting at the 00:15 UTC rollover, referencing the expired cert CN=radius-auth.corplabs.internal. Controller logs on WLC-HQ-01.corplabs.internal confirmed clients were associating but failing during 802.1X authentication across APs on floors 4 and 7 in the Arlington office. Replacing the expired certificate binding and restarting authentication services restored successful wireless access for all affected users.

Several devices still failed even after forget/rejoin attempts, indicating the issue was not limited to a stale endpoint profile but was server-side.
steps.evidence: Issue reproduced across multiple device types including Windows managed laptops, iPhones, and Android BYOD. Persisted after forget/rejoin for users mespinoza, dhuang, and jparker on floor 4. No improvement observed regardless of AP or device class.

steps.action: Reviewed NAC and RADIUS authentication logs for the denied wireless sessions after the rollover window.
steps.expected_result: Device authenticates and receives the correct network access policy.

All clients were denied normal network access and placed in the quarantine VLAN by NAC.
steps.evidence: Repeated RADIUS reject entries and NAC denial events aligned with the post-rollover period (00:15–18:30 UTC). Over 200 unique MAC addresses rejected. Logs reviewed by Priya Nair (pnair) confirmed consistent 'server certificate validation failed' across all authentication attempts.

steps.action: Checked wireless controller logs for widespread disconnect behavior and controller-side authentication anomalies after midnight rollout.
steps.expected_result: Controller shows stable association and no repeated disconnect reason.
steps.observed_result: Controller logs on WLC-HQ-01.corplabs.internal showed clients associating to APs on floors 4 and 7 but then being denied or disconnected during 802.1X authentication, with failures beginning immediately after the 00:15 UTC certificate rollover. No AP hardware or roaming issues detected.
steps.evidence: Controller disconnect reason codes pointed to EAP-TLS authentication rejects rather than AP roaming instability or RF issues. Events correlated 1:1 with RADIUS reject timestamps. Reviewed by network engineer Priya Nair (EMP-40821) using Wireless Controller WebUI.

root_cause: The wireless authentication stack continued presenting an expired EAP-TLS server certificate on the RADIUS service after the scheduled certificate rollover, causing client certificate validation to fail and NAC to reject 802.1X authentication requests.

steps: Installed the renewed PKI server certificate (CN=radius-auth.corplabs.internal, valid through 2027-04-28) on RADIUS-EAST-01.corplabs.internal and the wireless controller WLC-HQ-01.corplabs.internal components handling 802.1X authentication. Certificate deployment performed by Priya Nair (pnair).

Updated the active certificate binding on RADIUS-EAST-01.corplabs.internal (10.22.1.50) so the authentication services presented the new certificate instead of the expired rollover artifact. Verified the new cert thumbprint matched the PKI-issued renewal.

Restarted the FreeRADIUS listener on RADIUS-EAST-01.corplabs.internal and wireless authentication services on WLC-HQ-01.corplabs.internal to load the new certificate chain and clear all failed EAP-TLS sessions queued since 00:15 UTC.

Validated in controller and RADIUS logs that new client authentication attempts completed successfully without 'certificate expired' errors or NAC denials. Confirmed successful 802.1X authentication for test devices belonging to Derek Huang (dhuang) and Maria Espinoza (mespinoza) on both floors.

Directed impacted users to forget and rejoin the Corporate Wi-Fi profile (CorpNet-Secure). Manually re-enrolled the small subset of devices (approximately 8) that retained stale wireless profile state, including WORKSTATION-IPHONE-JP belonging to James Parker (jparker). Sent confirmation email to mespinoza@corplabs.com and dhuang@corplabs.com with reconnection instructions for their teams.

correspondence.message: Hi Rachel — please confirm whether affected laptops can still join the CorpNet-Secure SSID and whether the failure occurs before getting an IP address. We are checking if this is NAC authentication after the certificate rollover rather than a radio or AP issue. Can you also confirm the hostnames of a couple of the affected machines so we can trace them in RADIUS logs? This is Marcus Webb from the network support team.

Yes, the laptops connect to the SSID but then show "Access denied by NAC" and never get network access or an IP. My laptop LAPTOP-RTHORN-W10 (IP 10.22.3.117) and Kevin Osei's MacBook MACBOOK-KOSEI-12 are both affected. We are seeing the same behavior on company-managed Windows and macOS devices across floors 3 and 4. Kevin's extension is 512-555-0194 if you need to reach him directly.

NAC and RADIUS logs on the controller confirm certificate-based 802.1X denials after the wireless certificate rollover. Specifically, devices authenticating as users rthornt and kosei were denied with EAP-TLS certificate trust errors. The controller certificate chain was corrected and remaining impacted devices — including Rachel's and Kevin's — required Wi-Fi profile refresh or certificate re-enrollment to authenticate successfully. Escalating findings to Priya Nagarajan on the network infrastructure team for the certificate chain remediation.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed this was not a general RF or controller stability issue because affected devices (including LAPTOP-RTHORN-W10 at 10.22.3.117 and MACBOOK-KOSEI-12) could join the SSID consistently. NAC/RADIUS review showed certificate-related 802.1X denials for users rthornt and kosei after the recent rollover, and endpoint checks found some managed devices needed Wi-Fi profile refresh or certificate re-enrollment before NAC would authorize access and DHCP assignment.

steps.evidence: Wireless controller dashboard showed stable SSID association counts on Building A floors 3-4 APs. Symptoms consistently showed SSID association without IP assignment, pointing away from RF or roaming causes.

root_cause: Wireless 802.1X/NAC authentication failures were caused by the certificate rollover not being fully trusted by all managed endpoints and NAC/authentication chain components, leaving some devices with stale Wi-Fi profiles or unrefreshed client trust state after the controller/RADIUS certificate update.

steps: Validated and corrected the renewed wireless/RADIUS certificate chain presented by the controller so the full trust chain matched endpoint and NAC expectations after the rollover. Priya Nagarajan verified the intermediate CA was properly included in the chain.
Restarted wireless controller authentication services to ensure the updated certificate and chain were actively loaded for new client authentications.

Reviewed NAC authentication results and confirmed affected devices (LAPTOP-RTHORN-W10, MACBOOK-KOSEI-12, and others) were being denied during 802.1X/EAP-TLS evaluation rather than at DHCP or RF association stages.

Remediated impacted endpoints by refreshing the corporate Wi-Fi profile and re-enrolling device certificates on clients that still held stale trust or profile data after the rollover. Desktop support technician Luis Medina handled the on-site re-enrollment for floors 3-4.

Had affected users — including Rachel Thornton and Kevin Osei — forget and reconnect to the corporate SSID, then verified successful NAC authorization and IP assignment on previously failing devices. Both LAPTOP-RTHORN-W10 and MACBOOK-KOSEI-12 received valid DHCP leases and full network access.

correspondence.message: After the wireless profile update this morning, my laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN, IP 10.42.18.97) sees the Corporate SSID, connects briefly, then shows "Connected, no network access" and drops within about a minute. This is Rachel Nguyen in Engineering — my username is rnguyen and I need connectivity restored for a sprint deadline. I've tried forgetting the network and reconnecting but the behavior repeats.

Removed the existing wireless profile from Rachel's endpoint (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN), pushed the standard Corporate Wi-Fi profile again via the Network Access Control portal, and had the user reconnect. The device received an IP lease (10.42.18.97), but intermittent disconnects continued during testing — particularly when roaming near AP-DURHAM-3F-07. Escalating to network_team for controller-side review. — Kevin Marsh, Desktop Support (kmarsh@corplabs.com)

Investigation confirmed corrupt client wireless profile entries and cached supplicant state on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN were causing repeated re-authentication. After re-enrollment and cache cleanup by Kevin Marsh, connectivity stabilized and internal access was restored for rnguyen. Controller logs for AP-DURHAM-3F-07 showed transient instability during the recovery window but normalized after endpoint remediation. Verified with Rachel Nguyen that all Engineering resources are accessible. — Priya Desai, Network Team (pdesai@corplabs.com)

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics covered the endpoint wireless profile on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (user rnguyen, EMP-40821), NAC authentication behavior, and controller-side disconnect patterns for the Durham office 3rd-floor APs. The primary fault was confirmed on the client: corrupt Wi-Fi profile data and cached supplicant entries triggered repeated 802.1X re-authentication after the scheduled profile update. NAC was not the primary cause because the device received a valid lease (10.42.18.97) and proper access after re-enrollment. Controller review suggested AP-specific instability on AP-DURHAM-3F-07 during the recovery window, but service stabilized after endpoint remediation and validation by Priya Desai.

Re-enrolled the laptop to Corporate Wi-Fi using the current standard wireless profile template and verified the endpoint received a valid IP lease (10.42.18.97) after reconnecting to the Durham office network.

Confirmed the device wireless certificate and authentication state were valid after profile re-registration so 802.1X authentication could complete normally; Kevin Marsh validated the certificate chain on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN matched the current CA trust anchor.

Applied a temporary connectivity stabilization policy during recovery for rnguyen's device, then validated that the device maintained association without repeated re-authentication loops across multiple access points on the Durham 3rd floor.

Reviewed controller behavior for the access points involved in the user session (including AP-DURHAM-3F-07) and confirmed stable connectivity after remediation, closing the incident once internal resource access was restored for Rachel Nguyen per verification by Priya Desai.

correspondence.message: Hi Kevin — please confirm whether the affected devices are managed endpoints already enrolled for Corporate Wi-Fi via Cisco ISE, and whether the issue is seen on more than one floor or device type. Can you also verify whether your own device (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-KP) is experiencing the same rejection? We need to rule out a localized AP issue versus a broader NAC policy problem. Please share the MAC address or hostname of one or two affected devices so we can trace them in the RADIUS logs.

Yes, this is happening to managed laptops and phones across floors 4, 6, and 8. My laptop WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-KP (IP 10.42.16.88) gets the same rejection. Users like Rachel Nguyen on floor 6 and Tom Brierly on floor 8 can see the SSID but get no access after joining — several devices report 802.1X authentication failure in the Windows event log. Rachel's phone (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-RN) also fails. We've had at least 30 people report in since 08:00. Nothing changed on our end — all devices were working fine yesterday.

Network Support (lead analyst Priya Vasquez, pvasquez) reviewed NAC and Wireless Controller logs and found widespread RADIUS rejects tied to this morning's NAC policy update pushed by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) at 06:45. The policy change altered the authorization profile mapping for the CorpWiFi-Secure SSID, causing managed devices to fail policy matching on Cisco ISE node ISE-PRIMARY-01.corpnet.internal. A temporary exception rule was applied for a pilot group of five devices including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-KP and WORKSTATION-IPHONE-RN, which restored access immediately — confirming incorrect NAC policy mapping as the primary fault rather than certificate or endpoint profile issues.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics ruled out an endpoint profile/certificate issue on sampled managed devices (tested across Windows, iOS, and Android platforms belonging to users kpratt, rnguyen, and tbrierly) and did not support an AP-only failure. The strongest evidence came from Cisco ISE NAC and RADIUS logs, which showed policy mismatch/rejection events (authorization profile 'CorpWiFi-FullAccess' no longer matched) starting immediately after the 06:45 NAC policy change pushed by mdelgado. This confirmed the outage was caused by incorrect NAC policy mapping rather than client configuration or localized wireless infrastructure instability. Approximately 30+ users across floors 4, 6, and 8 in the Denver North Tower were impacted.

steps.action: Verify test endpoints have the current corporate Wi-Fi profile and valid client certificate enrollment.
steps.expected_result: Device has the active Wi-Fi profile and valid wireless certificate.
steps.observed_result: Test devices across multiple platforms had valid corporate Wi-Fi profiles and certificates, indicating the issue was not isolated to expired or missing endpoint configuration. Specifically, WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-KP (Windows 11, user kpratt) and WORKSTATION-IPHONE-RN (iOS 18, user rnguyen) both had current EAP-TLS certificates valid through 2027-02-15 and active CorpWiFi-Secure profiles.
steps.evidence: Failure reproduced on Windows laptop WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-KP (IP 10.42.16.88) and mobile device WORKSTATION-IPHONE-RN with existing managed profiles and valid certificates. Certificate thumbprints matched the expected corporate CA chain.

steps.action: Review NAC and RADIUS logs for authentication, authorization, and policy matching results for affected devices.
steps.expected_result: Device authenticates and receives the correct network access policy.
steps.observed_result: NAC logs on Cisco ISE showed policy rejection and authorization profile mismatch behavior beginning at 06:47 — two minutes after the NAC policy change by mdelgado. Devices authenticated successfully at the 802.1X layer but did not receive the intended 'CorpWiFi-FullAccess' authorization profile; instead they were assigned 'Default-Deny' due to a misconfigured policy set condition.
steps.evidence: Cisco ISE RADIUS live logs and controller syslogs aligned with widespread 802.1X authorization failures and RADIUS reject events. Over 140 reject entries were logged between 06:47 and 11:48 for endpoints across floors 4, 6, and 8. Sample reject entry for MAC endpoint belonging to user rnguyen showed 'AuthorizationPolicyMatchedRule: Default-Deny' instead of expected 'CorpWiFi-FullAccess'.

steps.action: Review wireless controller behavior to determine whether access points or client roaming instability caused the connection failures.
steps.expected_result: Controller shows stable association and no repeated disconnect reason.
steps.observed_result: Wireless Controller review did not indicate a floor-specific AP outage; rebooting APs on floor 4 did not restore service, pointing away from controller or AP health as the primary cause. Client association counts remained normal — devices were joining the SSID but being rejected post-authentication by NAC.
steps.evidence: Single-floor AP reboot on floor 4 had no meaningful improvement while RADIUS rejects continued in Cisco ISE. Controller dashboard showed stable AP health across all three affected floors with normal client association rates, confirming the failure occurred at the NAC policy layer, not the wireless infrastructure layer.

root_cause: An early-morning NAC configuration change introduced incorrect policy mapping for the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID, causing valid 802.1X/EAP-TLS device authentications to miss the intended access policy and be rejected by NAC/RADIUS.

steps: Identify and remove or roll back the NAC policy change introduced by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) at 06:45 that altered Corporate Wi-Fi policy matching on Cisco ISE. The misconfigured policy set condition in the 'CorpWiFi-Managed-Devices' authorization rule was reverted to the previous known-good configuration snapshot from 2026-04-28.

Correct the NAC policy assignments for the CorpWiFi-Secure SSID on Cisco ISE, including restoring the intended authentication rule, the 'CorpWiFi-FullAccess' authorization profile, and the RADIUS profile mapping used for corporate-managed endpoints. Priya Vasquez (pvasquez) validated the corrected policy set against the change management baseline.

Validate that affected device classes receive the correct network access result after authentication by testing a pilot set across Windows, iOS, and Android devices. Pilot devices included WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-KP (kpratt, floor 4), WORKSTATION-IPHONE-RN (rnguyen, floor 6), and Tom Brierly's Android device (tbrierly, floor 8) — all three received 'CorpWiFi-FullAccess' authorization successfully.

Clear or refresh any stale session state for impacted wireless authentications on Cisco ISE as needed, then have affected users reconnect or refresh their wireless profile/certificate enrollment if their device remained in a rejected state. Kevin Pratt (kpratt@corpnet.com) coordinated with floor wardens to notify approximately 30 affected staff to toggle Wi-Fi or reconnect.

Monitor NAC and wireless controller logs after the change to confirm RADIUS rejects return to normal baseline and users can associate and obtain network access across floors 4, 6, and 8 in the Denver North Tower. Priya Vasquez confirmed RADIUS reject rate dropped to baseline within 20 minutes of the policy rollback, and no further reports were received by 14:00.

root_cause: The EAP-TLS certificate presented by the Corporate Wi-Fi service had expired on the wireless controller, causing 802.1X authentication failures and NAC access denials for affected devices; some legacy clients also required profile refresh or manual reprovisioning after certificate replacement.

steps: Renewed the expired EAP-TLS certificate for Corp-WiFi and installed the replacement certificate and chain on the wireless controller certificate store. Certificate renewal was coordinated by network engineer Priya Nair (pnair).
Restarted the 802.1X/authentication service on the wireless controller so the new certificate was actively presented to connecting clients across the Frankfurt site.

Validated that NAC authentication requests were succeeding again after certificate deployment for users abrandt, leriksson, and moliveira, and that Access Denied responses tied to the expired certificate condition had stopped.

Directed affected users including Andrea Brandt and Lars Eriksson to forget the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID and re-enroll through the CorpConnect enrollment process so devices received the refreshed wireless profile and trust chain. Instructions were also emailed to rmehta@corplabs.com for distribution to the wider Frankfurt sales team.

correspondence.message: Hi Rachel — before we replace certificates, please confirm whether the device (hostname LAPTOP-RGARCIA-7F) connects to the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID-Corp and then drops to no network access, or if authentication fails immediately with the 802.1X EAP-TLS error message. Also, can you confirm whether Marton Kovacs and the other affected Sales users in Frankfurt are seeing the same behavior on their devices? Please share the client IP if you have it.

It joins the SSID briefly — my laptop LAPTOP-RGARCIA-7F gets an IP like 10.42.18.97 for a few seconds — then changes to no network access and shows an 802.1X authentication error. Marton's phone (IPHONE-MKOVACS-3A) does the same thing. The temporary NAC exception that Dmitri Petrov set up helped last night, but it failed again this morning when we tried reconnecting around 07:15 local time.

Review of Wireless Controller (WLC-EMEA-01) and ISE logs confirms EAP-TLS authentication is failing because the wireless server certificate presented in the trust path is expired or not fully updated after last night's rotation. Specifically, the certificate CN=wifi-auth.corplabs.internal expired at 2026-04-29T22:00:00Z and the renewed cert was not propagated to all controller nodes. We are replacing the certificate chain across the cluster and will retest normal 802.1X access for rgarcia, mkovacs, and the remaining affected Sales endpoints without the NAC exception. — Dmitri Petrov, Network Engineering

diagnostics.summary: Standard Wi-Fi authentication diagnostics confirmed the issue was not limited to a single endpoint — at least six Sales devices in the Frankfurt office were affected, including LAPTOP-RGARCIA-7F (IP 10.42.18.97) and IPHONE-MKOVACS-3A. NAC and Wireless Controller evidence showed EAP-TLS handshake failures caused by an expired or not fully updated wireless server certificate chain (CN=wifi-auth.corplabs.internal) after the scheduled rotation on 2026-04-29. A temporary NAC exception configured by dpetrov provided short-term access, but permanent recovery required renewing the controller certificate on WLC-EMEA-01, updating ISE trust, and then revalidating normal 802.1X access for all affected users.

root_cause: Expired or improperly propagated EAP-TLS server certificate and trust chain on the Wireless Controller and Cisco ISE after the scheduled certificate rotation, causing 802.1X authentication failures and intermittent post-association network denial for Corporate Wi-Fi clients.

steps: Renewed the wireless EAP-TLS server certificate (CN=wifi-auth.corplabs.internal) and reinstalled it on the Wireless Controller cluster WLC-EMEA-01 with the correct certificate chain, verified by Dmitri Petrov (dpetrov).

Updated the Cisco ISE trust anchor to trust the renewed wireless certificate path and verified certificate validity across the authentication workflow. Anita Sharma (asharma) confirmed the updated trust store on the ISE policy node.

Validated 802.1X authentication from affected Corporate Wi-Fi clients — including LAPTOP-RGARCIA-7F (rgarcia, IP 10.42.18.97) and IPHONE-MKOVACS-3A (mkovacs) — and confirmed successful policy application and network access without relying on the temporary NAC exception "EMEA-Sales-TempBypass."

Removed the temporary NAC exception "EMEA-Sales-TempBypass" after certificate propagation completed and authentication stabilized for the affected Sales user group in Frankfurt. Removal confirmed by dpetrov at 2026-04-30T01:45Z.

Instructed affected users (Rachel Garcia, Marton Kovacs, and four other Sales team members) to forget and re-add the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID-Corp and re-enroll device certificates where needed so endpoints would trust and use the updated certificate chain. Follow-up confirmation received from rgarcia@corplabs.com.

correspondence.message: My MacBook (WORKSTATION-MBP-RCHEN, IP previously assigned 10.42.17.88) tries to join Corporate Wi-Fi, then drops with "EAP authentication failed." The client logs also show a RADIUS reject from the NAS at wlc-east-02.corp.internal, and I still cannot get network access. My colleague Priya Nair (pnair) sitting near me in Arlington is experiencing the same thing on her device. Please advise — I need connectivity for a 6 AM meeting.

Reviewed RADIUS and wireless controller logs for user rchen (employee E-20841) and pnair and found the authentication failures line up with an expired controller certificate on wlc-east-02.corp.internal, which expired 2026-04-29T23:59:59Z. This explains the EAP rejects seen during Corporate Wi-Fi sign-in. A total of 14 endpoints in the Arlington office were affected, all authenticating through the same controller. Network engineer David Kowalski confirmed the certificate serial had not been rotated during the scheduled maintenance window.

Renewed the WLAN controller certificate on wlc-east-02.corp.internal and pushed the updated configuration to all affected access points in the Arlington office. User rchen, please forget the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID on WORKSTATION-MBP-RCHEN and reconnect; if it still fails, remove the saved wireless profile under System Preferences > Network and re-enroll the device via the MDM portal. I've also notified pnair and the other impacted users. Reach out to David Kowalski or myself (tmorales) if issues persist.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the issue was not isolated to a single endpoint — at least 14 devices in the Arlington office were affected, including WORKSTATION-MBP-RCHEN (rchen, 10.42.17.88) and pnair's laptop. RADIUS and controller logs on wlc-east-02.corp.internal showed 802.1X/EAP authentication failures caused by an expired WLAN controller certificate (expired 2026-04-29T23:59:59Z). After certificate renewal and configuration deployment by network engineer David Kowalski, remaining failures were traced to stale or corrupt local Wi-Fi profiles on some devices, which were resolved by forgetting the SSID or removing and re-enrolling the wireless profile.

correspondence.message: Retested CorpNet after reboot on my laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-KP, IP 10.22.14.88) and with known-good domain credentials for kpatel; the laptop still shows "authentication failed" in the Wi-Fi connection dialog and never gets an IP address. Colleague Jorge Morales on the same floor confirmed identical behavior on his device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-JM (10.22.14.91). We both had working connectivity before the maintenance window last night.

Wireless Infrastructure review by nwilson (Network Engineering) found repeated RADIUS Access-Reject events during EAP-TLS on NPS-EAST-01.corp.ntinfra.net, with Event ID 6273 referencing an expired server-side authentication certificate (thumbprint 4A:CF:9B:…, expired 2026-04-29T23:59:59Z). The certificate was issued to radius-auth.corp.ntinfra.net by the internal PKI CA and was not auto-renewed during the maintenance window as expected. All CorpNet 802.1X attempts from the Manhattan 14th-floor AP group were affected.

Requested certificate renewal through the internal PKI team (ticket PKI-REQ-8821, handled by Diane Cho, dcho@corplabs.com) and scheduled controller certificate deployment on WLC-EAST-02. A temporary NAC bypass rule was placed for Karen Patel (kpatel, MAC AA:BB:CC:11:22:33) only, as she had a critical client demo at 12:00 ET, until normal 802.1X authentication was restored for all users.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics ruled out a simple endpoint profile issue across affected devices (including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-KP and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-JM) and identified repeated RADIUS Access-Reject responses (Event ID 6273) during 802.1X EAP-TLS on NPS-EAST-01.corp.ntinfra.net. Evidence pointed to an expired server-side wireless authentication certificate (expired 2026-04-29T23:59:59Z) on the RADIUS/controller path, which blocked successful CorpNet authentication and DHCP IP assignment for at least seven Sales-group users on the Manhattan 14th floor after the 04:00–06:00 ET maintenance window.

steps.evidence: Issue reproduced across at least seven Sales-group users on the Manhattan 14th floor after the 04:00–06:00 ET maintenance window, reducing likelihood of a single-device profile problem. Client-side wireless logs on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-KP showed "The server certificate has expired" during EAP-TLS negotiation.

steps.evidence: Escalation notes from nwilson referenced expired certificate findings on NPS-EAST-01.corp.ntinfra.net; the server certificate for radius-auth.corp.ntinfra.net had lapsed at 2026-04-29T23:59:59Z and was not auto-renewed during the scheduled maintenance window.

This indicated the primary fault was RADIUS authentication rejection rather than AP roaming, RF instability, or controller-level association failure.
