root_cause: Expired EAP-TLS server certificate on the CorpNet wireless authentication path caused RADIUS/controller authentication to reject 802.1X requests after the maintenance window.

steps: Renew the expired EAP-TLS server certificate (thumbprint 4A:CF:9B:…, expired 2026-04-29) used by the CorpNet RADIUS authentication service on NPS-EAST-01.corp.ntinfra.net via internal PKI request PKI-REQ-8821 (processed by Diane Cho), and confirm the new certificate has a valid chain and dates extending through 2027-04-30.

Install and bind the renewed certificate on the RADIUS service (NPS-EAST-01.corp.ntinfra.net) and wireless controller components (WLC-EAST-02) participating in CorpNet 802.1X EAP-TLS authentication, verifying the full certificate chain is trusted.

Restart or reload the affected NPS authentication service and WLC-EAST-02 controller RADIUS integration so the updated certificate is actively presented during EAP-TLS exchanges; confirm via test TLS handshake that the new certificate thumbprint is served.

Validate successful test authentication on CorpNet for kpatel (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-KP) and jmorales (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-JM), and confirm clients complete 802.1X, receive the correct Sales VLAN network authorization, and obtain IP addresses normally via DHCP.

Instruct affected users (including Karen Patel and Jorge Morales) to forget and rejoin the CorpNet SSID or restart wireless services so cached authentication state is refreshed, then remove the temporary NAC bypass for kpatel (MAC AA:BB:CC:11:22:33) after verification that all seven affected users have restored connectivity.

correspondence.message: Hi Rachel — please confirm whether your laptop (hostname LAPTOP-RSIMMONS) can still connect by Ethernet or the guest SSID, and whether anyone else nearby on the 3rd floor is seeing the same Corporate-WiFi authentication failure. Also, can you share your current IP address if you're on wired so we can cross-reference NAC logs?

Ethernet works fine — my wired IP is 10.40.22.87 — and I can join the guest wireless, but Corporate-WiFi keeps failing to authenticate on my laptop LAPTOP-RSIMMONS. Two other users near me, Derek Huang (d.huang) and Priya Nair (p.nair), reported the same issue starting this morning around 8:30. Derek's laptop is LAPTOP-DHUANG and he's also on the 3rd floor in Charlotte.

Network review by Carlos Medina (network_team) found repeated 802.1X authentication failures and NAC denies for MAC addresses associated with r.simmons, d.huang, and p.nair — all caused by an expired RADIUS wireless authentication certificate (CN=radius-wifi.corplabs.internal, expired 2026-04-30T00:00:00Z). Certificate renewal and controller deployment across the WLC cluster are in progress. Affected users should regain Corporate-WiFi access within 30 minutes of propagation.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics ruled out a single-endpoint Wi-Fi profile issue because multiple users in the Charlotte office (r.simmons, d.huang, p.nair) were affected and wired/guest connectivity remained available. NAC and controller review showed repeated 802.1X authentication failures tied to an expired RADIUS/wireless certificate (CN=radius-wifi.corplabs.internal, expired 2026-04-30T00:00:00Z) in the authentication chain. After the certificate was renewed and deployed to controllers, clients including LAPTOP-RSIMMONS and LAPTOP-DHUANG could complete EAP authentication and receive network access normally.

Cleared stale wireless state by removing the affected device Wi-Fi profiles on LAPTOP-RSIMMONS and LAPTOP-DHUANG and instructing Rachel Simmons and Derek Huang to forget and rejoin the Corporate-WiFi SSID to complete authentication against the renewed certificate. Priya Nair (p.nair) was contacted at ext. 704-555-3198 and confirmed reconnection as well.

Monitored post-change authentication and NAC logs to confirm successful EAP transactions and allow events for r.simmons, d.huang, and p.nair, and advised temporary use of wired or guest access only until controller propagation completed across all sites.

correspondence.message: Hi Markus — please confirm whether the laptop (WORKSTATION-DLAT-MK, IP currently showing as 10.99.50.37 on the Guest VLAN) stays connected to the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID but only loses internal access, and whether removing/rejoining the wireless profile or renewing the device certificate changes the VLAN assignment. Also, can you verify that your colleague Renata Oliveira on the same Sales group is experiencing the identical Guest VLAN placement? I'd like to rule out a device-specific issue before escalating to the network team.

Yes, the laptop stays connected and shows authenticated under my username mkaplan, but it still lands in the Guest VLAN (10.99.50.x range). I removed and rejoined the CorpNet-EMEA SSID, renewed the cert via Corporate Certificate Enrollment, and rebooted, but internal resources like the file server and CRM portal are still unreachable. Renata confirmed the same behavior on her machine (WORKSTATION-DLAT-RO) — she's also stuck on Guest VLAN with no corporate access. This seems to be affecting the whole Sales I group here in Frankfurt.

NAC log review on the Network Access Control appliance shows successful 802.1X authentication for mkaplan (MAC: 5C:BA:2F:19:A7:03) and roliveira but incorrect authorization after the 14:00 UTC policy rollout. Both devices are matching the 'Default-Guest' policy group instead of 'Sales-CorpAccess', resulting in Guest VLAN (VLAN 50) assignment. The root issue is a group mapping error introduced during today's NAC policy push — the Sales OU CN path was inadvertently remapped. Updating the group mapping for Sales I devices and clearing stale session bindings for affected endpoints now. Network engineer Priya Nair is applying the corrected policy.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics ruled out an endpoint certificate/profile failure on WORKSTATION-DLAT-MK and wireless controller instability on the Frankfurt EMEA controller cluster. The key finding was that 802.1X authentication succeeded for user mkaplan (and other Sales I members such as roliveira), but NAC authorization matched the device to the wrong post-rollout policy group ('Default-Guest' instead of 'Sales-CorpAccess'), assigning Guest VLAN 50 access instead of corporate VLAN 110. After network engineer Priya Nair corrected the NAC mapping, cleared stale bindings, and forced re-authentication, the device received the proper corporate network access on VLAN 110 with a valid DHCP lease.

Change applied by network engineer Priya Nair (pnair).

Pushed the updated NAC policy and associated authorization changes to the Wireless Controller cluster serving the Frankfurt EMEA site to ensure the revised VLAN 110 assignment was available across the wireless environment for all Sales I group members.

Cleared stale policy bindings and session state for the affected devices (WORKSTATION-DLAT-MK, MAC 5C:BA:2F:19:A7:03; WORKSTATION-DLAT-RO), then forced a fresh 802.1X re-authentication so the corrected 'Sales-CorpAccess' policy would be reevaluated and the proper VLAN assignment applied.

Had the user mkaplan remove the old Corporate Wi-Fi profile for CorpNet-EMEA, forget the SSID, and re-enroll the managed wireless profile and certificate via Corporate Certificate Enrollment to eliminate any cached endpoint-side mismatch. Same steps communicated to Renata Oliveira for her device.

Verified after policy convergence and reconnection that WORKSTATION-DLAT-MK was no longer assigned to the Guest VLAN 50 and that internal network access was restored on VLAN 110 (new IP 10.20.110.54) without relying on the temporary NAC exception. correspondence.message: Hi Maria — please confirm whether affected users can join the Corporate SSID (CorpNet-Secure) but then receive a NAC access denied message, and whether this started after today's certificate rotation around 03:45 UTC. Could you also let me know the hostnames or IPs of a few affected devices so we can trace them in the NAC logs? Yes, users can authenticate to the Corporate Wi-Fi but then have no network access and see NAC access denied. I'm on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (IP 10.42.3.117) and my colleague Raj Patel on the 4th floor (username: rpatel) is seeing the same thing. Reports started shortly after the planned certificate rotation this morning. We've had at least 15 people reach out to our floor leads about it.

Reviewed controller (WLC-PDX-01.corp.internal) and NAC authentication behavior and found the wireless controller TLS/RADIUS certificate had expired after rotation, causing EAP-TLS failures and NAC denials for all clients authenticating via CorpNet-Secure. Certificate renewal restored service for most users. A small subset — including rpatel and user jmartinez — needed profile removal and re-enrollment. I've coordinated with Kevin Driscoll to confirm the new certificate chain is valid through 2027-05-01. All affected users on floors 3 and 4 in Portland should now have connectivity restored.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed the outage was not caused by access point instability or roaming across the Portland 3rd/4th floor APs. NAC and controller authentication review on WLC-PDX-01.corp.internal showed EAP-TLS failures immediately after the scheduled certificate rotation (performed by kdriscoll at 03:45 UTC) because the wireless controller's TLS/RADIUS certificate had expired — the new cert was not properly activated. After certificate renewal and NAC configuration refresh, most clients authenticated normally; the remaining failures were isolated to endpoints (e.g., WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC at 10.42.3.117, and devices belonging to rpatel and jmartinez) with stale Wi-Fi profiles that required manual removal and re-enrollment.

correspondence.message: Hi Maria — please confirm whether affected users fail only on 'corp-wifi' and whether reconnecting or reapplying the wireless profile changes the behavior on the impacted laptops. We need to distinguish between an endpoint profile issue and a shared NAC or controller problem. Could you also confirm the hostnames of the devices you and Kevin tested? The issue is affecting several Sales users here in Charlotte on 'corp-wifi' since about 9:45 this morning. I tried reconnecting and reapplying the profile on my laptop (LAPTOP-MDELGADO, IP 10.42.18.55) and Kevin did the same on his (LAPTOP-KOSTROWSKI, IP 10.42.18.61) — neither helped, and we still get disconnected without network access. Priya Nair (pnair) and Tom Beckett (tbeckett) on the same floor are also affected. Our manager, James Whitfield (jwhitfield, EMP-40227), has asked for an ETA since the whole team is blocked.

Controller logs on wlc-charlotte-02.corp.internal confirm the wireless controller certificate (serial 4A:7C:03:EE) expired at 2026-05-01T00:00:00Z. Recommend immediate certificate renewal, trust chain update on the RADIUS/NAC infrastructure, validation of successful Access-Accept responses for each affected user, and removal of the temporary NAC exception after full recovery.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics ruled out a simple endpoint profile issue after re-applying profiles on LAPTOP-MDELGADO and LAPTOP-KOSTROWSKI with no improvement, and localized the failure to infrastructure handling of 802.1X authentication on wlc-charlotte-02.corp.internal. NAC/RADIUS logs on nac-east-01.corp.internal showed repeated Access-Reject results for users mdelgado, kostrowski, pnair, and tbeckett among others. Controller logs identified an expired wireless controller certificate (serial 4A:7C:03:EE, expired 2026-05-01T00:00:00Z). correspondence.message: Multiple employees in Building A at the Raleigh office cannot connect to the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID 'CorpWiFi-Secure'. Devices show 802.1X failures and certificate warnings during EAP-TLS, and both laptops and phones are affected. I'm Karen Whitfield (kwhitfield, EMP-40821) — my laptop WORKSTATION-KW-4082 at IP 10.42.16.55 was the first device I noticed the issue on, but colleagues on the 3rd and 4th floors are reporting the same problem. My phone also fails to authenticate. Please escalate — this is impacting our entire team.

Reviewed Cisco WLC (wlc-east-01.corp.netops.local) and Cisco ISE NAC authentication logs. The controller certificate used in the EAP-TLS flow expired on 2026-04-30T23:59:59Z (CN=wlc-east-01.corp.netops.local, issued by CorpCA-Intermediate), which is causing the repeated wireless authentication failures for multiple users including kwhitfield, jparikh, and mdelgado. Verified that the certificate serial 4A:3F:91:CC:07 is no longer valid. NAC logs on ise-east-02.corp.netops.local show corresponding RADIUS reject events for all affected endpoints. — David Moreno, Network Engineering (dmoreno)

Reissued and installed the renewed TLS certificate (new serial 5B:72:A0:DD:18, valid through 2028-05-01) on wlc-east-01.corp.netops.local, refreshed NAC trust and policy on ise-east-02.corp.netops.local for the new thumbprint, and asked affected users — including Karen Whitfield (kwhitfield), Jaya Parikh (jparikh), and Marco Delgado (mdelgado) — to forget and rejoin the SSID or re-enroll legacy profiles where necessary. Confirmed successful 802.1X handshakes from kwhitfield's workstation WORKSTATION-KW-4082 (10.42.16.55) and jparikh's device WORKSTATION-JP-3371 within minutes of the certificate swap. — David Moreno (dmoreno)

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics confirmed this was a wireless infrastructure certificate failure rather than an isolated endpoint issue. WLC logs on wlc-east-01.corp.netops.local showed EAP-TLS failures caused by an expired controller certificate (CN=wlc-east-01.corp.netops.local, expired 2026-04-30), and NAC trust/policy on ise-east-02.corp.netops.local required refresh after certificate replacement. Affected users included kwhitfield (EMP-40821), jparikh (EMP-33710), and mdelgado (EMP-29154) among others in the Raleigh Building A site. Service was restored after certificate renewal, trust update, and validation of successful authentication from multiple endpoints.

Please reach out to me at ndesk-emea@corplabs.com or call ext. 4417 if the issue recurs.

Yes, my iPhone mail and Teams apps were still signed in with the old credentials, and I kept getting account locked or invalid password errors after the portal reset said it was successful. I removed the corporate account from the Mail app and re-signed into Teams, but the lockouts kept happening. My employee ID is E-20418 if that helps look things up. Diagnostic findings changed the resolution path: The reset workflow for mreeves was healthy — a new token was issued and the password propagated correctly to AD. However, diagnostics disproved the original assumption that the iPhone cache (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MR / 10.47.83.112) was causing the recurring lockouts. correspondence.message: Comparing affected corp.local lookups between the corporate resolver (dns-resolver-01.corp.local / 10.20.1.10) and authoritative DNS servers (ns1-internal.corp.local, ns2-internal.corp.local) now. Running nslookup and dig queries from WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.20.44.112) as reported by Marcus Delgado, and cross-referencing with queries from the monitoring host. — Priya Nair, Network Engineering

Authoritative internal DNS servers ns1-internal.corp.local and ns2-internal.corp.local have the same records, but the corporate resolver is intermittently returning NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, and an older A record (10.10.10.5) for several hosts including internal-portal.corp.local and inventory-api.corp.local. Ran dig +trace from 10.20.44.112 and confirmed the authoritative servers themselves are returning the outdated 10.10.10.5 address — this points to stale zone data in the authoritative zone rather than a resolver caching issue. Looping in Raj Okonkwo (rokonkwo) from the DNS infrastructure team to review zone file history.

Diagnostic findings changed the resolution path: The issue was not caused by stale cache on the corporate resolver. Both recursive (dns-resolver-01.corp.local) and authoritative DNS servers (ns1-internal.corp.local, ns2-internal.corp.local) consistently returned the same wrong data — 10.10.10.5 instead of the current 10.20.50.20 for internal-portal.corp.local and 10.10.10.7 instead of 10.20.50.22 for inventory-api.corp.local. Cache clearing via rndc flush had no effect, confirming the authoritative corp.local zone records themselves were incorrect. I updated the A records in the zone file, incremented the serial, and reloaded the zone on both authoritative servers. Verified from WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.20.44.112) and from the Austin monitoring probe that all affected hostnames now resolve correctly. Marcus Delgado and the service-discovery team confirmed application connectivity is restored. — Priya Nair

correspondence.message: We confirmed the controller certificate on WLC-PDX-01.corp.internal was renewed last week, but some devices are still failing 802.1X. Diagnostic findings changed the resolution path: Available diagnostics were mixed and did not isolate a single failing layer. correspondence.message: Hi Marcus, thanks for reporting this. Please confirm what you see in Company Portal and BitLocker status on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR. We need to verify whether encryption is off, whether a recovery key appears in Intune for your device (enrolled under username mreeves), and whether provisioning showed any TPM-related failure. Also, can you confirm the device IP address so we can cross-reference Intune enrollment logs?

Company Portal says the device is noncompliant for encryption. BitLocker shows not enabled on the C: drive, I do not see a recovery key in Intune under my account (mreeves), and the earlier setup attempt mentioned a TPM initialization problem. The device IP is 10.47.83.112. I also checked with my manager, Linda Choi (lchoi@corplabs.com), and she confirmed other laptops in our group didn't have this issue.

Thanks for the details, Marcus. Diagnostic findings changed the resolution path: Diagnostics ruled out local TPM readiness as the blocker on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR. The failure point was policy delivery on the management side — specifically, the Intune disk encryption profile 'Corp-BitLocker-Win11' was not applying to the device due to an assignment filter mismatch. The endpoint had hardware readiness and a TPM protector, but the effective encryption policy was not applying successfully, which also left recovery key escrow incomplete. I corrected the policy assignment targeting for the device group 'Corporate Laptops - Portland', triggered a fresh sync, and verified the reported service impact cleared. Recovery key is now escrowed and visible under mreeves in the Intune portal, and Company Portal shows compliant status.

steps: Reviewed the device's Intune policy targeting and applicability details for WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (enrolled user: mreeves). correspondence.message: We found repeated 504 timeouts during the overnight CustomerSync batch (02:00–04:30 UTC on 2026-05-13) on gw-prod-west-02.integrations.corplabs.internal and a failed token refresh event in the same window. Please reach out to me at r.nakamura@corplabs.com or ext. 4-7831 if you need to discuss offline. — Reiko Nakamura, Integration Support

We only saw delayed customer updates overnight starting around 02:12 UTC, and the logs on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD show the token refresh job for svc-custsync failed around the same time the timeout alerts started firing in the Monitoring System dashboard. I applied the matching fix (temporary timeout increase to 90s, exponential backoff with jitter) and verified the reported service impact cleared after re-running the affected CustomerSync jobs. — Reiko Nakamura

correspondence.message: We are seeing 401 Unauthorized and 504 timeout errors during the scheduled sync window for the CustomerDataSyncApp running on pod cluster us-east-1. Logs from the Integration Gateway service account svc-custsync show repeated failures starting at approximately 2026-05-14T01:15:00Z. Diagnostic findings changed the resolution path: The timeout symptoms were secondary to downstream API rate limiting. Authentication for service account svc-custsync remained valid and baseline latency was acceptable, but quota enforcement during the overnight batch caused retries to stack up until jobs exhausted their retry window. I applied the matching fix — reducing concurrency and adding exponential backoff — and verified with Priya Nair that the reported service impact cleared. Marcus Delgado confirmed the gateway worker queue drained successfully after the configuration change.

root_cause: The overnight sync workload exceeded the downstream API's rate or quota limits, leading to 429 throttling responses and retry exhaustion that appeared as integration timeout failures.

steps: Confirmed the throttling pattern in gateway and downstream logs (batch-20260514-0115) and reduced request concurrency for the affected overnight batch jobs from 50 to 10 concurrent workers on the Integration Gateway EKS deployment in us-east-1.

Implemented stronger pacing, exponential backoff (initial delay 2s, max 60s, jitter enabled), and batch spreading on the Integration Gateway to stay within the downstream API rate limits of 100 requests/minute. Configuration was updated by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) and reviewed by Priya Nair.

Requested a quota review or temporary limit increase from the downstream API owner (contacted via api-support@partnerservices.net) where supported, referencing the CustomerDataSyncApp integration and projected batch volumes.

Escalation note authored by Priya Nair (pnair), cc: Rafael Tomescu (rtomescu@corplabs.com).

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostic evidence was incomplete and mixed across all three playbook checks. Token failure for service account integration-svc-custsync was not confirmed post-incident. Downstream latency to api.partnerdata.io may have contributed (p99 response times reached ~6.2s during the batch window), and isolated throttling signals (3 out of ~1,200 requests returned HTTP 429) were present, but no single cause was proven for the timeout spike observed on igw-worker-node-04 between 02:00–03:30 UTC.

steps.action: Confirm the integration token or secret remained valid for the affected overnight synchronization window.
steps.expected_result: Token validation succeeds and the API accepts authenticated calls.
steps.observed_result: The active downstream API token for service account integration-svc-custsync appeared valid in configuration review (vault path: secret/igw/custsync/api-token, last rotated 2026-04-28). However, only limited authenticated test calls were completed by Priya Nair after the incident window (~05:45 UTC), so full token behavior during the 02:00–03:30 failure period could not be conclusively reproduced. No HTTP 401 or 403 responses were logged.
steps.evidence: The active downstream API token for service account integration-svc-custsync (vault path: secret/igw/custsync/api-token, last rotation: 2026-04-28, expiry: 2026-07-27) appeared valid in configuration review. Post-incident test calls at 05:45 UTC returned HTTP 200 with valid payloads, but only 5 test requests were issued — insufficient to reproduce burst-load conditions. No 401/403 entries found in gateway logs for the failure window. Full token behavior during the 02:00–03:30 period could not be conclusively reproduced.

steps.action: Compare failed integration job timing with Integration Gateway latency metrics and downstream service responsiveness.
steps.expected_result: API response latency is within the integration timeout window.
steps.observed_result: Some gateway metrics from igw-gw-east-01.corplabs.internal showed elevated response times near the batch peak (p50 rose from 220ms to 1,400ms; p99 spiked to ~6,200ms against a configured 30s timeout), but trace coverage for the exact failed requests was incomplete (10% sampling rate yielded only 47 captured traces out of ~1,200 requests) and did not establish whether latency alone exceeded the timeout window for all 38 impacted jobs.
steps.evidence: Gateway latency dashboard (Monitoring System, panel: igw-downstream-latency-custsync) showed p99 response time spike to ~6,200ms between 02:10–03:15 UTC on igw-gw-east-01.corplabs.internal. Trace sampling at 10% captured 47 of ~1,200 requests; of those, 12 traces showed response times exceeding 5s but none exceeded the 30s timeout threshold. Pod igw-worker-node-04 (IP 10.42.18.77) logged 38 ETIMEDOUT errors. Incomplete trace coverage prevents confirming whether latency alone caused all failures.

steps.action: Review API gateway logs for rate-limit responses, retry exhaustion, or throttling indicators during the failure period.
steps.expected_result: No rate-limit response prevents the integration job from completing.
steps.observed_result: Log review on igw-gw-east-01.corplabs.internal found a small number of throttling-related entries (3 HTTP 429 responses with Retry-After headers) mixed with 38 generic timeout errors (504/ETIMEDOUT), but not enough consistent evidence to confirm rate limiting as the primary driver of the incident. The 429 responses occurred at 02:22, 02:47, and 03:08 UTC.
steps.evidence: API gateway structured logs (index: igw-access-2026.05.14) filtered for status_code=429 returned 3 entries at 02:22:14, 02:47:33, and 03:08:51 UTC, each with Retry-After: 60 header from the downstream endpoint api.partnerdata.io. Remaining 38 failures were 504 Gateway Timeout or ETIMEDOUT with no throttle indicator. Rate-limit quota headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining) were not present in captured responses, limiting analysis. Insufficient evidence to confirm rate limiting as primary cause.

root_cause: Unknown; available diagnostics were insufficient to distinguish between intermittent downstream latency, burst-based throttling, or another transient external integration condition during the overnight batch window.

steps: Captured additional gateway debug logging (log level set to DEBUG on igw-gw-east-01.corplabs.internal, namespace igw-custsync-prod) and enabled 100% request tracing for subsequent overnight runs to improve visibility into authentication, latency, and throttle responses. Configuration change applied by Priya Nair (pnair) at 06:05 UTC.

Applied a temporary workaround by increasing the API timeout from 30s to 45s and reducing batch concurrency from 20 to 8 parallel workers on igw-worker-node-04 to limit repeat failures while evidence collection continued. Changes deployed via Helm values override in the igw-custsync-prod namespace.

Escalated the ambiguous findings to the downstream API owner at PartnerData (contact: Lena Kowalski, lkowalski@partnerdata.io) and internal integration engineering team lead Rafael Tomescu (rtomescu@corplabs.com, EMP-51934) for joint review of the next occurrence. Escalation ticket XREF-AIT-0033 created.

Verified partial recovery by re-running the 38 failed sync jobs (batch IDs SYNC-20260514-0200 through SYNC-20260514-0330) at 06:20 UTC and monitoring whether the backlog of ~14,000 customer records drained without recurring timeout spikes. All re-run jobs completed successfully within 12 minutes; no 504 or ETIMEDOUT errors observed. Confirmed by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) that downstream CRM data was current by 06:45 UTC.

correspondence.message: Hi Rachel, we can see the device WORKSTATION-DELL-RN (IP 10.42.18.97) is marked Noncompliant in Intune under your account rnguyen@corplabs.com. Please confirm whether Company Portal also shows an encryption-related compliance issue and whether the device has been online recently.

Yes, Company Portal shows the device as Noncompliant and I cannot access Exchange Online. The laptop was on earlier today at my desk in Arlington, but I had not opened Company Portal before contacting support. My username is rnguyen if that helps look things up.

Diagnostic findings changed the resolution path: Diagnostics ruled out stale check-in and policy scoping problems for device WORKSTATION-DELL-RN. The device was evaluating against the correct compliance policy (US-Marketing-Compliance-v3), and the current compliance run failed because the endpoint reported an unhealthy encryption state — specifically BitLocker protection was suspended. I applied the matching fix (re-enabled BitLocker) and verified the reported service impact cleared. Rachel Nguyen's Exchange Online access has been restored and the device now shows as Compliant in Intune.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics ruled out stale check-in and policy scoping problems for device WORKSTATION-DELL-RN (user: rnguyen, EMP-40821). The device was evaluating against the correct compliance policy (US-Marketing-Compliance-v3), and the current compliance run failed because the endpoint reported an unhealthy encryption state — BitLocker protection was suspended on the endpoint at IP 10.42.18.97.

steps.action: Confirmed the device's recent Intune check-in status and whether compliance evaluation had run after the reported access issue.

steps.action: Reviewed the failing compliance signal for device encryption to determine why the endpoint was marked noncompliant.
steps.expected_result: Required compliance signals report healthy values.
steps.observed_result: The blocking compliance signal was device encryption; BitLocker protection was actually suspended on the endpoint WORKSTATION-DELL-RN, so the encryption requirement evaluated as unhealthy. The manage-bde -status output confirmed protection status was 'Suspended'.
steps.evidence: Intune compliance detail for device WORKSTATION-DELL-RN showed 'Require encryption of data storage on device: Not compliant'. Remote PowerShell session confirmed manage-bde -status C: returned 'Protection Status: Protection Off (Suspended)'. BitLocker had been suspended, likely during a recent BIOS update cycle.

steps.expected_result: Device is in the intended policy scope with no stale assignment.
steps.observed_result: The device WORKSTATION-DELL-RN was still assigned to the intended compliance policy (US-Marketing-Compliance-v3) scoped to the Marketing user group, and there was no stale or incorrect policy targeting.
steps.evidence: Intune policy assignment confirmed WORKSTATION-DELL-RN (user rnguyen, group: Marketing) was correctly targeted by US-Marketing-Compliance-v3. No duplicate or conflicting compliance policies were assigned. Policy version matched the latest published revision.

root_cause: BitLocker/device encryption on the endpoint was suspended or otherwise not in an active protected state, causing the encryption compliance requirement to fail and Conditional Access to block access.

steps: Confirmed local BitLocker status on device WORKSTATION-DELL-RN via remote PowerShell (manage-bde -status C:) and identified that protection was suspended rather than missing due to stale reporting. Agent Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) coordinated with Rachel Nguyen to perform the remediation.

Re-enabled BitLocker protection on WORKSTATION-DELL-RN by running 'manage-bde -protectors -enable C:' and verified the encryption state returned to healthy on the endpoint. Protection status confirmed as 'Protection On' after the command completed.

Triggered a device sync from Company Portal on WORKSTATION-DELL-RN and confirmed Intune marked the device Compliant again within approximately 5 minutes. Validated that Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen@corplabs.com) could successfully sign in to Exchange Online without Conditional Access blocks. Ticket closed by agent mdelgado.

correspondence.message: Hi Fatima — thanks for reporting this. Please open Company Portal on your device (WORKSTATION-GALAXY-FK) and confirm whether it still shows Not Compliant, especially the encryption status, after signing in with your account f.elkhoury@corplabs.com and running a manual sync. Also, could you ask Ravi Menon (r.menon@corplabs.com) to do the same on his device so we can compare results? This is agent Lukas Brandt, EMP-61034, handling your case.

Hi Lukas, I ran the sync on my device (WORKSTATION-GALAXY-FK, IP 10.47.83.112) and Company Portal still showed Not Compliant — encryption was listed as 'Not reported'. Outlook improved briefly after the sync, but OneDrive was still blocked. Ravi confirmed the same behavior on his device (WORKSTATION-PIXEL-RM) from the Dubai office — his encryption also shows 'Not reported' even though he has device encryption enabled. My username is f.elkhoury if you need to look me up in the admin console.

Diagnostic findings changed the resolution path: Diagnostics did not support an endpoint encryption failure on either Fatima's device (WORKSTATION-GALAXY-FK) or Ravi's device (WORKSTATION-PIXEL-RM). Both devices were checking in and reporting healthy encryption at the OS level, but a stale compliance policy targeting — specifically the retired policy scope 'EMEA-Sales-Legacy-Encryption-v1' — caused Intune to evaluate them against the wrong assignment group, leaving them incorrectly noncompliant. I corrected the policy assignment in the Intune admin center and verified the reported service impact cleared for both users. — Lukas Brandt, Service Desk

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics did not support an endpoint encryption failure. Devices belonging to users f.elkhoury and r.menon were checking in regularly and reporting healthy encryption at the Android OS level, but the stale compliance policy scope 'EMEA-Sales-Legacy-Encryption-v1' — which was retired on 2026-05-10 but never fully unassigned — caused Intune to evaluate the EMEA Sales device group against the wrong assignment. This left affected devices incorrectly marked noncompliant, triggering Conditional Access blocks on Exchange Online, OneDrive, and other M365 services.

steps.observed_result: Affected devices including WORKSTATION-GALAXY-FK (user f.elkhoury, IP 10.47.83.112) and WORKSTATION-PIXEL-RM (user r.menon) had recent Intune check-ins within the last 4 hours and compliance evaluations had run after the reported access failures, ruling out stale check-in as the root cause.

No endpoint-side encryption fault was found during review of either device's compliance payload.

The 'Not reported' status in Company Portal was a display artifact caused by the stale policy evaluation, not an actual missing signal.

steps.action: Compare the assigned compliance policy with the user's device group membership to rule out stale or incorrect assignment.
steps.expected_result: Device is in the intended policy scope with no stale assignment.
steps.observed_result: The devices were still assigned to the retired compliance policy scope 'EMEA-Sales-Legacy-Encryption-v1', which had been superseded on 2026-05-10 but was never fully removed from the EMEA Sales Azure AD group. This caused Intune to continue evaluating devices against stale targeting that required a different encryption reporting format, leaving them incorrectly noncompliant.
steps.evidence: Intune policy assignment audit showed the 'EMEA-Sales-Legacy-Encryption-v1' policy was still actively assigned to the 'SG-EMEA-Sales-Mobile' device group containing both WORKSTATION-GALAXY-FK and WORKSTATION-PIXEL-RM. The current intended policy 'EMEA-Sales-Encryption-v2' was also assigned but the legacy policy took precedence due to conflict resolution order, overriding the correct evaluation.

root_cause: A stale or incorrect Intune compliance policy assignment kept affected devices in the wrong policy scope after a policy change, causing erroneous noncompliant results despite healthy encryption state.

steps: Reviewed compliance policy assignments in the Intune admin center and removed the stale retired targeting ('EMEA-Sales-Legacy-Encryption-v1') that was still applying to the 'SG-EMEA-Sales-Mobile' device group containing the affected device population, including devices for f.elkhoury and r.menon.

Reassigned the intended current compliance policy scope ('EMEA-Sales-Encryption-v2') as the sole active policy for the group and forced a sync on affected devices — including WORKSTATION-GALAXY-FK and WORKSTATION-PIXEL-RM — so they would download the corrected targeting and re-evaluate compliance.

Verified a fresh compliance evaluation completed under the correct policy for both Fatima El-Khoury (WORKSTATION-GALAXY-FK) and Ravi Menon (WORKSTATION-PIXEL-RM), confirming devices now showed Compliant in Company Portal. Confirmed Conditional Access stopped blocking access to Exchange Online, Outlook Mobile, and OneDrive Mobile. Follow-up confirmation received from both users in the Düsseldorf and Dubai offices.

correspondence.message: Hi Marcus — thanks for reporting this. Please confirm whether the MFA prompt repeats after approval for all SSO Portal apps or only Salesforce, and whether this started after this morning's 04:00 UTC identity sync. Also, can you let me know if other affected users (e.g., Priya Nair or Kevin Ostrowski) are seeing the same behavior on their machines? I'd like to check whether it's tied to specific devices or accounts.

It happens for Salesforce and Concur through the SSO Portal. Users approve MFA via Okta Verify but get sent back to the prompt again — I tested on my laptop WORKSTATION-DELL-MD and Priya tested on WORKSTATION-HP-PN, same result. Kevin Ostrowski (kostrowski, emp ID E-50921) also confirmed the loop on his end. The problem started this morning after the sync, nobody could get through before about 04:15 UTC.

Diagnostic findings changed the resolution path: Diagnostics ruled out stale MFA enrollment as the primary issue. The loop was reproducible for accounts mdelgado, pnair, and kostrowski across multiple browsers and devices. Factor state was healthy in Okta for all three users. The main fault was a group and policy scope mismatch between Azure AD and Okta — specifically, the 'SalesApps-SSO-Access' group lost its synced membership for these users during the 04:00 UTC identity sync, causing them to be re-evaluated against a default conditional access policy during SSO and sent back through MFA. I applied the matching fix (re-added the group scope and triggered a resync) and verified the reported service impact cleared for all affected accounts.

diagnostics.summary: Diagnostics ruled out stale MFA enrollment as the primary issue. The loop was reproducible for users mdelgado, pnair, and kostrowski (all Sales, Charlotte office). Factor state was healthy in Okta, and no stale enrollments were found. The main fault was a group and policy scope mismatch between Azure AD and Okta: the 'SalesApps-SSO-Access' group lost synced membership for affected users after the 04:00 UTC identity sync, causing them to be re-evaluated against a default conditional access policy during SSO and sent back through MFA repeatedly.

steps.action: Reproduced the affected user login flow through the SSO Portal to verify whether the MFA prompt loop occurred after challenge completion.
steps.expected_result: User completes MFA once and reaches the application landing page.
steps.observed_result: Reproduced the login flow using account mdelgado (IP 10.42.18.77) on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD and confirmed the MFA prompt loop occurred after Okta Verify challenge completion. The user was returned to the verification step instead of receiving an application session token — the SSO Portal showed AUTH_401_MFA_REQUIRED on each redirect.
steps.evidence: Reproduced the login flow using account mdelgado from IP 10.42.18.77 on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD. After Okta Verify push approval, the SSO Portal returned AUTH_401_MFA_REQUIRED and redirected back to the MFA prompt. Browser HAR capture showed three consecutive 401 responses within 12 seconds, each triggering a new /authn/factors/verify call. No application session cookie was ever set.

steps.action: Checked MFA enrollment state and active factor records for impacted users in Okta after the identity sync.
steps.expected_result: User has an active factor with no stale or disabled enrollment.
steps.observed_result: Okta admin console showed active MFA factors (Okta Verify push) for impacted users mdelgado, pnair (emp ID E-47833), and kostrowski with no stale, disabled, or duplicate enrollments after the 04:00 UTC sync. Factor last-used timestamps were current.
steps.evidence: Okta factor enrollment report for mdelgado, pnair, and kostrowski all showed status=ACTIVE for Okta Verify (push), enrolled dates predating the sync, and last-verified timestamps matching the morning's failed attempts. No secondary or orphaned factor records were present. Enrollment state was healthy.

steps.action: Compared affected user group membership with conditional access and application assignment policy scope between Azure AD and Okta.
steps.expected_result: User belongs to the expected access group and policy scope.
steps.observed_result: Affected users mdelgado, pnair, and kostrowski were missing from the 'SalesApps-SSO-Access' synced group in Okta after the 04:00 UTC identity sync. Azure AD showed them as members of the source group (CN=SalesApps-SSO-Access,OU=App Groups,DC=corplabs,DC=internal), but Okta's group mirror did not reflect the membership, causing application assignment evaluation to differ between Azure AD and Okta.
steps.evidence: Azure AD audit log confirmed mdelgado, pnair, and kostrowski remained in the 'SalesApps-SSO-Access' security group (object ID visible in sync logs). However, Okta's group membership API (/api/v1/groups) for the mirrored group returned zero matching members for these three accounts. The conditional access policy 'Sales-SaaS-MFA-Bypass' scoped to this group therefore did not apply, and users fell through to the default policy requiring MFA re-challenge on each app redirect.

root_cause: A post-sync group membership and application policy assignment mismatch between Azure AD and Okta caused affected users to fall outside the expected access scope during SSO evaluation, resulting in repeated MFA challenges instead of successful session establishment.

steps: Reviewed synced group membership and application assignment for affected Sales users (mdelgado, pnair, kostrowski) across Azure AD and Okta. Confirmed the 'SalesApps-SSO-Access' group membership was present in Azure AD but missing in the Okta mirror after the 04:00 UTC sync.

Corrected the conditional access and application policy scope so the expected 'SalesApps-SSO-Access' group was consistently included in both identity platforms. Updated the Okta group rule to re-map the Azure AD source group and validated the 'Sales-SaaS-MFA-Bypass' conditional access policy scope.

Triggered a manual group resync via Azure AD Connect (delta sync) and refreshed affected users' assignments in Okta. Confirmed mdelgado, pnair, and kostrowski appeared in the Okta mirrored group within 2 minutes.
Cleared active authentication sessions for impacted users (mdelgado, pnair, kostrowski) in both Okta and Azure AD to force policy re-evaluation with the corrected group scope.

Retested SSO to Salesforce and Concur for all three affected users and confirmed they completed MFA once and reached the target application landing pages without looping. Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) confirmed normal access restored from WORKSTATION-DELL-MD at 05:04 UTC.

correspondence.message: Please confirm whether the MFA challenge is looping after approval for all Sales contractor users — specifically mdelgado, rpatel, and any others affected — and whether the same behavior occurs when launching both Salesforce and Workday from the SSO Portal at https://sso.corplabs.com. Diagnostic findings changed the resolution path: After capturing Okta system logs and Azure AD sign-in traces for mdelgado and rpatel, diagnostics showed the reported symptom resembled an MFA loop, but the actual failure occurred after successful MFA completion. The Okta event log showed a successful verify_factor event followed by an immediate federation redirect failure (error: 'Invalid session state — missing group claim in SAML assertion'). MFA enrollment and conditional access policy assignments were both validated as healthy for the affected accounts. The problem points to a federated SSO session handling issue introduced during the CHG-20260514-0087 change window, specifically a misconfigured claim mapping in the Okta-to-Azure AD federation trust that omitted the contractor group claim from the SAML token. I applied the matching fix by working with identity engineering lead Kevin Ostrowski (kostrowski) and verified the reported service impact cleared for both test accounts.

correspondence.message: Hi Marcus, please confirm whether Outlook on the desktop (WORKSTATION-DELL-MD) still shows Disconnected, whether Outlook on the web at https://outlook.office365.com is current, and whether the same mailbox mdelgado@corplabs.com is affected on your iPhone only or on any other device as well. Also, can you confirm whether you're connecting from your usual IP 10.42.17.88 or from a remote network?

Desktop Outlook on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD still shows Disconnected and my iPhone is not getting new mail either. I'm connecting from my usual network at the Atlanta office, IP 10.42.17.88. The issue appears to be only this mailbox; there is no Microsoft 365 outage showing. My colleague Priya Nair on the same floor has no issues with her Exchange Online mailbox.

Diagnostic findings changed the resolution path: The findings do not support an endpoint-only mobile compliance issue because both desktop (WORKSTATION-DELL-MD) and mobile were affected for mdelgado@corplabs.com, the device was compliant per MDM policy, and client session refresh did not restore sync. This shifts the interpretation toward a mailbox-side or service-side issue requiring deeper platform investigation. I applied the matching fix and verified the reported service impact cleared. Escalation was coordinated with messaging engineer Raj Patel (rpatel) for backend mailbox health review.
